s7ccc51f7d5.description: arXiv:2611.26722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. sd63805c1ed.summary: ChatAtom is a multi-agent LLM system that turns natural-language requests into complete molecular dynamics workflows, including writing input scripts and analysis.

se212b10205.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
se212b10205.description: arXiv:2611.26794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) could automate these readouts with an explanation, but two gaps remain. Pathology MLLMs read H&E alone, while these readouts need the cell phenotypes that mIF measures. And their reasoning has no step-level truth to be checked against, so R1-style reinforcement learning rewards only the final answer and leaves the reasoning unverified. Same-section H&E and mIF provide what both gaps lack: mIF measures every cell without manual annotation, which gives cell-level ground truth
se212b10205.summary: Researchers propose interpretable tumor immune microenvironment reasoning by combining H&E tissue images with multiplex immunofluorescence cell phenotypes in multimodal LLMs.
se212b10205.why: Highlights the need for step-level verifiable reasoning in multimodal models, though the text offers limited detail on outcomes.

s7b900895fb.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
s7b900895fb.description: arXiv:2611.26797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcomes of one retrieval process. First, we show that diffusion models behave as AMs. With little data, a diffusion model forms a distinct basin of attraction around each training sample. As the data grows,
s7b900895fb.summary: A thesis argues that memorization and generalization can coexist in generative models, framing spurious states in associative memory as a source of creativity.

s392b2bf540.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
s392b2bf540.description: arXiv:2611.26870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, where they must distinguish between normative reasoning (what should happen) and descriptive reasoning (what is likely to happen). Most fairness benchmarks evaluate demographic discrimination under a single reasoning objective, and none we know of tests whether a model treats the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one. s392b2bf540.summary: Researchers introduce normative-descriptive calibration, a benchmark testing whether LLMs treat the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one.
s392b2bf540.why: Adds a evaluation dimension beyond demographic fairness, relevant to teams deploying LLMs in socially consequential decisions.

sf9653447a3.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
sf9653447a3.description: arXiv:2611.26903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial-edit deepfake localization aims to identify manipulated regions within otherwise authentic speech. Recent systems report strong overall results, but aggregate scores do not reveal whether this performance holds across different editing conditions. In this work, we present an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization (SAL) using WavLM-Large and XLS-R representations on the VoiceCraft and SSR-Speech subsets of PartialEdit. We categorize edits along three transcript-derived axes, namely content, meaning change, and editing operation, and evaluate each generator separately. While both representations achieve strong overall performance, localization is noticeably weaker on SSR-Speech. From our experiments, we f
sf9653447a3.summary: Researchers analyze partial-edit deepfake localization for speech across edit and generator conditions, using WavLM-Large and XLS-R on PartialEdit subsets.
sf9653447a3.why: Shows aggregate detection scores can hide weaknesses across editing conditions, which matters for teams evaluating audio deepfake detectors.

s692a19875b.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
s692a19875b.description: arXiv:2611.26906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revises the allocation as verification feedback becomes available. The allocation problem changes as proving progresses. Early decisions mainly determine which solver should handle an untried subgoal, while
s692a19875b.summary: Researchers present BudgetPV, an agentic system that allocates compute across subgoals and heterogeneous LLM theorem solvers based on cost and capability.
s692a19875b.why: Demonstrates routing subtasks to cheaper or stronger models to balance inference cost against success, a pattern applicable to production model routing.

s0d97de254e.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
s0d97de254e.description: arXiv:2611.26910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, whether its own evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it gets in the world. It is built on the game Outer Wilds, where each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets, only the agent's
s0d97de254e.summary: AstronautBench is a benchmark measuring LLM agent self-improvement across episodes through knowledge, evidence, and task progress views on the same run.
s0d97de254e.why: Argues that task success alone doesn't show learning, offering a multi-view evaluation approach for agent developers.

s5ab33db955.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
s5ab33db955.description: arXiv:2611.26912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. We present ZhuLong-SE (Self-Evolution), an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces. Building on ZhuLong, it enhances the task-level harness with API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox execution, and static checking, then adds governed cross-task self-evolution. Beyond solving individual tasks, ZhuLong-SE distills past execution traces into a three-tier memory store governed by ground
s5ab33db955.summary: ZhuLong-SE is an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces to improve EDA scripting with API retrieval and sandbox execution.
s5ab33db955.why: Shows agents learning from past traces to handle sparsely documented proprietary APIs, relevant to hard-to-document toolchains.

s3433b5b74f.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
s3433b5b74f.description: arXiv:2611.26935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop a theory for the organization of predictive information based on the scaling behavior of a family of information measures, and the theory predicts that if this organization has the same form at all me
s3433b5b74f.summary: Researchers study how predictive information is carried by preceding text and distributed along history, examining the self-similar organization of information in language.

sc8d198630f.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
sc8d198630f.description: arXiv:2611.26942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents ship more code with minimal human oversight, code review becomes the critical quality-control checkpoint -- but one without a reliable, objective verifier: review quality is nuanced and ultimately a judgment call by the PR author. Existing benchmarks are structurally misaligned with this: annotators are third-party reviewers, like the bots they evaluate, not the PR authors who actually decide what to fix. They also rely on small, static issue sets that require full re-evaluation as tools update, limiting how frequently progress can be tracked. We introduce CodeReviewBench, built on a fundamentally different signal: revealed developer preferences -- if a developer acts on a bot's suggestion, we treat it as useful; if they ignore i
sc8d198630f.summary: CodeReviewBench is a proposed automated benchmark for evaluating AI code review, using PR authors rather than third-party reviewers as the judges of review quality.
sc8d198630f.why: Targets code review as a quality gate for AI-generated code, relevant to teams scaling agent-written pull requests.

s397a58d08f.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
s397a58d08f.description: arXiv:2611.26966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. We study an execution boundary that separates agent proposals from business-controlled authority, context disclosure, and supplier selection. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. We evaluate this runtime with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers: 2,400 fault episodes across four policies, 60 process-termination/restart episodes, 19,000 timed calls across 19 configurations, five targeted mutations over 43 fixtures, and 160 substitution records. No language model or autonomous agent is evalua
s397a58d08f.summary: The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) is a runtime that mediates tool-using agents' capability calls, recording uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without replying.
s397a58d08f.why: Addresses authorization and audit of agent actions with external side effects, a key concern for production agent governance.

s967eeb51cb.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Story: When LLMs Narrate Financial Changes Beyond Their Inputs
s967eeb51cb.description: arXiv:2611.26968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A financial report drafted by an LLM can state every number correctly but still go beyond its input, adding judgments and causes that no one supplied. Strong demand: Not in input Higher prices: Kept fessionals, and attempts to fix them by prompting with how each word is used instead make such judgments more frequent. We therefore propose FrameCheck, a plug-in that sits beFrameCheck Revenue increased 3%
s967eeb51cb.summary: Researchers show LLM-drafted financial reports can state every number correctly yet add unsupported judgments and causes, appearing far more often than in human-written 10-K filings.
s967eeb51cb.why: Accurate figures do not guarantee faithful financial narratives, so teams deploying LLM report drafting need checks beyond numeric accuracy.

s8140136569.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
s8140136569.description: arXiv:2611.26975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.
s8140136569.summary: ToRA is an adapter that runs a second safety-check model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing weights and KV cache for near-free streaming guardrails on local LLMs.
s8140136569.why: It offers guard-model accuracy for streaming safety checks without nearly doubling per-token latency on local assistants.

s7d212e2fba.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs
s7d212e2fba.description: arXiv:2611.26976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sub-4-bit quantization allows mobile devices to run larger LLMs, but its memory savings do not always translate into faster decoding on mobile NPUs. Their matrix units support only a few native integer datatypes, and converting unsupported weight formats on the vector unit can erase the gains from fewer bits. Mixed precision faces an additional constraint: each matrix-unit tile uses one datatype. MixFold executes 3-bit and perfectly symmetric 2-bit weights using native integer operations without expanding the weights to wider datatypes during decoding. s7d212e2fba.summary: MixFold proposes executing sub-4-bit mixed-precision LLM weights with native integer operations on mobile NPUs, avoiding conversion to wider datatypes during decoding.
s7d212e2fba.why: Memory savings from low-bit quantization only speed up mobile decoding if conversion overhead is avoided, which this method targets.

sb051403af0.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness
sb051403af0.description: arXiv:2611.26988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In letter-of-credit (LC) document examination, a correct final decision does not show that every requirement was examined. We therefore evaluate examination requirement by requirement and make each requirement executable. A language model converts the bill of lading (BL) and commercial invoice (IV) requirements of a credit into atomic conditions and logical structures, and a deterministic verifier retrieves the named evidence and computes each outcome, so every check can be compared with a gold encoding and traced to logged evidence. Because LC records are confidential, our on-premises 9B parser is fine-tuned only on synthetic pairs built from templates and human-reviewed public document values. sb051403af0.summary: Researchers propose converting letter-of-credit requirements into executable, atomic checks via a language model and deterministic verifier, evaluated requirement by requirement against gold encodings.
sb051403af0.why: Checking each requirement rather than only the final decision gives auditable, traceable verification for trade-finance document review.

s27117f410f.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
s27117f410f.description: arXiv:2611.26998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reward fidelity in an adversarial reinforcement-learning loop for red-teaming financial-services language-model guardrails. Apparent wins can arise when an attack omits prescribed personally identifiable information (PII), or when a reward judge credits a response that did not break the targeted policy. On attacker-generated and public benchmark examples, TypeSafe Jev checks whether the prescribed PII is present. For outcome scoring, we compare the decision models TypeSafe Jev, Laya (pretrained and post-trained), and pretrained CLM-8B with logged Opus 4.8 judgements from a replay corpus. Post-training markedly improves Laya's agreement with the judge. A separate author-reviewed off-target set establishes that Opus can award false win
s27117f410f.summary: The paper studies reward fidelity in adversarial RL for red-teaming financial-services LLM guardrails, finding apparent attack wins can come from missing PII or lenient reward judges.
s27117f410f.why: Reward judges that credit non-successful attacks can mislead guardrail evaluation, so reward signals need verification before trusting results.

s17169dd0c7.title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
s17169dd0c7.description: arXiv:2611.27007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigorously evaluating medical artificial intelligence (AI) requires testing open-ended clinical management across diverse presentations and stages of care. However, existing benchmarks rely on manual expert authoring, limiting coverage across conditions, conditional care pathways, and evolving guidelines. We develop an automated pipeline that extracts and verifies structured clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations to generate scenarios spanning the care continuum, including nuanced presentations and practice variations across regions and guideline editions. Applied to 436 BMJ Best Practice clinical monographs (354 US, 82 International), this yields 3,200 scenarios spanning differential diagnosis, investiga
s17169dd0c7.summary: Researchers describe an automated pipeline that extracts clinical criteria and decision trees from practice recommendations to generate medical AI test scenarios across the care continuum.
s17169dd0c7.why: Automatically generated, guideline-grounded scenarios could scale evaluation of medical AI beyond costly manual expert benchmark authoring.

sb4c5575ce5.title: Many Plans at Once: Diverse Top-Quality Planning in Continuous Time
sb4c5575ce5.description: arXiv:2611.27012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Planners for physical systems usually return a single trajectory, which leaves no alternative when an unmodeled constraint invalidates the chosen route or downstream preferences change. A set of plans computed in advance provides ready-made alternatives and warm-starts for fast adaptation, but only if the plans are both low-cost and mutually distinct. Discrete planning addresses this with top-quality and diverse planning, but these ideas do not transfer to continuous time, where every valid trajectory has infinitely many valid near-copies, and existing trajectory planners converge to one or a few solutions. sb4c5575ce5.summary: Researchers present methods for computing diverse, top-quality plans in continuous time, giving alternative trajectories for physical systems when constraints change.
sb4c5575ce5.why: Precomputed diverse plans offer ready alternatives and warm starts for robotics and physical planners facing unmodeled constraints.

scb843bf8d5.title: Same Facts, Different Decision: Fact-Invariant Manipulation and Provenance-Based Defense in Typed Decision Models
scb843bf8d5.description: arXiv:2611.27016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typed decision models such as TypeSafe's Jev answer only with a probability, an option, or a score, so software can act on them directly. Their inputs, however, often include text from outsiders. Prior attacks test this risk poorly. Injected instructions rarely work on these models, and added facts can make a changed decision correct. We show that outside comments can persuade these models to make a wrong decision without adding any fact. We propose LEVER, an attack that writes such comments with four levers from argumentation theory, uses a separate verifier to discard any comment that adds a fact, and searches for effective comments guided by the model's output probabilities. scb843bf8d5.summary: The paper introduces LEVER, an attack that uses argumentation-based outside comments to push typed decision models into wrong decisions without adding any new facts, and proposes a provenance-based defense.
scb843bf8d5.why: Decision models that consume third-party text can be steered by persuasive comments alone, so input provenance matters for security.

s94f914119f.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
s94f914119f.description: arXiv:2611.27018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exact representations of maximum functions by ReLU networks with two hidden layers and integer parameters. The least positive output multiplier is two for the six-input maximum, and either two or six for the seven-input maximum. We obtain these bounds from integral cubical fillings and a coefficient-preserving passage from polytope identities to networks. For the coordinate-facet complex of the six-simplex, we compute a coning index of six over the integers and three after inverting two, allowing arbitrary integral directions within each facet. s94f914119f.summary: The paper derives integer-parameter bounds on the least positive output multiplier for exact representations of six- and seven-input maximum functions by two-hidden-layer ReLU networks.

sced64c19e2.title: Disentangling Verbalized Evaluation Awareness and Refusal through Neuron-Level Intervention
sced64c19e2.description: arXiv:2611.27032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large reasoning models (LRMs) become more capable, reliable evaluation becomes essential. LRMs can sometimes recognize that they are being evaluated, a phenomenon known as \emph{evaluation awareness}. This phenomenon raises concerns about whether safety behavior, particularly refusal behavior, generalizes from evaluation to deployment. Prior work manipulates \emph{verbalized evaluation awareness (VEA)} through activation steering and observes higher refusal rates when VEA is present, but the mechanisms underlying this connection remain poorly understood. We identify \emph{VEA neurons} by contrasting their activations in VEA and non-VEA reasoning segments. Intervening on 5,000 VEA neurons reduces the VEA rate from 12.6--51.8\% to at most 1.
sced64c19e2.summary: Researchers use neuron-level intervention to separate verbalized evaluation awareness from refusal behavior in large reasoning models.
sced64c19e2.why: Understanding whether evaluation awareness drives refusals bears on whether safety tests generalize to deployment behavior.

sf0701cace4.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions
sf0701cace4.description: arXiv:2611.27046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on Web interaction, issuing searches, following links, and reading pages, to complete complex user tasks. Since each action is driven by the agent's private context, including the user's prompt, dialogue history, memory, and connected data, it also opens a new privacy exposure surface. Prior attacks either passively analyze network traffic, which yields only coarse correlations, or hijack the agent through indirect prompt injection, which must place sensitive content in an outgoing field and is blocked by content-level defenses. sf0701cace4.summary: The paper presents a stateful privacy attack in which LLM agents leak private context through behavioral covert channels in their web actions such as searches and link-following.
sf0701cace4.why: Agent actions on the web can reveal private user context even when content filters block direct leakage, expanding the privacy attack surface.

sb1d173c8f8.title: A Continuous Relaxation of Quantization-Aware Training
sb1d173c8f8.description: arXiv:2611.27056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantization is a critical piece of the deployment pipeline in the era of large generative models. Low-bit quantization, particularly 2-bits or sub-2-bits, is a notoriously difficult problem, particularly when using a channelwise quantization scheme which has been shown as a leading candidate for hardware-efficiency. The key challenges with low-bit quantization range from limited quantization levels to saddle points or flat regions in the loss surface. In this paper, we look at the problem of flat quantization loss surfaces through a lens of dynamically changing bitwidth. sb1d173c8f8.summary: Researchers propose a continuous relaxation of quantization-aware training to address flat, saddle-point-laden loss surfaces in low-bit, channelwise quantization of large models.
sb1d173c8f8.why: Sub-2-bit channelwise quantization is hard to train, and a better optimization approach could make hardware-efficient deployment more practical.

s7f5fd3cd46.title: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Vision-Language Models
s7f5fd3cd46.description: arXiv:2611.27064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) represent each image with hundreds of visual tokens, which can make inference costly even when a prompt depends on only part of the image. Dynamic Token Merging (DTM), introduced in MrT5 for byte-level text encoders, learns which tokens to remove: a lightweight delete gate scores contextualized hidden states, acts as a differentiable attention bias during training, and physically removes tokens at inference. We argue that DTM is a general token deletion framework rather than a byte-level technique, and extend it to the vision modality and to decoder-only models. s7f5fd3cd46.summary: The authors extend Dynamic Token Merging, a learned token deletion method, to vision-language models so they can drop visual tokens at inference and reduce cost.
s7f5fd3cd46.why: Removing unneeded visual tokens could cut VLM inference costs when prompts depend on only part of an image.

s9fd887eb66.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models
s9fd887eb66.description: arXiv:2611.27068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) from verifiable outcomes gives a language agent one reward per episode: every step is credited alike, and nothing about the task is learned when all rollouts fail. The last mile, step-level credit, usually requires step labels, a learned critic, costly LLM judges or hand-written rules. We introduce DM-PRM, which turns a general-purpose decision model -- one answering yes/no questions with probabilities -- into a general-purpose process reward model (PRM), zero-shot: no step labels, no fine-tuning, no critic. s9fd887eb66.summary: DM-PRM converts a general-purpose yes/no decision model into a zero-shot process reward model that gives step-level credit without step labels, fine-tuning, or a critic.
s9fd887eb66.why: Step-level rewards without labels or critics could simplify RL training for language agents on multi-step tasks.

s8112ef1cde.title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation
s8112ef1cde.description: arXiv:2611.27089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weight-space programming lets a language model inspect and edit another model's weights, offering an alternative to gradient-based adaptation. We evaluated both approaches using Qwen3.5-0.8B on a fixed reference-frame task (128 items), StepGame (200 items), and two untrained distance-comparison tasks. Randomly permuting its weight change removed the gain. s8112ef1cde.summary: Researchers compare weight-space programming, where one model edits another's weights, with LoRA fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks using Qwen3.5-0.8B.
s8112ef1cde.why: It compares a gradient-free adaptation method with LoRA on small-model reasoning benchmarks, though the reported gains are modest and task-specific.

s9e4c319f67.title: Reasoning in Two Dimensions: Quantifying Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Efficiency
s9e4c319f67.description: arXiv:2611.27100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning exposes intermediate steps, but a correct answer does not establish that an LLM relies on the dependence expressed by those steps or reasons efficiently. We operationalize CoT faithfulness and efficiency within a common framework. Specifically, we represent a CoT as a semantic reasoning graph and decompose the model's predictive dependence along two complementary axes: dependence explained by semantic support versus additional reasoning history, and dependence allocated to answer-reaching versus off-path reasoning. s9e4c319f67.summary: Researchers propose a framework that represents chain-of-thought as a semantic reasoning graph to measure its faithfulness and efficiency.
s9e4c319f67.why: Correct answers alone don't show a model uses its stated reasoning, so this offers a way to audit reasoning traces.

sb9a327b243.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
sb9a327b243.description: arXiv:2611.27116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of an LLM agent depends on both its model and its harness, the code that mediates its interaction with tools and environments. Can LLM researchers drive this co-evolution as a recursive improvement process, deciding round after round which component to change when each change alters the value of the other? Existing benchmarks evaluate post-training or data research with the harness out of scope, or harness optimization with the model fixed, leaving this joint decision unmeasured. Researchers start from a common base model and initial harness, train and revise within a 24-hour
sb9a327b243.summary: Researchers introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can decide which component of an agent system, model or harness, to change in recursive co-evolution.
sb9a327b243.why: Agent performance depends on both model and harness, so this benchmark targets a joint decision that existing benchmarks leave unmeasured.

s71b5734548.title: Portable Active Recovery under Timed and Position-Dependent Visual Outages
s71b5734548.description: arXiv:2611.27121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a camera blackout depends on physical position rather than elapsed time, stable hovering prevents visual recovery and mission completion. On stereo visual-inertial quadrotors without external localization, an exogenous timed blackout and an endogenous position-dependent dark zone appear identical at loss onset yet require opposite responses: hover-and-wait completes 93/96 timed blackouts but 0/96 spatial outages (13 hard failures), whereas blind continuation traverses many spatial zones yet fails heavily during timed blackouts. s71b5734548.summary: Researchers study quadrotor recovery during camera blackouts, finding hover-and-wait works for timed outages but fails for position-dependent dark zones, which need different responses.
s71b5734548.why: Drone teams relying on visual navigation without external localization need recovery strategies that distinguish timed from location-based outages.

sa8d6b2426a.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
sa8d6b2426a.description: arXiv:2611.27125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has become a core technique for post-training large language models, enabling students to learn from dense token-level supervision on their own generations. However, even with a capable teacher, OPD training can be unstable, leading to excessive response length, repetitive generation, and severe performance degradation. One example is \textit{spurious agreement}, where the student maintains high overlap with the teacher at the states visited but produces repetitive generations. sa8d6b2426a.summary: Researchers analyze why on-policy distillation for LLM post-training can be unstable, including a failure mode called spurious agreement that causes repetitive generation.
sa8d6b2426a.why: Teams using on-policy distillation to post-train LLMs may see length blowups and degradation, so understanding these dynamics matters for training stability.

s6065d7aa1b.title: MAPES: Multi-Value Alignment Pipeline via Expert Specialization
s6065d7aa1b.description: arXiv:2611.27133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences requires simultaneously satisfying multiple, often competing values. Existing preference optimization methods collapse these into a single implicit signal, and even multi-objective extensions optimize within a shared parameter space, leaving cross-value conflicts unresolved. We propose MAPES, a multi-value alignment paradigm in which conflict resolution is a first-class concern at every pipeline stage: it first decomposes supervision into value-specific experts trained in isolated parameter subspaces, then recomposes them via preference-aware value merging and a lightweight harmonization stage that aligns the merged model with the expert ensemble. s6065d7aa1b.summary: Researchers propose MAPES, a multi-value LLM alignment pipeline that trains value-specific experts in isolated parameter spaces before resolving conflicts.
s6065d7aa1b.why: Single-signal preference methods can hide conflicts between values, so this approach targets alignment tradeoffs explicitly.

s5b7b28b8b6.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
s5b7b28b8b6.description: arXiv:2611.27138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models fuse reports in retrieval, multi-agent consensus and agent memory, where treating shared-source reports as independent can double count evidence. A common remedy is an instruction to count each source once. Its value depends on the receiver's raw baseline. Pricing it needs an exact reference. s5b7b28b8b6.summary: Researchers show LLMs can double count shared-source evidence in fusion tasks and build an exact posterior reference to separate rule compliance from real posterior gain.
s5b7b28b8b6.why: Retrieval, multi-agent consensus, and memory systems can overcount correlated reports, so teams need measurable checks on evidence fusion.

s58fa5bdce9.title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout
s58fa5bdce9.description: arXiv:2611.27149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predictive world models learn to forecast observations, but accurate short-term predictions do not necessarily produce physically coherent behavior over longer horizons. We investigate how incorporating physical structure can strengthen world models while retaining their underlying predictive objectives. Across token-based models of planetary motion and JEPA-style visual models of mechanical systems, we study conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry-aware representations, temporal consistency, and learned structured dynamics. s58fa5bdce9.summary: Researchers study how adding physical structure, such as conserved quantities and symmetries, to predictive world models affects long-horizon physical coherence.
s58fa5bdce9.why: Accurate short-term forecasts don't guarantee physically coherent rollouts, which matters for anyone building world models for planning.

s3e35b02037.title: From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents
s3e35b02037.description: arXiv:2611.27159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Successful agent interactions provide training data, but success alone does not determine which records a student should learn from. We examine experience selection for a 4B language agent as a component of continual agent learning. Nine selectors are compared across two fixed experience pools, eight initialization seeds, and two sampling seeds, yielding 288 trained students. s3e35b02037.summary: Researchers compare nine experience selectors for training a 4B language agent across many seeds and pools to study continual agent learning.
s3e35b02037.why: Choosing which agent experiences to train on affects continual learning results, a practical design decision for agent builders.

sa32ba8ef01.title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility
sa32ba8ef01.description: arXiv:2611.27180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models(LLM) show promise for strategic reasoning, yet their ability to compute game-theoretic equilibria under dynamic conditions remains largely unexplored. This work investigates whether fine-tuned LLMs can serve as solver-free surrogates for online equilibrium computation in honeypot allocation, a setting in which network mobility continuously reshapes the underlying attack graph and forces repeated re-solving of a two-player zero-sum game. sa32ba8ef01.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to act as solver-free surrogates for computing equilibria in honeypot allocation games on networks with changing topology.
sa32ba8ef01.why: Fine-tuned models could approximate repeated game-theoretic re-solving in security settings, though the abstract gives limited evidence of production readiness.

s0b24363beb.title: What Does Matching a Human Intervention Effect Establish? Benchmark Checks for LLM Simulations
s0b24363beb.description: arXiv:2611.27186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM simulations are validated by equivalence with human effects, yet a zero reference passes whenever the human 90 percent interval lies inside the margin, as the human benchmark shows before simulation. s0b24363beb.why: Teams using LLM simulations as stand-ins for human studies may be overstating validation if they rely on zero-reference equivalence tests.

s5cb0308074.title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization
s5cb0308074.description: arXiv:2611.27196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPU acceleration has transformed electronic design automation (EDA), yet further improving expert-engineered GPU tools still demands substantial manual effort. Automating this work calls for coding agents that can trace bottlenecks across host and device code while preserving correctness and design quality. We introduce EDAGoat, to our knowledge the first EDA-aware GPU optimization agent for this task. Its optimization enhancement (OE) mode guides edits with four cross-project GPU optimization patterns. s5cb0308074.summary: Researchers introduce EDAGoat, an EDA-aware coding agent that optimizes project-level GPU code with optimization patterns and mandatory validation.
s5cb0308074.why: Automating GPU optimization in EDA tools with validation could reduce manual engineering effort while preserving correctness.

s65d8d4e046.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training
s65d8d4e046.description: arXiv:2611.27222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A visual agent acts on what it sees: it taps and types on a screen, or points on a camera image to show a robot where to act. One wrong step can fail its task, yet the right action is often among its own samples, passed over by its greedy decode. s65d8d4e046.summary: Researchers present Bel, a training-free method that improves visual agent steps by choosing among the agent's own sampled actions using a visual judgment model.
s65d8d4e046.why: Teams building screen or robot visual agents may improve step accuracy without retraining, though the abstract gives few benchmark details.

s6672e5bff7.title: LiDAR Signals for Robot Locomotion: Spherical Range Images Enable Robust Sim-to-Real Transfer
s6672e5bff7.description: arXiv:2611.27223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing legged-locomotion systems commonly rely on depth images or online elevation maps. However, depth-based policies suffer from perceptual sim-to-real discrepancies due to imperfect depth sensor modeling, while map-based approaches are vulnerable to drift and misalignment. LiDAR offers direct measurements of the surrounding geometry, but raw LiDAR scans lack a compact, structured representation for high-frequency control. s6672e5bff7.summary: Researchers propose a LiDAR perception pipeline using spherical range images to improve sim-to-real transfer for legged robot locomotion.
s6672e5bff7.why: Depth-image and elevation-map approaches suffer sim-to-real gaps, so a LiDAR representation could make locomotion policies more robust on hardware.

s1b398c5722.title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
s1b398c5722.description: arXiv:2611.27260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expecting guardrails to provide a general guarantee of safety fails to recognize the limits of computational enforcement and policy specification. We argue that promising such perfection is an ethical failure of precision, and that invoking it to abdicate responsibility is a moral failure. s1b398c5722.summary: Authors argue LLM output guardrails cannot guarantee safety and present a computational boundary on deciding output policies.
s1b398c5722.why: Teams relying on guardrails as complete safety guarantees should note theoretical limits and keep human responsibility and testing in place.

sc2dfcaf92f.title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
sc2dfcaf92f.description: arXiv:2611.27283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dermatologists describe lesions with a standardized morphological lexicon, which makes concept-based models attractive for interpretable skin disease diagnosis. How much diagnostic information these concepts actually carry, however, is rarely quantified. We present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the expert-annotated SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k (3,230 images, 48 concepts, 113 diseases). DermKG has 3,452 nodes of 8 types and 19,365 edges of 11 relation types, and encodes disease concept profiles, concept co-occurrence, a three-level diagnostic hierarchy, and 20 clinical morphology rules, all of which are supported by the training data (15 strong, 5 moderate). sc2dfcaf92f.summary: Researchers present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k for interpretable skin disease diagnosis.

scd268a271b.title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting
scd268a271b.description: arXiv:2611.27286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current large language model (LLM) agents still struggle to forecast real-world events. This stems from two primary limitations: i) standard ReAct harness accumulates reasoning and evidence within one growing context, and ii) outcome-based rewards in forecasting lead to a slow and noisy signal that cannot distinguish sound reasoning from lucky guesses. To address these, we introduce a forecasting training framework including harness design and post-training. scd268a271b.summary: Researchers propose a forecasting training framework for LLM agents, combining Proactive Belief-State Management in the harness with rubric-based rewards in post-training.
scd268a271b.why: It targets two known weaknesses of agentic forecasting: context bloat in ReAct loops and slow, noisy outcome-only rewards.

s56f47ff6a1.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
s56f47ff6a1.description: arXiv:2611.27294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. s56f47ff6a1.summary: HookEvo is a framework that uses agent runtime lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses, with an improver proposing candidates that are evaluated against the current harness.
s56f47ff6a1.why: It offers a method for automatically repairing tool-using agent failures by coordinating changes to tool receipts, context assembly, and action checks.

s74a9dcadb0.title: $\gamma$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
s74a9dcadb0.description: arXiv:2611.27306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent embodied agents construct and adapt robot behavior through executable programs, tool use, and interaction feedback. Studying these systems in mobile manipulation calls for physical worlds that connect agent-directed execution with its physical consequences and reusable interaction experience. We introduce $\gamma$-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence. Agents compose motion tools and learned skills to carry out complete tasks that combine navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. s74a9dcadb0.summary: Researchers introduce γ-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform where agents compose motion tools and learned skills for mobile manipulation tasks.
s74a9dcadb0.why: It provides a persistent physical simulation benchmark for evaluating embodied agents that combine navigation and manipulation.

sd6efc31d2a.title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection
sd6efc31d2a.description: arXiv:2611.27329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large instruction-tuning corpora contain substantial semantic redundancy, motivating the selection of compact subsets that preserve useful supervision while reducing training cost. We introduce H-MSAE, a hierarchical sparse instruction selection framework that organizes multi-resolution concepts learned by a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder into a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. sd6efc31d2a.summary: H-MSAE is a hierarchical sparse instruction selection method that organizes concepts from a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder to pick diverse, compact instruction-tuning subsets.
sd6efc31d2a.why: It aims to cut instruction-tuning costs by removing semantic redundancy without the annotation overhead of existing diversity selectors.

s3a75be3aed.title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning
s3a75be3aed.description: arXiv:2611.27330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A planner deciding whether to turn left or continue straight needs to inspect different parts of the scene for each maneuver. Yet many end-to-end driving planners evaluate every candidate trajectory against the same compressed scene representation. s3a75be3aed.why: It proposes a per-trajectory attention mechanism for planning, relevant to autonomous driving stack design.

sb2c44c249e.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
sb2c44c249e.description: arXiv:2611.27349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout e-commerce workflows to generate content that informs purchasing decisions and supports customer interactions. Evaluating these systems requires accounting for user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that are not fully captured by general-purpose writing benchmarks. We introduce EcomWriteBench, a real-world benchmark containing 3,861 queries from 69 e-commerce writing tasks across 13 categories and five languages. sb2c44c249e.summary: EcomWriteBench is a benchmark of 3,861 queries across 69 e-commerce writing tasks, 13 categories and five languages, for evaluating LLMs on commerce content.
sb2c44c249e.why: It offers a domain-specific evaluation set for teams deploying LLMs in e-commerce content and customer workflows.

sc15a9d5ce0.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
sc15a9d5ce0.description: arXiv:2611.27350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GraphRAG combines a language model's parametric knowledge with retrieved graph evidence, yet aggregate accuracy cannot show whether failures stem from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge. sc15a9d5ce0.summary: GRACE is a GraphRAG benchmark built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata, applying controlled evidence interventions to diagnose knowledge integration failures.

s1f40527b0d.title: WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs
s1f40527b0d.description: arXiv:2611.27365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bringing multimodal intelligence from the cloud to users' devices keeps sensitive data local and reduces inference cost, but deploying a specialized model per capability duplicates vision-language capacity under tight memory and compute budgets. s1f40527b0d.why: It addresses running several multimodal capabilities in one model under tight memory and compute budgets on user devices.

sb9e9d87c99.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance
sb9e9d87c99.description: arXiv:2611.27369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain specialization of large language models (LLMs) often improves target-domain performance but degrades broad capabilities. sb9e9d87c99.why: It offers a training-free alternative to fine-tuning that may preserve broad model abilities when adding domain specialization.

s600ed65a73.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
s600ed65a73.description: arXiv:2611.27372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World-action models (WAMs) often generate future visual states alongside robot actions, introducing substantial computational overhead during inference. se2054f5cfa.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
se2054f5cfa.description: arXiv:2611.27390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. s7a2bf0a96f.title: Beyond Linear Decodability: Understanding and Improving Instruction Following in World Action Models
s7a2bf0a96f.description: arXiv:2611.27401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World action models (WAMs) exhibit strong manipulation capabilities yet often fail to follow test-time language instructions. s830195f89c.title: Jagged Robustness: Uneven Safety Transfer and Emerging Vulnerabilities under LLM Quantization
s830195f89c.description: arXiv:2611.27424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantization enables efficient inference in language models through model parameter compression. s1431d3eec6.title: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy: A judgment-aggregation perspective
s1431d3eec6.description: arXiv:2611.27463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy is based on the idea that some sentences, or predicates within them, have multiple competing interpretations or specifications. s10b9bbb2d3.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
s10b9bbb2d3.description: arXiv:2611.27483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). se5e8375acb.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
se5e8375acb.description: arXiv:2611.27489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. s47609eed3e.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
s47609eed3e.description: arXiv:2611.27495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning enables safety-aligned code language models to adapt to diverse downstream tasks. s9c3ba71680.title: Altair-Nidhogg: Which Model-Merging Theories Hold for a One-Pass Decision Encoder? Soups, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE Against Joint Training and Prediction Ensembling
s9c3ba71680.description: arXiv:2611.27550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laya is a small model that answers a multiple-choice question in one pass: each option has a name and a written description. A new skill costs a training run, so we test whether published recipes for merging fine-tuned models (weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE) work for it, and whether the theories behind them hold. All 156 models start from one released checkpoint: four plain fine-tunes, five specialists (each adds one kind of training row), joint fine-tunes on all rows, and prediction ensembles. Items are held-out, synthetic and LLM-labelled. In-family, each skill is scored on new items of its own kind, and "kept" is the share of a specialist's gain over the plain fine-tune. Averaging four specialists keeps 52% [38, 64] with +1.
s9c3ba71680.summary: Researchers test whether model-merging methods like weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES and DARE work for a small one-pass multiple-choice decision model across 156 models.
s9c3ba71680.why: Tests whether cheap model merging can replace retraining for adding skills, which matters for maintaining small specialized models.

s86d158aa7c.title: Vega-Fafnir: Is Greedy Decoding the Same Decoding? Where Rounding Noise in Speculative Verification Comes From and What Removing It Costs
s86d158aa7c.description: arXiv:2611.27554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Serving engines treat the ways of running a greedy language model as interchangeable: cached or not, padded or not, alone or batched, one token or several verified at once (speculative decoding). In finite precision they round differently. We measure how often the greedy text of Qwen3-0.6B (bfloat16, 128 new tokens, GSM8K and ARC prompts) differs from a reference that decodes one token per pass. Verifying 4 guessed tokens per pass changes 60% of 150 prompts and padding changes 68%; every first divergence has a top-1 minus top-2 logit gap of 0.375 or less. A split of the noise shows that cache entries written by multi-token passes are about as noisy as the multi-token pass itself. A margin gate (fall back to one token when the gap is below a b
s86d158aa7c.summary: Researchers show that greedy decoding outputs can differ across serving configurations such as batching, padding and speculative decoding due to finite-precision rounding noise.
s86d158aa7c.why: Serving optimizations like speculative decoding and padding can change greedy outputs, which matters for reproducibility and evaluation consistency.

s87e00e1f86.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
s87e00e1f86.description: arXiv:2611.27559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of inverse-designed, pixelated passives for microwave and millimeter-wave applications has been a major development in the field of RFIC design. These devices, which appear to be QR-code-like in structure, exist in a generalizable, high-dimensional design space that includes conventional passive topologies. However, these structures are naturally unintuitive for designers, and failures or deviations in performance are difficult to debug. In this work, we ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict, and edit the responses and layout structure of pixelated passives. The agent, run with all tools disabled, is first asked to read layouts on 18x18 and 27x27 tile grids and, in a single reply, predict the input impeda
s87e00e1f86.summary: Researchers ask whether a frontier language model can understand, predict and edit pixelated inverse-designed RFIC passive structures.
s87e00e1f86.why: Tests whether LLMs can help RF engineers interpret and debug unintuitive inverse-designed circuit layouts.

sdfd85174f2.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
sdfd85174f2.description: arXiv:2611.27622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public benchmarks guide model selection, post-training rewards and claims of progress in artificial intelligence, yet leaderboards report aggregate scores without verifying whether each task's prompt, environment and grader agree on what counts as success. How often that agreement fails in contemporary evaluations, and in which direction confirmed defects move scores, has remained unmeasured across grading designs. Here we synthesize task-level quality reviews of 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations spanning closed-form question answering, document rubrics and agentic execution to assess whether prompts, environments and graders align. Task validity stratifies sharply by grading architecture. Closed-form
sdfd85174f2.summary: Researchers review 749 tasks across eight frontier benchmarks and 767 public model evaluations to measure how often task prompts, environments and graders disagree on success.
sdfd85174f2.why: Benchmark scores may be distorted by grading defects, so leaders should verify evaluation validity before trusting leaderboard claims.

s1f92924c89.title: Learning Inside Types: Epistemic Typestates for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
s1f92924c89.description: arXiv:2611.27631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Type disciplines make programs safe by construction: components checked against each other's types compose into programs that cannot go wrong in the ways the types exclude. Types suit reinforcement learning: a type constrains what an agent may choose, not how it chooses, so the guarantee holds for every policy a learner produces. We introduce epistemic typestates, a type discipline for safe multi-agent reinforcement learning. An agent's type is a protocol whose states record its beliefs, the worlds it cannot rule out from its own observations and actions, and permits only actions that are safe in every world of the belief, whatever the others do within their public types. Agents learn inside their types, which are built and checked one agent
s1f92924c89.summary: Researchers introduce epistemic typestates, a type discipline intended to make multi-agent reinforcement learning agents safe by construction.
s1f92924c89.why: Offers a type-based approach to constraining multi-agent learning agents so safety guarantees hold for any learned policy.

s24f6bd9328.title: Learning in Symbiosis: Heterogeneous Federated Learning with ANNs and SNNs
s24f6bd9328.description: arXiv:2611.27686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), widely regarded as the third generation of neural networks, represent a promising neuromorphic computing paradigm with the potential to reduce the energy footprint of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Their en-ergy efficiency makes SNNs particularly attractive for resource-constrained Edge AI devices, motivating growing research interest in Federated Learning (FL) with SNNs. Despite these advantages, integrating SNNs into existing FL systems remains challenging, as replacing all conventional Artificial Neural Network (ANN) devices with SNN-based alternatives is impractical. Instead, we envision a gradual transition toward neuromorphic Edge AI, where ANN and SNN devices coexist and collaboratively participate in FL.
s24f6bd9328.summary: Researchers propose heterogeneous federated learning that combines conventional ANNs and spiking neural networks for resource-constrained edge devices.
s24f6bd9328.why: Mixing ANN and SNN clients could let energy-efficient edge devices join federated systems without replacing existing architectures.

s6eddeb3fca.title: Comparative Performance of Machine Learning Architectures for Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Chemical Processes
s6eddeb3fca.description: arXiv:2611.27696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) is crucial for both maintenance and control in chemical industries, where early fault detection can prevent costly failures and optimize operations. This is particularly critical in pilot units like those at IFP Energies Nouvelles (IFPEN), which operate under short-term experimental conditions with frequently varying operational parameters. This study conducts an extensive benchmarking analysis using the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP), a widely used simulated chemical process dataset, to evaluate multiple approaches for fault detection and diagnosis, featuring numerous continuous operations with different sensors and faults. Several methods were implemented and compared including Multi Scale PCA (MS-PCA),
s6eddeb3fca.summary: Researchers benchmark multiple machine learning architectures for fault detection and diagnosis on the Tennessee Eastman Process chemical simulation dataset.
s6eddeb3fca.why: Provides comparative evidence on which ML architectures perform best for industrial process fault detection.

sd21f7f6805.title: Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Fault Detection and Structural Learning in Chemical Processes: Use Case on the Tennessee Eastman Process
sd21f7f6805.description: arXiv:2611.27698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) methods, including many data-driven approaches, assume a static normal operating space and interpret deviations from a fixed reference as fault indicators. When Operating Conditions (OCs) vary over time, this assumption breaks down: legitimate transitions trigger false alarms while moderate faults go undetected. We propose a spatiotemporal Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework that decomposes the normal operating space into OC-specific subspaces linked by transition functions, with a dual learning objective combining reconstruction loss and a Deep SVDD one-class term. It learns adjacency matrices through Graph Attention Networks (GATs) and integrates spatial modelling with temporal encoding to repr
sd21f7f6805.summary: Researchers propose a spatiotemporal graph neural network that models varying operating conditions for fault detection on the Tennessee Eastman Process.
sd21f7f6805.why: Addresses false alarms from legitimate operating-condition changes, a practical problem for industrial monitoring systems.

s821b16eae4.title: Abstract What Varies, Reuse Longer Patterns: Efficient Offline Chain-of-Thought Compression
s821b16eae4.description: arXiv:2611.27710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Offline chain-of-thought (CoT) compression creates shorter supervision for efficient reasoning, but per-example compressors repeatedly process similar expressions across traces, wasting compressor budget. Methods that reuse identical text across examples miss longer shared expressions when names, numbers, or formulas change from one question to another. We introduce CRAFT, which abstracts problem-specific details into slots to uncover partially lexicalized expression templates (PLETs) and clusters wording variants into families. Compressing each family representative once yields shared deletion or rewriting edits, which are applied with each occurrence's own details to construct compact, ordinary-text training targets. Compared with per-examp
s821b16eae4.summary: Researchers introduce CRAFT, an offline chain-of-thought compression method that abstracts problem details into slots to reuse longer shared expression templates.
s821b16eae4.why: Reusing shared reasoning templates could cut compressor cost when generating shorter supervision for efficient reasoning models.

s57d3c90b15.title: When Are Images Needed in Multimodal Machine Translation? Text-Only Routing for On-Demand Visual Context
s57d3c90b15.description: arXiv:2611.27712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image-guided multimodal machine translation (MMT) leverages visual context to resolve translation-relevant uncertainty. However, prevailing systems either process images unconditionally or apply gating only after visual encoding, leaving redundant visual computation unavoidable. To mitigate this computational overhead, routing decisions must rely on a pre-visual source signal. Crucially, surface-level ambiguity does not equate to visual dependence, as intra-sentence textual context often suffices for disambiguation. We therefore formulate visual invocation as source-text sufficiency prediction: determining exclusively from the source text whether translation-relevant uncertainty remains unresolved. To support this formulation, we construct a
s57d3c90b15.summary: Researchers propose text-only routing to decide when images are needed in multimodal machine translation, skipping visual encoding when unnecessary.
s57d3c90b15.why: Routing before visual encoding could reduce redundant compute in multimodal translation pipelines without losing needed visual context.

s7b6e82a7e9.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
s7b6e82a7e9.description: arXiv:2611.27713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated meta-analysis requires not only accurate numerical extraction but also the consistent preservation of result identity across stages, including the associated study, comparison, population, outcome, time point, and analysis conditions. We present MetaRigor, an LLM workflow framework for verifiable end-to-end evidence synthesis. MetaRigor organizes study results as Study x Target units and operationalizes scientific decision boundaries at the task level through Task Contracts, programmatic rules, and source binding. The model performs semantic interpretation that depends on study context, whereas programs execute formalizable rules, computations, validation, and source verification. We conducted controlled evaluations across five stag
s7b6e82a7e9.summary: Researchers present MetaRigor, an LLM workflow framework for automated meta-analysis that preserves result identity and applies programmatic verification rules.
s7b6e82a7e9.why: Shows an approach to making LLM-driven evidence extraction verifiable through task contracts and source binding.

s139ff49e39.title: Recoverable Symbols, Unstable Execution: Auditing Internal Pathways and Decision Identity in Visual State Tracking
s139ff49e39.description: arXiv:2611.27715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual features can retain every symbol a task needs while a model built on them still changes its answer when irrelevant parts of the image change. We study this gap in visual state tracking, where a recurrent executor reads a sequence of symbol tiles through a frozen ViT encoder and decides whether a displayed candidate equals the final state. Our diagnostic pairs each input with a donor view that preserves every queried tile, checks with a symbol-supervised decoder that the full symbol chain is recoverable from both feature sequences, and swaps individual internal channels of the same fitted executor in both directions. On 3,526 pairs in which every symbol is recovered in both views, changing the surrounding context lowers the balanced acc
s139ff49e39.summary: Researchers audit visual state tracking models and find that a model can retain needed symbols yet change answers when irrelevant image content changes.
s139ff49e39.why: Reveals that correct internal features do not guarantee stable decisions, a reliability concern for vision-based systems.

sd2dad4dc7c.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing
sd2dad4dc7c.description: arXiv:2611.27738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layer skipping can reduce large language model inference costs, but a request budget does not specify how to allocate layer execution across generated tokens. We introduce \method{}, which allows tokens to execute different numbers of layers while matching each request's mean executed depth to a continuous budget. At each routed layer, a router reads the current token state and its request's budget and decides whether to execute the Transformer block. Tokens that skip the block pass through a lightweight residual adapter and write no key/value (K/V) entry at that layer. A single checkpoint serves requests with different budgets in the same batch. Across three LLaMA backbones, six quality metrics, and 13 budgets, AVERT is best or tied for best
sd2dad4dc7c.summary: Researchers introduce a method that lets tokens execute variable numbers of Transformer layers, matching each request's mean executed depth to a set budget.
sd2dad4dc7c.why: Per-token layer routing could let inference providers meet request-level compute budgets more precisely than uniform layer skipping.

s1b99b0ff5e.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
s1b99b0ff5e.description: arXiv:2611.27741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have endowed multimodal agents with increasingly strong visual perception and long-horizon reasoning capabilities, making VLM-based autonomous game playing feasible. Existing game benchmarks primarily evaluate whether an agent can select appropriate actions from the current visual state across different scenarios and games. However, most of them adopt a step-by-step interaction paradigm where the current visual observation is sent to the agent before each action. In practical deployment, this paradigm introduces two fundamental limitations: the game loop must wait for model inference, making real-time interaction impractical, and repeated VLM calls incur substantial cost. Therefore, we propose
s1b99b0ff5e.summary: Researchers study whether vision-language models can synthesize executable programs that play games, instead of choosing actions step by step from visual observations.
s1b99b0ff5e.why: It suggests agents could generate reusable game-playing code rather than querying a model at every step, potentially cutting inference costs.

sc56d7a1954.title: QuASAR: Toward an LLM-Assisted Framework for Screening, Prototyping, and Assessing Quantum-Advantage Opportunities in Scientific Computing
sc56d7a1954.description: arXiv:2611.27778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying scientific computations that could benefit from quantum algorithms requires both domain knowledge and fluency in quantum algorithm design, expertise that rarely resides in one person. We report results from QuASAR, an experimental, two-agent, LLM-driven pipeline intended to bridge this gap. One agent screens scientific literature for computational kernels with a plausible quantum-algorithmic analogue and proposes candidates, each backed by citations. A second agent independently verifies those citations. For candidates that survive verification, it reconstructs the source's computational structure, formulates a quantum mapping, builds and executes a prototype, and benchmarks it against classical baselines. We applied this pipeline
sc56d7a1954.summary: QuASAR is an experimental two-agent LLM pipeline that screens scientific literature for computations that might benefit from quantum algorithms, with a second agent verifying citations.

s1f0f0192e1.title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification
s1f0f0192e1.description: arXiv:2611.27783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated EEG seizure type classification systems are typically trained and evaluated under the closed-set assumption, where all seizure types encountered at deployment are seen during training. In clinical practice, this assumption fails: patients present with rare or atypical seizure types that fall outside the training label space, and a system that forces a wrong label is worse than one that abstains. We introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus (TUSZ v2.0.3), defining known and unknown classes using the clinical taxonomy itself: seizure types with sufficient subject representation (at least 12 subjects) form the known set, and rare types form the
s1f0f0192e1.summary: Researchers introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus, with a fairness analysis.
s1f0f0192e1.why: Clinical classifiers that abstain on unfamiliar seizure types may be safer than ones forced to pick a wrong label, which matters for medical ML design.

se2b76be353.title: ChildAI-Gov: An Evidence-Linked AI System for Assessing EdTech Policies Against Children's Digital Rights
se2b76be353.description: arXiv:2611.27799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ChildAI-Gov, an explainable AI system for assessing whether education-technology (EdTech) policies respect children's digital rights. Generative AI is reaching children's education faster than its governance can keep pace, yet checking a tool against children's rights remains manual, expert-dependent, and slow. We propose the Child Rights Impact Score (CRIS), an evidence-linked measure across five dimensions: safety, privacy, transparency, autonomy, and non-discrimination. ChildAI-Gov reads an EdTech tool's privacy or AI policy and scores each dimension by combining a large-language-model judgement (gpt-4o-mini) with a deterministic rule check. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) component grounds every score in the governing pr
se2b76be353.summary: ChildAI-Gov is an explainable AI system that scores EdTech policies against children's digital rights using a proposed Child Rights Impact Score across five dimensions.
se2b76be353.why: Teams building or selling EdTech products may need evidence-linked compliance checks against children's privacy and safety expectations.

sb4fe9c5d14.title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
sb4fe9c5d14.description: arXiv:2611.27810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. Each statement the model makes about the voice needs to be checked against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. On clinical speech, existing evaluations score only the final answer. We introduce Speech Language Pathologist Bench (SLP-Bench), a benchmark grading each acoustic claim in the chain of thought against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. sb4fe9c5d14.summary: SLP-Bench is a benchmark that grades each acoustic claim made by reasoning audio language models on clinical speech, checking them against clinicians' perceptual ratings.
sb4fe9c5d14.why: It shows final-answer accuracy can hide unsupported reasoning, so evaluators of reasoning models should check intermediate claims too.

sb1113a1c71.title: Auditable Financial Knowledge Graphs: Schema-Driven Construction and Intrinsic Quality Evaluation
sb1113a1c71.description: arXiv:2611.27835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial documents combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, management commentary, and time-dependent facts, making them difficult to represent using conventional chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation systems. This paper presents an auditable, schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents parsed using a general purpose document intelligence service. Overlapping document windows undergo phased large language model extraction of structural entities, quantitative observations, and domain-specific relationships. sb1113a1c71.summary: The paper presents a schema-driven method for building auditable temporal financial knowledge graphs from parsed documents using phased LLM extraction.
sb1113a1c71.why: Auditable knowledge graphs offer an alternative to chunk-based RAG for financial documents where temporal facts and traceability matter.

sb9d67ea5a4.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
sb9d67ea5a4.description: arXiv:2611.27839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems for scientific claim verification increasingly rely on role-structured LLM debate to pressure-test hypotheses. However, when debating agents are instantiated from the same underlying base model, they share identical latent representations, making self-critique bias structurally inevitable. Static fixed-iteration protocols compound this by either halting prematurely before evidence stabilizes or wasting inference compute after convergence. We present \sys{}, a multi-agent research verification framework that addresses both failure modes.
