sb9d67ea5a4.summary: The paper proposes an epistemic convergence control framework for multi-agent research verification, addressing self-critique bias from debating agents built on the same base model.
sb9d67ea5a4.why: Same-model debate agents share latent representations, so adaptive stopping based on convergence may improve verification while reducing wasted compute.

s2f4425693f.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
s2f4425693f.description: arXiv:2611.27865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Specification-guided reinforcement learning (RL) translates formal specifications of desired behavior of agents into shaped rewards. This paper introduces SLICR, a significant paradigm shift that advances the state of the art to specification-guided RL in adversarial settings under partial observability. We employ Strategy Logic (SL), which allows explicit quantification over agents' strategies and uses the linear temporal logic (LTL) to specify the agents' objectives and constraints. This enables reasoning not only about how agents should act to satisfy a specification, but also about how they should respond to the strategies and behaviors of other agents. We evaluate SLICR on three popular benchmarks: Predator-Prey, Google Research Football
s2f4425693f.summary: SLICR is a specification-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning method that uses Strategy Logic and LTL to shape rewards in adversarial, partially observable settings.

s6bbcef2675.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence with Learning Style Models: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
s6bbcef2675.description: arXiv:2611.27868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for transforming learning. This review examines how Generative AI can be integrated with established learning style models (VARK, Kolb, Felder-Silverman, and Honey & Mumford) to support student engagement in large online classes. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar (2015 to 2026) and included 41 studies that met the eligibility criteria. The review maps Generative AI capabilities to learning style preferences, synthesizes existing implementations, highlights benefits and challenges, and proposes pathways for future research and practice. Despite ongoing debates regarding the empirical validity of learning styles,
s6bbcef2675.summary: A PRISMA-guided review of 41 studies examines how generative AI can be integrated with learning style models to support engagement in large online classes.

s41ceb802cc.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
s41ceb802cc.description: arXiv:2611.27891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. s41ceb802cc.summary: The paper introduces DICE, a speculative decoding method that fixes sampling randomness before drafting to better anticipate the target model's path.
s41ceb802cc.why: Speculative decoding speedups depend on drafting accuracy, so better candidate selection could improve LLM inference throughput in production.

s324f6fffad.title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
s324f6fffad.description: arXiv:2611.27899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution. Tier 1 (Macro System) acts as a scalable user sentiment regression detector, utilizing a fine-tuned encoder-decoder LLM (based on Gemini XS) on telemetry features. s324f6fffad.summary: Google researchers describe the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, an industrial system that automates UX attribution for large-scale web search using telemetry and multimodal analysis.
s324f6fffad.why: It offers a scalable alternative to slow surveys for evaluating UX during rapid A/B testing in production search systems.

s2746ba9799.title: Functional Depth Is Learned: Isolating the Computation That Layers Produce Only Together
s2746ba9799.description: arXiv:2611.27911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. s2746ba9799.summary: The paper introduces an inclusion-exclusion decomposition to track how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, using public checkpoints such as Pythia.
s2746ba9799.why: Understanding whether layers compute jointly rather than independently informs architecture and pretraining decisions for model depth.

sca45f71708.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
sca45f71708.description: arXiv:2611.27924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. sca45f71708.summary: BioEmu2 is a generative model that predicts atomically resolved biomolecular structures and dynamics, sampling orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics.
sca45f71708.why: Fast generative emulation of molecular dynamics could make large-scale biomolecular simulation practical for drug discovery workflows.

sd69e6d56f6.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
sd69e6d56f6.description: arXiv:2611.26504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual reinforcement learning requires agents to adapt when the task changes while reusing what they know about the environment. Successor features separate dynamics from task-specific reward, but their effectiveness depends on the choice of base features. Taking the identification of entorhinal grid cells with eigenvectors of the successor representation as a design principle, we build this basis from eigenvectors of the transition matrix of a fixed reference policy. sd69e6d56f6.summary: The paper proposes building a successor-feature basis from eigenvectors of a reference policy's transition matrix, inspired by entorhinal grid cells, for continual reinforcement learning.

s6156f2b42b.title: VerifiQuant: Governance-by-Execution for Financial LLM Workflows
s6156f2b42b.description: arXiv:2611.26649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models embedded in financial workflows fail most dangerously by emitting confident, well-formatted but wrong numbers with no signal distinguishing them from correct ones. We argue that the central deployment problem is governability: a system must determine when a question supports a numeric answer and when it should instead clarify, intercept, or refuse. We present VerifiQuant, a governance-by-execution framework that packages financial logic into inference contracts and evaluates each query through an executable diagnostic funnel before deterministic computation. This separation makes computation, clarification, and refusal structured and auditable while keeping financial arithmetic outside the language model. Against match
s6156f2b42b.summary: VerifiQuant is a governance-by-execution framework that routes financial LLM queries through an executable diagnostic funnel to answer, clarify, intercept, or refuse.
s6156f2b42b.why: Financial teams deploying LLMs need mechanisms to detect when confident numeric answers are unsupported and should not be returned.

s79baee7cb3.title: Computing Weighted Set Covers with Heterogeneous Stochastic Oracles: Deadline-Constrained Token Complexity
s79baee7cb3.description: arXiv:2611.26656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study computation in which a probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) uses AI systems, abstracted as heterogeneous stochastic oracles (HSOs), to solve Weighted Set Cover. A pilot study shows that an LLM can outperform weighted greedy. HSOs differ in capabilities, response distributions, latencies, and token costs. We study how the PTM selects HSOs to obtain, by a deadline and with a required success probability, a full cover satisfying a prescribed weight threshold, and we analyze expected token cost. s79baee7cb3.summary: Researchers study a probabilistic Turing machine that selects among heterogeneous AI oracles to solve Weighted Set Cover under deadline and success-probability constraints, analyzing expected token cost.
s79baee7cb3.why: It offers a theoretical framework for choosing among LLMs by latency, cost, and capability under deadlines, relevant to cost-aware model routing.

sf6d163deda.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
sf6d163deda.description: arXiv:2611.26671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While the critical points of the loss landscape in linear neural networks have been extensively studied since the seminal work of Baldi \& Hornik in the late 1980s, a description of this landscape at an intermediate or global scale is still lacking. Such a characterization is crucial, particularly as a substantial body of literature indicates that gradient descent circumvents critical points. The present article introduces an intermediate structure, termed the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and exhibits key geometric properties. Beyond providing a geometric proof of Baldi \& Hornik's results using simpler assumptions than the existing literature, this framework offers a global view of the loss landscape that can be
sf6d163deda.summary: A paper introduces the critical thalweg, an intermediate structure describing the loss landscape of linear neural networks beyond their critical points.
sf6d163deda.why: It is theoretical work on optimization geometry in linear networks, with limited direct near-term impact for practitioners.

s17e1c230ba.title: Model the Annotation, Not the Noise: Semantic Annotation-Channel Prompt Learning against Noisy Labels
s17e1c230ba.description: arXiv:2611.26702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parameter-efficient prompt learning has become a cornerstone for adapting pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs), yet it remains highly vulnerable to label noise in few-shot Web and retrieval scenarios. Existing noise robust methods typically rely on hard sample selection or deterministic label correction, which discard valuable semantic ambiguity and overlook how observed annotations are actually generated. To bridge this gap, we reformulate noisy prompt learning through the perspective of data generation, proposing SACP, a Semantic-aware Annotation Channel-based Prompt learning framework. Instead of suppressing noise heuristically, SACP decouples latent clean-label prediction from instance-dependent annotation generation. By integratin
s17e1c230ba.summary: Researchers propose SACP, a method that models how annotations are generated to improve prompt learning for vision-language models under label noise.
s17e1c230ba.why: It addresses label-noise robustness in few-shot prompt tuning of vision-language models, useful for teams training on noisy web data.

s33fa89e5f0.title: INCISE: Training-Free In-Context Segmentation of Surgical Videos
s33fa89e5f0.description: arXiv:2611.26734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surgical video analysis requires video object segmentation (VOS), yet existing methods are commonly based on pretrained model fine-tuning using a large number of expert labels. In-context segmentation (ICS) offers the promise of bypassing this high cost by segmenting a target video using a few annotated references, which are the sole source of surgical knowledge for a frozen model. However, existing ICS methods tend to draw such references at random, which concentrate on a few views that dominate a surgical video and can miss other objects of interest (e.g., transient instruments and small structures). To address these challenges, we propose INCISE, a training-free ICS framework for surgical videos. INCISE selects unlabeled frames from mult
s33fa89e5f0.summary: INCISE is a training-free in-context segmentation method for surgical videos that selects reference frames more diversely than random sampling.
s33fa89e5f0.why: It shows how few annotated references can drive segmentation with a frozen model, reducing expert labeling costs in medical video.

s939dd4e24e.title: MomentMem: Memorizing Key Moments for Robot Manipulation
s939dd4e24e.description: arXiv:2611.26745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. Existing approaches typically rely on full observation histories, which become redundant over long horizons, or text summaries, which may omit precise visual details. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. To support this study, we introduce VMBench, a suite of long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring memory of spatial locations, visual appearances, and their associations. We further propose MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture in which a VLM-based memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on the
s939dd4e24e.summary: MomentMem is a method for robot manipulation that stores key visual moments, evaluated on a new benchmark, VMBench, of long-horizon memory-dependent tasks.
s939dd4e24e.why: It targets memory limits in robot policies over long horizons, a practical concern for embodied AI system design.

s097f75a8ae.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
s097f75a8ae.description: arXiv:2611.26752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Iterative architectures such as looped language models improve parameter efficiency and reasoning capacity of transformers, yet their sequential backbone iterations introduce substantial computational latency. Conversely, parallelizable learnable special tokens (such as the register tokens in Vision Transformer) enable efficient single-pass inference, but often suffer from the absence of sequential refinement and exhibit redundant representations across tokens. To address these challenges, we introduce Depth-Linked Residual Tokens (DepThink), an efficient framework designed for multimodal retrieval and generation. Operating within a single pre-filling forward pass, DepThink appends a sequence of K learnable residual tokens whose hidden stat
s097f75a8ae.summary: DepThink introduces Depth-Linked Residual Tokens, learnable tokens for multimodal retrieval and generation that aim to combine single-pass efficiency with sequential refinement.
s097f75a8ae.why: It proposes a way to get iterative-style refinement without sequential latency, relevant to efficient multimodal model design.

s33d293c9ef.title: Self-verifiable LLM-driven science and why it needs human researchers
s33d293c9ef.description: arXiv:2611.26754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models are now used throughout all sciences - for reading literature, extracting numbers from tables and spectra, analyzing data, drafting conclusions - and their answers arrive in the same polished confident tone whether they are right or wrong, so a result has to be re-derived by a human researcher before it can be relied on. The cost of that re-checking, not the ability to generate results, is what currently limits AI-assisted research. In the field of mathematics, this problem is solved by proof assistants like Lean 4 and Coq that let any formal statement and its proof be written down and checked - a perfect match for LLMs, which are now actively used to search for proofs with every step automatically validated, rather than rel
s33d293c9ef.summary: A paper argues that LLM-driven scientific results need self-verification, comparing it to proof assistants like Lean 4 and Coq, and argues human researchers remain necessary.
s33d293c9ef.why: It frames verification cost as the bottleneck for AI-assisted research, a concern for teams relying on model-generated analysis.

safaaa1ede6.title: Windchime: an Audiovisual Installation with Audio-Language Model implementations
safaaa1ede6.description: arXiv:2611.26759v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Windchime is an audiovisual installation in which spoken language retrieves music and interactive animations from an artist authored corpus. A local Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model transcribes each prompt while an audio-language model (ALM) embeds it and retrieval over 406 audio stems returns a soundscape with live coded Strudel fragments that layer into audio output. Simultaneously each spoken input results in retrieval of interactive Three.js animation scenes each containing unique tactile control via monome grid and arc hardware. Windchime distributes agency in three distinct directions; across the artist who authored the possible outputs, the ALM that influences what areas of the corpus can be retrieved, and the visitor whose s
safaaa1ede6.summary: Windchime is an audiovisual installation where spoken prompts are transcribed by ASR, embedded by an audio-language model, and used to retrieve music and animations.
safaaa1ede6.why: It is an artistic installation showcasing audio-language retrieval, with limited direct relevance for engineering teams.

s855fdd5d81.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference
s855fdd5d81.description: arXiv:2611.26776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Systems that flag violent video for a human operator can now be built from language models without training, by combining perception models and letting a language model decide. We ask how the observations of the perception models should reach the decision, and which evidence matters. On the XD-Violence test set (799 clips) we fix one set of perception agents (video description, object detection, sound tagging, speech recognition and speech tagging) and one reasoning model, and compare three interfaces: messages between agents, a typed evidence graph explored with tools, and flat text read in one pass; and a single audio-visual model given the raw clip. Two annotators provide a human reference that records the decision, the incident segments
s855fdd5d81.summary: A controlled study on XD-Violence compares three interfaces for language-model agents that flag violent video: inter-agent messages, a typed evidence format, and a human evidence reference.
s855fdd5d81.why: It shows how agent communication design affects accuracy in multi-agent content moderation pipelines.

s15cb294b11.title: MedicalRSI: Medical Recursive Self-Improving Agents via Clinical Model-Harness Co-Evolution
s15cb294b11.description: arXiv:2611.26806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical agents built on large language models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly, yet most stay fixed once deployed and do not keep using their experience to improve later attempts. As a result, the same kind of error can recur across patients. To address this, existing self-improvement methods update an agent's weights or its medical harness from its own experience, but their improving strategy stays fixed and never learns which changes actually help, which caps how much the agent can improve. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) instead improves both the agent and its improving strategy. However, achieving RSI for medical agents is challenging, because clinical workflows rarely come with a reference harness, and a change that fixes early errors may
s15cb294b11.summary: MedicalRSI proposes medical LLM agents that recursively self-improve by co-evolving the model and its clinical harness, rather than using a fixed improvement strategy.
s15cb294b11.why: It addresses agents that repeat the same errors after deployment, a key reliability concern for clinical AI systems.

s3a32e13f20.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
s3a32e13f20.description: arXiv:2611.26809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed with access to search tools at inference. Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training. We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora. Specifically, we augment pretraining corpus at scale with web-search queries and retrieve web response using a local index. Training on this augmented corpus teaches models to generate search calls and incorporate retrieved evidence during language modeling. Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ("QueryLM") show improv
s3a32e13f20.summary: Search-Native Pretraining augments pretraining corpora with web-search queries and local-index retrieval so models learn search behavior during pretraining.
s3a32e13f20.why: It suggests search skills could be built in at pretraining rather than only in post-training, affecting how tool-using models are trained.

s7becd94492.title: Realistic Robustness Evaluation of Tabular Data Driven Models
s7becd94492.description: arXiv:2611.26818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The increasing adoption of Machine Learning (ML) models in high-stakes applications has raised critical concerns regarding their robustness against adversarial attacks. While extensive research has focused on adversarial example generation in image and text domains, the study of such examples in tabular data remains comparatively limited, despite its widespread use in real-world systems. This work introduces AURORA, a modular, open-source tool for evaluating the robustness of ML models on tabular data classification. It integrates multiple adversarial perturbation methods and evaluation metrics within a unified framework to systematically assess model behavior under adversarial conditions. Central to AURORA is its evaluation report, which f
s7becd94492.summary: AURORA is an open-source modular tool for evaluating the adversarial robustness of machine learning models on tabular data classification.
s7becd94492.why: It gives teams a tool to test tabular models against adversarial attacks, relevant to high-stakes deployments.

s448134cca8.title: Rethinking Full-Weight LoRA with Domain and Task Adapter Scaling for Question Answering over Portuguese Well Drilling Reports
s448134cca8.description: arXiv:2611.26833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) to specialized domains remains challenging, particularly for technical documents such as Portuguese well drilling reports, where annotated data are scarce and domain adaptation may compromise instruction-following capabilities. Although Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is widely used for parameter-efficient adaptation, its scaling after training remains insufficiently explored. This study investigates the impact of LoRA adapter scaling on question answering over Portuguese drilling reports using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. Domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT) is performed either directly on instruction-tuned models or on their base counterparts, with subsequent adapter transfer, while task-specific adapters ar
s448134cca8.summary: A study examines how LoRA adapter scaling after training affects question answering over Portuguese well drilling reports using Qwen2.5-7B and Llama models.
s448134cca8.why: It gives practical evidence that post-training LoRA scaling can be tuned for domain adaptation with scarce data.

safb2985349.title: Non-Expanding Gated Continued Fraction Architecture for Feedforward Layers in Language Models
safb2985349.description: arXiv:2611.26835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent work has shown that continued fraction inspired neural architectures (CoFrGeNets) can be highly parameter efficient yet performant for language modeling. In this work, we revisit continued fraction-based channel mixing with the goal of improving its performance and simplifying integration into standard pre-training protocols for language models. We achieve this by two simple yet critical contributions: i) we propose a novel non-expanding gated continued fraction inspired architectural component to replace feedforward layers in established language model architectures that may use vanilla multilayer perceptrons or gated linear units or (vanilla/gated) experts in mixture-of-experts (MoE) type architectures. ii) We propose a way to re-i
safb2985349.summary: Researchers propose a non-expanding gated continued fraction component to replace feedforward layers in language models, aiming for better performance and easier pretraining integration.
safb2985349.why: It proposes a parameter-efficient alternative to feedforward layers, though results are early and it remains a research architecture.

sa317892191.title: Scoliosis5K: Multimodal Gait Analysis via Clip-Conditioned RGB-Silhouette Fusion
sa317892191.description: arXiv:2611.26849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Color walking video records body boundary motion alongside clothing folds, surface appearance, and recording-environment cues. To examine what an explicit binary silhouette contributes to participant-level classification of scoliosis-related gait when a classifier already observes the paired color sequence, we construct Scoliosis5K, a multi-site collection of 4,998 corridor-walking sequences across 3,010 participant identifiers in which RGB person crops, binary silhouettes, and two-dimensional poses share each recording identifier and frame index. Our architecture uses each patch's pixel deviation from its clip mean to weight two low-rank query and value updates inside a pretrained RGB encoder, fusing the resulting video representation with
sa317892191.summary: Scoliosis5K is a multi-site dataset of 4,998 walking sequences from 3,010 participants, pairing RGB crops, silhouettes, and poses to study scoliosis-related gait classification.

s0a81ce2ad9.title: LoCo-WAM: Test-Time Training as Long Context for World-Action Models
s0a81ce2ad9.description: arXiv:2611.26853v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World-action models guide robot actions by predicting what happens next, but typically condition on a short observation history. Extending this history increases computation at every decision and can require a separately trained model. We introduce LoCo-WAM, which learns from the outcomes of its actions through test-time training while keeping the same short history length. It uses newly observed frames to update a low-rank adapter in the video expert, whose adapted predictions guide subsequent actions. The updates accumulate within each episode and are reset between episodes, allowing past observations to influence decisions after they leave the input window. LoCo-WAM thus learns from a longer stream of experience without expert action lab
s0a81ce2ad9.summary: Researchers introduce LoCo-WAM, which uses test-time training on newly observed frames to adapt a world-action model's video expert while keeping a short history.
s0a81ce2ad9.why: Offers a way for robot policies to learn from action outcomes within an episode without longer context windows or extra trained models.

sac822da2db.title: Coherent Moment Propagation: Epistemic Uncertainty for Pre-trained Robot Policies
sac822da2db.description: arXiv:2611.26855v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow matching policies underpin the state-of-the-art in robot learning, with impressive results ranging from long-horizon planning to dexterous manipulation. However, they provide no measure of whether their predicted commands can be trusted, particularly in novel situations outside their training set. Epistemic uncertainty reflects uncertainty about the model's weights and quantifies this ignorance, but calculating it at inference time from a flow matching policy is not trivial. Actions are produced by an ODE solver, requiring uncertainty to be propagated through the entire integration process. sac822da2db.summary: Researchers propose Coherent Moment Propagation, a method for estimating epistemic uncertainty in pre-trained flow matching robot policies at inference time.
sac822da2db.why: Gives engineers a way to tell when a flow matching robot policy's commands may be untrustworthy in novel situations.

s4b53343fee.title: Your Judge Inherits Your Prompt: In-Context Label Bias in an LLM-as-Judge Is Directional, Not Symmetric
s4b53343fee.description: arXiv:2611.26881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-as-judge has become a standard way to score open-ended model outputs, yet the judge is itself a frozen language model steered by a few in-context examples, and such models are known to absorb the label balance of their demonstrations rather than treat them as neutral illustrations. We ask whether this label bias reaches an LLM judge used inside a multimodal (video question answering) evaluation pipeline, and what form it takes. Using a fully frozen generator-judge pipeline, we hold the generated answers fixed and vary only the Yes/No balance of the judge's few-shot examples across four demonstration sets. s4b53343fee.summary: A study finds that in-context Yes/No label balance in demonstrations biases an LLM judge used in a video question answering evaluation pipeline, in a directional rather than symmetric way.
s4b53343fee.why: Shows LLM-as-judge scores can drift with prompt example balance, so evaluation pipelines need controls for judge bias.

s272bb8861b.title: ProbeAgent: Principled Diagnosis of Agent Failures in Verifiable Environments
s272bb8861b.description: arXiv:2611.26897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving agents requires discovering where they fail and understanding why. An agent acts over multiple steps in a changing environment, so diagnosing its failures requires more than inspecting the final response of a large language model (LLM). The same unsuccessful outcome can arise from task difficulty or from an error the agent repeats across tasks. We introduce ProbeAgent, an automated framework that discovers agent failures, tests their proposed causes, and identifies shared failure modes. Starting from benchmark tasks, ProbeAgent builds executable tests and validates them using reference solutions, automated checks, and review of the task requirements. For each failed trajectory, it explains the error and constructs new tasks that p
s272bb8861b.summary: ProbeAgent is an automated framework that discovers agent failures in verifiable environments, tests proposed causes, and identifies shared failure modes.
s272bb8861b.why: Provides a systematic method for diagnosing multi-step agent failures beyond inspecting final outputs.

s452aca6c0a.title: Modeling Attributional Style at Scale: A Dataset and Analysis for Psychological Attribution Assessment and Reframing
s452aca6c0a.description: arXiv:2611.26900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: According to the reformulated Learned Helplessness theory, repeated exposure to uncontrollable negative events can foster a depressogenic attributional style, increasing susceptibility to depression yet remaining a tractable target for cognitive therapy. Computational research on attributional cognition, however, is hampered by the lack of large-scale datasets and robust evaluation protocols. In this work, we introduce the Attributional Style Transfer Dataset (ASTD) along with dedicated evaluation metrics, the first benchmark designed to model, assess, and reframe attributional explanations at scale. Constructed via a Prevent-Filter-Validate pipeline that integrates LLM-based generation with specialist validation, ASTD contains 42,000 real-
s452aca6c0a.summary: Researchers release the Attributional Style Transfer Dataset and evaluation metrics, a benchmark for modeling and reframing attributional style in text.

sdfe0e1f588.title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
sdfe0e1f588.description: arXiv:2611.26902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An embodied agent cannot afford a large vision-language model (VLM) at every step of a long video, so a cascade runs a small VLM continuously and escalates only uncertain decisions to a large one. Each escalation, however, forces the large model to re-encode a history the small model has already perceived, and this dominates its cost. We present Baton, which hands the large model the small model's visual memory, its key-value (KV) cache over the history. Baton rests on one finding: the large model needs a usable memory, not a faithful copy of its own. sdfe0e1f588.summary: Baton proposes handing a small vision-language model's key-value cache over to a large VLM so escalations avoid re-encoding the video history.
sdfe0e1f588.why: Targets the dominant cost of cascaded VLM escalation in long-video embodied agents, relevant to inference budgets.

s7ef124dc9d.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
s7ef124dc9d.description: arXiv:2611.26909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance. With a full grid of competitors and stochastic race events, the ranking of D
s7ef124dc9d.summary: Researchers build a calibrated Formula 1 pit-stop simulator and compare five deep reinforcement learning agents against a quadratic mixed-integer programming formulation.

sd3dde3688e.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
sd3dde3688e.description: arXiv:2611.26919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Production retrieval systems are tied to the embedding model that indexed their corpus. Moving queries to a different encoder normally requires re-embedding the whole corpus, and at cold start there are no query logs while every document embedded by the new encoder incurs an API or compute cost. We present ERA (Embed, Route, Adapt), a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval. sd3dde3688e.summary: ERA is a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval that uses a small anchor budget and a lightweight adapter to avoid re-embedding the whole corpus.
sd3dde3688e.why: Could let teams switch query encoders without costly full corpus re-embedding, reducing retrieval migration cost.

sd8eb48fbaa.title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
sd8eb48fbaa.description: arXiv:2611.26920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) develop rich internal representations of language, but whether their individual coordinate axes carry meaning, or whether meaning is encoded only in directions in representation space, is still an open question. A common assumption is that individual axes in LLMs are arbitrary. We here challenge this view: across 12 LLMs from six model families, the native axes are reliably more aligned with other models' representations, with human brain responses to language, and with interpretable linguistic features than randomly rotated axes that preserve the same geometry. sd8eb48fbaa.summary: Across 12 LLMs from six model families, researchers find native coordinate axes are more aligned with brain responses and interpretable linguistic features than random rotations.

s69ac0c0529.title: Tokenize Moments, Not Frames: Tokenizer-Aware Budget Allocation for Training-Free Video LLM Acceleration
s69ac0c0529.description: arXiv:2611.26933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video large language models (LLMs) represent each video with thousands of visual tokens, and training-free accelerators that prune or merge these tokens lose accuracy on long videos. Analyzing frame similarity and the vision tokenizers of 16 open models, we trace this loss to a step before token selection. Under a token budget, the frames of a long video are sampled farther apart than the roughly 2 s over which frames remain similar. The two-frame 3D patches of models such as Qwen-VL then blend two unrelated scenes into each visual token, a double exposure that arises before any pruning or merging. s69ac0c0529.summary: Researchers propose tokenizer-aware budget allocation that samples video frames to match tokenizer temporal structure, improving training-free acceleration of video LLMs.
s69ac0c0529.why: Suggests cheap training-free token pruning for long video can be improved by respecting how the vision tokenizer groups frames.

s92ecbd2cf3.title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
s92ecbd2cf3.description: arXiv:2611.26936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can infer private information from shared images, including locations, personally identifiable information (PII), and personal attributes such as age and sex, even from medical images. Adversarial perturbations can protect such information against black-box VLMs, but existing methods overlook image quality and introduce visible artifacts into the images they protect. We present SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework that protects image privacy against VLMs while preserving visual fidelity. s92ecbd2cf3.summary: SecretAgent is a multi-agent framework that adds adversarial perturbations to images to protect private information from black-box vision-language models while preserving visual fidelity.
s92ecbd2cf3.why: Offers a privacy-protection approach for shared images that aims to avoid the visible artifacts of prior methods.

sc24424da6f.title: MG-EDA: Maturity-Gated Skew-Normal Estimation of Distribution Algorithms
sc24424da6f.description: arXiv:2611.26938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gaussian estimation of distribution algorithms shrink their variance on slopes and stall far from the optimum. This paper equips the corrections that act along the direction of movement -- a mean shift, an elongation of the covariance along the path and a skewness -- with the rule they lack: a calibrated gate, driven by a maturity statistic of the population, decides whether, how strongly and for how long each correction acts, and when the gate is closed the algorithm is exactly the estimation of multivariate normal algorithm (EMNA). sc24424da6f.summary: MG-EDA adds a maturity-gated skew-normal correction to estimation of distribution algorithms to help them escape stalls far from the optimum.

s0f4f657297.title: CENTRY: A Probabilistic Latent-State Model for Continual AI Risk Estimation, Monitoring, and Regulation
s0f4f657297.description: arXiv:2611.26940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, yet existing AI safety frameworks primarily define, categorize, or govern AI risk rather than proposing implementable models and methods for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk throughout an AI system's operational lifetime. This paper proposes CENTRY, a probabilistic framework that enables continual risk estimation, monitoring, and regulation of a deployed AI system from its interactions with its environment. The framework models AI risk as arising from three intrinsic sources: datasets, hardware resources, and models/algorithms. A structured latent-variable model is developed in which the latent representation is decomposed
s0f4f657297.summary: CENTRY proposes a probabilistic latent-state framework for continually estimating, monitoring, and regulating risk of a deployed AI system from its environmental interactions.
s0f4f657297.why: Proposes an implementable runtime risk monitoring model, relevant to teams operating safety-critical deployed AI systems.

sc82989c8f5.title: Tracking and Limiting Unsupported Claim Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Provenance-Aware Framework
sc82989c8f5.description: arXiv:2611.26957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This research examines how unsupported claims change as they move through multi-agent pipelines. It also examines whether preserving provenance can reduce these changes. We test both homogeneous and heterogeneous pipelines. Homogeneous pipelines use the same model across agents, while heterogeneous pipelines use different models. We compare the baseline with a provenance-aware framework. The framework passes each claim with its support status, source, evidence and transmission history. No new evidence is introduced during transmission. We measure changes in claim meaning, unsupported detail accretion, semantic drift, and provenance preservation. These metrics show whether the framework limits unsupported changes as claims pass between agent
sc82989c8f5.summary: Researchers study how unsupported claims change across multi-agent LLM pipelines and test a provenance-aware framework that passes support status and evidence with each claim.
sc82989c8f5.why: Shows provenance metadata may limit unsupported claim drift in multi-agent systems, a reliability concern for agent pipelines.

s84e905a057.title: Beyond Prompt Heuristics: Assessing Child Safety Alignment in LLMs
s84e905a057.description: arXiv:2611.26965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Child-safety taxonomies typically characterize safety risks through a predefined set of harm categories, and existing evaluations largely operationalize these categories using prompts that explicitly invoke them. However, child-safety considerations can also arise in seemingly benign requests that lack recognizable harm-category cues. We therefore investigate how child-safety alignment generalizes to such settings. Across six models, we find considerably higher misalignment rates on requests without recognizable harm-category cues than on those containing such cues (80.0, 54.0, and 48.4 percentage-point gaps for Qwen3.5-27B, GPT-5.4-mini, and Claude-Haiku-4.5, respectively). s84e905a057.summary: A study finds six LLMs show considerably higher child-safety misalignment on benign-seeming requests lacking recognizable harm-category cues than on explicit ones.
s84e905a057.why: Indicates keyword-style safety evaluations may miss child-safety failures, so teams need broader test sets.

s744bf692b6.title: When Perception Collides with Priors: Diagnosing Modal Polarization in Video Understanding Models
s744bf692b6.description: arXiv:2611.26972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong video comprehension, largely benefiting from extensive training on realistic video data. However, when video perception severely conflicts with internal priors or common sense, we identify a critical failure pattern termed Modal Polarization, where models fail to integrate modalities and instead bifurcate into two distinct extremes: Cognitive Inertia, where models rigidly adhere to priors despite contradictory visual evidence, and Perceptual Inertia, where they blindly trust video perception while ignoring logical inconsistencies. To investigate this, we introduce TheaterBench, a benchmark designed to expose Modal Polarization using counter-intuitive scenarios that violate physic
s744bf692b6.summary: Researchers identify "Modal Polarization" in multimodal LLMs, where video models either ignore visual evidence for priors or blindly trust video when they conflict.
s744bf692b6.why: Shows video models can fail by over-trusting either priors or perception, a risk for any system that relies on video understanding.

s892a569d59.title: Contexture: Runtime Context Eviction for High-Throughput Agent Serving
s892a569d59.description: arXiv:2611.26980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents such as Hermes, OpenClaw, and Codex repeatedly resend growing execution histories, increasing shared GPU key-value (KV) cache demand in high-bandwidth memory (HBM). We show that shared KV capacity limits agent-serving throughput. Existing context-reduction methods lack global cache-state visibility, while runtime KV managers lack tool-execution information. Tracing tokens to their originating tool operations reveals that later operations supersede earlier outputs and associated turns, identifying 64% of recorded final-history tokens as removal candidates. We present Contexture, a harness- and model-agnostic architecture for runtime context eviction. Contexture separates the harness's full conversation history from the model's exe
s892a569d59.summary: Contexture proposes runtime context eviction for LLM agent serving, arguing shared GPU KV cache capacity limits agent throughput and that many earlier tool outputs are superseded.
s892a569d59.why: Suggests agent serving throughput can be improved by evicting superseded tool-execution context from GPU KV cache.

se4980fd66e.title: Privacy Protection in Self-Evolving Personal Agents: Persistent Memory and Cross-Carrier Transfer
se4980fd66e.description: arXiv:2611.26983v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personal agents carry private experience into later decisions through persistent memory. This thematic survey compares memory admission, maintenance, release, and withdrawal by protected change, observer, and validation setting. Direct evidence in the screened corpus comes from controlled memory workflows. Three worked scenarios follow one private fact through booking, feedback-driven learning, and withdrawal. We show when prompt revision and memory reads compose, when skills inherit a private head's bound, and why reader non-use does not establish cleanup of learned state. Diagnostic experiments measure the utility costs of wider label protection and broad memory deletion, and test how missing lineage obscures descendants.
se4980fd66e.summary: A thematic survey examines privacy in self-evolving personal agents with persistent memory, covering memory admission, maintenance, release, and withdrawal.
se4980fd66e.why: Highlights privacy risks of persistent agent memory and the need for controlled memory withdrawal in deployed personal agents.

se5eee1065d.title: JevRisk: Zero-Shot Financial Risk Assessment with a Language Decision Model
se5eee1065d.description: arXiv:2611.26999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Banks must monitor every customer's financial risk, such as money laundering and credit default, by interpreting financial activity in the context of the customer's profile. Existing risk monitoring systems of banks are mostly based on expert-designed risk indicators, which apply predefined thresholds to every customer and cannot adapt to their personal situations. Supervised models recognise risk patterns from labelled customers, but each label often needs an expert's review or months of repayment history, which is slow and costly. Financial risk assessment therefore calls for a zero-shot decision system that minimises the need for labels and generalises across customers and risk types. To this end, we present JevRisk, a system for zero-sh
se5eee1065d.summary: JevRisk introduces a zero-shot financial risk assessment approach using a language decision model to monitor bank customers for risks like money laundering and credit default.
se5eee1065d.why: Offers a possible alternative to threshold-based and labelled-data risk monitoring in banking, though the description gives limited evaluation detail.

sc4833a0430.title: FoRe: A Force-Guided Framework for Autonomous Grasp Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Models
sc4833a0430.description: arXiv:2611.27011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong performance in grasp-based manipulation, yet reliable recovery from local grasping failures remains challenging. Specifically, in pick-and-place tasks, policies may continue transport after a failed grasp instead of retrying, potentially reflecting overreliance on proprioceptive cues for stage progression and limited retry supervision. Existing recovery approaches typically rely on deployment-time guidance or demonstration augmentation. We introduce Force-guided Recovery (FoRe), a framework for autonomous recovery from local grasping failures. Using force feedback, FoRe partitions demonstrations into approach-grasp and transport-placement stages to train separate policies. To supp
sc4833a0430.summary: FoRe proposes a force-guided framework enabling vision-language-action robot policies to retry after failed grasps instead of continuing transport.
sc4833a0430.why: Addresses a concrete failure mode in VLA manipulation policies, where robots proceed after a failed grasp instead of retrying.

s42ec6c7924.title: Ruby: State-of-the-Art Potency Prediction across Discovery Regimes Using Learned Structural Representations
s42ec6c7924.description: arXiv:2611.27015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery proceeds through repeated design-make-test-analyze cycles. The goal is often to maximize potency while keeping other properties within the ranges required for a viable therapeutic candidate. Compound prioritization places different demands on computational methods as drug discovery progresses from hit identification through hit-to-lead and lead optimization, with changing computational budgets and increasing amounts of on-target experimental data. We introduce Ruby, a Robust Universal Binding affinitY predictor that uses intermediate representations from the structural foundation model Pearl without requiring an explicit binding pose for every compound. Ruby is trained on proprietary data plus GenesisPotency-20
s42ec6c7924.summary: Ruby is a binding affinity predictor for small-molecule drug discovery, claiming state-of-the-art potency prediction across discovery stages using learned structural representations.

sefbb694449.title: Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced Hierarchy-Aware Semi-Supervised Graph Classification
sefbb694449.description: arXiv:2611.27043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semi-supervised graph classification aims to learn graph-level representations by leveraging a large number of unlabeled graphs alongside a small set of labeled ones, effectively mitigating the issue of label scarcity. Despite significant progress by various semi-supervised learning strategies, complex relationships among graph vertices beyond pairwise edges, especially hierarchical structures, remain underexplored by existing methods. In this work, we propose a Hypergraph Structural Entropy-Enhanced hierarchy-aware framework, namely HypSEE, for semi-supervised graph classification. Specifically, we first construct walk-induced and embedding-derived hypergraphs to capture hierarchy-aware local and long-range higher-order relationships withi
sefbb694449.summary: HypSEE proposes a hypergraph structural entropy-enhanced, hierarchy-aware framework for semi-supervised graph classification.

s6e016613ed.title: Learning 3D MRI Representations with Generative Adversarial Networks
s6e016613ed.description: arXiv:2611.27057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning representations of visual images is a challenging task. It requires extracting abstract patterns from high-dimensional data without explicit supervision. This becomes pronounced with 3D MR imaging due to sparse features, higher dimensional inputs, and smaller datasets. Many state-of-the-art representation learning algorithms successfully rely on transformers and diffusion-based architectures. However, these methods struggle with smaller datasets. In effect, solution methods relax the problem by slicing 3D volumes and solving the problem for 2D medical imaging, resulting in a loss of spatial 3D information. We present R2RG, a representation learning method based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), with Generative Adversarial Ne
s6e016613ed.summary: Researchers propose learning 3D MRI representations with generative adversarial networks, aiming to avoid slicing volumes and to work better on small datasets than transformers or diffusion models.
s6e016613ed.why: Offers an approach for representation learning on small 3D medical imaging datasets where transformer and diffusion methods struggle.

sde8822de29.title: PACE: Policy Augmentation and Compensation With Explicit Disturbance Estimation for Robust Locomotion
sde8822de29.description: arXiv:2611.27061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning has made quadrupedal locomotion remarkably robust. To handle unmodeled dynamics and external disturbances, domain randomization is usually employed to make a policy hedge against every condition it might meet. However, maintaining accurate tracking across varying dynamics and generalizing beyond the sampled range remain challenging. Here we show that explicitly estimating the disturbance and feeding the resulting estimation back into both the policy and the controller can relax this compromise. We introduce Policy Augmentation and Compensation with Explicit disturbance estimation (PACE). The framework lumps payload variations, center-of-mass (CoM) shifts, actuator degradation, and external forces into one joint-space
sde8822de29.summary: PACE explicitly estimates external disturbances and feeds them into both the policy and controller to improve robust quadrupedal locomotion.
sde8822de29.why: Suggests explicit disturbance estimation can reduce the tradeoff of domain randomization in learned robot locomotion controllers.

sa25e27fc12.title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
sa25e27fc12.description: arXiv:2611.27079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate that weight-space programming and edits guided by sparse autoencoders can remove unwanted aspects of a particle-physics foundation model through direct edits to its weights. In a foundation model trained on jets, we observe that adding a single soft neutral particle causes large changes in jet classification, violating infrared safety. We locate the responsible attention heads with mechanistic analysis and trace the flaw's origin to pretraining on datasets with different reconstruction thresholds. sa25e27fc12.summary: Researchers use sparse autoencoders and mechanistic analysis to edit weights of a particle-physics foundation model, fixing an infrared safety violation caused by pretraining data.
sa25e27fc12.why: Demonstrates targeted weight edits and mechanistic interpretability as a way to correct specific flaws in a foundation model.

scd64341212.title: Fooling the Mind Twice: Human Detection of Audiovisual Deepfakes Under Repeated Exposure and Corrective Feedback
scd64341212.description: arXiv:2611.27080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Human deepfake detection remains unreliable, and whether reassessment with corrective feedback improves subsequent judgments remains unclear. This study examined differences between initial and repeated deepfake assessments among 110 participants using audiovisual stimuli from the FakeAVCeleb and Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC) datasets. Participants evaluated 40 videos from each dataset in phase 1 (PhaseI) and reassessed the same videos in phase 2 (PhaseII) under a procedure combining repeated presentation and corrective feedback. For the FakeAVCeleb dataset, the participants' mean accuracy increased by 4.68 percentage points from 63.30 in PhaseI to 67.98 in PhaseII (t(109)=5.61, p<.001, d_z=0.54). A judgment-level logistic regression
scd64341212.summary: A study of 110 participants finds human audiovisual deepfake detection is unreliable and examines whether repeated exposure with corrective feedback improves judgments.
scd64341212.why: Shows humans remain unreliable deepfake detectors, which matters for designing verification workflows that rely on human review.

s94757dab97.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes
s94757dab97.description: arXiv:2611.27090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When an AI coding agent deletes the wrong files or a long agent run crashes, users fall back on recovery mechanisms: resume from a checkpoint, undo, ask for approval, read the log. Research runtimes promise stronger guarantees, such as saga-style compensation and transactional rollback. We ask what public evidence shows about whether either kind works in real use. Under a protocol frozen before data collection, we graded 12 persistent agent runtimes, 26 coding-agent harnesses and 12 research runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, from not found to exercised in a real run, with two blind coding passes, adjudication and re-verification against archived sources. Recovery is exercised almost everywhere in practice: 11 of 12 runtimes and 25 of 2
s94757dab97.summary: A study grades 50 AI agent harnesses and runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, based on public reports about how agents recover from wrong deletions or crashes.
s94757dab97.why: Suggests recovery mechanisms like checkpoints and rollback are rarely evident in real agent tools, a concern for anyone running coding agents.

s906d302ef4.title: Separating Automation Gains from Agent Contributions in AI-Assisted Model Validation
s906d302ef4.description: arXiv:2611.27094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents are being proposed for bank model validation, yet evaluations that compare agent-assisted work with manual practice credit the agent with gains that come from digitized evidence and deterministic tests. We propose a staged architecture in which an LLM-free controlled workflow (P1) is both the fallback and the control arm for individually authorized agent tasks (P2), and an attribution protocol that credits an agent only for faults P1 does not already report. The protocol charges decoy false alarms, unnecessary actions and endorsed developer assertions, counts invalid outputs as misses, folds newly automatable findings back into P1 with discovery credit, and fixes safety bounds and a break-even cost gate in advance. On a synthetic
s906d302ef4.summary: A paper proposes an attribution protocol for LLM agents in bank model validation that credits agents only for faults a deterministic LLM-free workflow does not already find.
s906d302ef4.why: Offers a method to measure true agent contribution versus gains from automation in regulated model validation workflows.

s6d4a57c91a.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
s6d4a57c91a.description: arXiv:2611.27095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard
s6d4a57c91a.summary: Epistemic Guard proposes runtime verification for MCP tool-using agents, addressing action fabrication, provenance collapse in memory, and syndicated echo amplification.
s6d4a57c91a.why: Targets concrete runtime gaps in MCP agents, such as prose narrating failed side effects and unverified content entering durable memory.

se05939eff2.title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology
se05939eff2.description: arXiv:2611.27102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A synoptic pathology report is a checklist of questions with fixed answer sets, many composed from others. Pathology foundation models answer them accurately with one classifier trained with labels for each, and frontier language models, which compose freely, cannot fit a slide of fourteen thousand tiles in their context. On 189 breast report questions, frontier models that read a written description of the slide or look at a thumbnail and tiles of it answer at 0.50 to 0.66, below the majority class at 0.67. A description is written before the question is known, and a look covers a handful of tiles. se05939eff2.summary: Opsis pairs a frontier model with typed pathology classifiers, reporting that frontier models reading slide descriptions or thumbnails underperform the majority-class baseline on 189 breast report questions.
se05939eff2.why: Shows frontier models alone underperform on structured pathology questions, pointing to hybrid designs that combine specialist classifiers with LLMs.

s43ae79ddd3.title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations
s43ae79ddd3.description: arXiv:2611.27106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to extract records, generate SQL, summarize reports, answer policy questions, and route operational work. At these software boundaries, parseable output is necessary but does not establish task correctness. We present a reproducible benchmark protocol, a public executable artifact, and a confirmatory live API evaluation that separate structural validity from task-specific correctness across five business workflow tasks and six Python implementation conditions: PydanticAI, LangGraph, DSPy, CrewAI, Agno, and a framework-free SDK reference. We hypothesize that (H1) schema validity and task quality are separable, (H2) structured-output binding paths are heterogeneous under a shared model and lowest-co
s43ae79ddd3.summary: A paper proposes a reproducible benchmark protocol and public artifact comparing six Python LLM workflow frameworks on schema-valid output and task correctness across five business tasks.
s43ae79ddd3.why: It separates structurally valid LLM output from correct results, helping teams choose frameworks and test LLM outputs at software boundaries.

scc0dedbb4f.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
scc0dedbb4f.description: arXiv:2611.27139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly divide long tasks among subagents whose reports a senior agent turns into the final answer. Such a division of labor pays off only if each agent, and above all the senior agent, carries out the duties of its role. Current evaluations, however, mostly score the final answer, and a fluent, well-cited answer cannot show whether the senior agent weighed its subagents' reports or merely aggregated them. To assess whether a senior agent meets its assigned responsibilities, we define role integrity as the preservation of an agent's functional responsibilities when it acts on its subordinates' material. scc0dedbb4f.summary: Researchers define role integrity and propose measuring whether senior LLM agents truly weigh subordinate agents' reports rather than merely aggregating them.
scc0dedbb4f.why: Final-answer scores can hide whether a multi-agent orchestrator actually does its job, so teams need process-level evaluation.

sa1d86b49f0.title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer
sa1d86b49f0.description: arXiv:2611.27142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Promptable segmentation foundation models are increasingly used in specialized domains, but it remains unclear how SAM-3 should be fine-tuned when adapting it beyond its original training distribution. We study this question by comparing five adaptation families --LoRA, HiRA, KRAdapter, QuanTA, and Full Fine-Tuning-- across five segmentation datasets spanning medical imaging, remote sensing, and dense material segmentation. Across these datasets, compact parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods often match or approach Full Fine-Tuning in DSC and IoU, suggesting that strong in-domain adaptation does not always require updating the full model. However, this performance cannot be explained by nominal adapter rank or trainable parameter count al
sa1d86b49f0.summary: A study compares five fine-tuning methods for adapting SAM-3 segmentation to medical imaging, remote sensing, and material segmentation datasets.
sa1d86b49f0.why: Parameter-efficient methods often approach full fine-tuning here, suggesting cheaper adaptation options for specialized vision domains.

sd7549dbebf.title: Structure Over Scale: Rethinking Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
sd7549dbebf.description: arXiv:2611.27148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is often framed as a choice between the expressivity of Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) and the efficiency of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). We find that this framing misses an important variable: the geometry of the update. Under a common cold-start GRPO protocol, LoRA exhibits rank collapse: performance remains broadly stable at low rank, then fails abruptly as rank increases. On DeepMath-Hard, for example, accuracy drops from 73.1% at r=64 to 4.7% at r=128. In contrast, Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) and Quantum-Informed Tensor Adaptation (QuanTA) remain stable over a wider tested optimization region and are competitive with FFT while updating less than 0.6% of the model parameters.
sd7549dbebf.summary: Researchers report that LoRA suffers rank collapse under GRPO reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, while a weight-decomposed variant avoids the failure.
sd7549dbebf.why: Adapter rank choice can abruptly break RL fine-tuning, so teams using LoRA for RLVR should validate rank settings carefully.

s9be6c68a69.title: Co-Evolving Behavioral Agents and Detectors for Adaptive Information Operations
s9be6c68a69.description: arXiv:2611.27156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Detectors of state-sponsored information operations (IOs) are trained on campaigns that platforms have already taken down. They lose much of their accuracy on an actor they have not seen, even though no operator in the archived data is trying to avoid them. A real operator wants two things, to reach an audience and to avoid being caught. We present IO-AI, a framework that gives simulated agents these two capabilities, engagement and evasion, and tests what each one does to detection. The agents are built from the posting behavior of real campaigns and choose the emotion, type, and timing of each post. An agent and a detector then train against each other in turn. We rank the trained agents by how hard they are to detect and train one detect
s9be6c68a69.summary: IO-AI is a framework that gives simulated information-operation agents engagement and evasion capabilities to test how these affect detector accuracy.
s9be6c68a69.why: It offers a way to stress-test detectors against adaptive adversaries rather than only archived, already-removed campaigns.

s253a177be9.title: Felid: A Flexible and Efficient Design for Transformer Fine-Tuning over Encrypted Data
s253a177be9.description: arXiv:2611.27175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables non-interactive, privacy-preserving transformer fine-tuning, protecting highly sensitive data as inputs to large language models. Prior work has predominantly pursued efficiency gains through architectural refinements, yet overall performance remains bounded by the substantial cost inherent in encrypted computation. To address these issues, we target the bottleneck at the ciphertext operation level. Concretely, we propose a novel packing strategy that supports batching over a flexible number of inputs, making it well-suited for fine-tuning workloads. s253a177be9.summary: Felid proposes a new ciphertext packing strategy to speed up transformer fine-tuning over fully homomorphic encrypted data.
s253a177be9.why: Lowering encrypted computation cost could make privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning on sensitive data more practical.

s673e102a3c.title: GEG-SAM: Gaze Exploration-Guided Segment Anything Model for Weakly Supervised Polyp Segmentation
s673e102a3c.description: arXiv:2611.27183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Endoscopist gaze offers an unobtrusively acquired record of lesion-oriented visual exploration during routine clinical inspection, providing relevant supervision for tasks. However, existing methods treat fixations as isolated spatial prompts directly associated with the target, overlooking the fact that natural gaze records a continuous visual search process in which fixations are temporally connected, spatially organized, and coupled with the visual content. Interpreting each fixation independently based only on its local visual content overlooks the temporal evolution and spatial organization of the gaze trajectory, whereas modeling relations among fixations alone cannot reveal the visual semantics of the regions they attend to. To this
s673e102a3c.summary: GEG-SAM uses temporally connected endoscopist gaze fixations to guide the Segment Anything Model for weakly supervised polyp segmentation.

s83325b18b5.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI
s83325b18b5.description: arXiv:2611.27189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: India's AI debate often swings between two insufficient options: replicating the compute-intensive, capital-heavy foundation-model programmes of the United States or China, or remaining a downstream adopter of foreign AI with localised interfaces and safeguards. Neither serves a country that must deliver AI to a very large, diverse population across uneven infrastructure and within constrained budgets. This white paper from the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI), IIT Madras, proposes a third path: Responsible Frugal AI, which applies principle-based frugal engineering alongside Responsible AI. s83325b18b5.summary: An IIT Madras CeRAI white paper proposes Responsible Frugal AI as a third path for India, favoring right-sized AI over replicating large foundation-model programmes.
s83325b18b5.why: It offers a policy and design perspective on building AI under tight compute and budget constraints for large, diverse populations.

s61299b2edb.title: DepthMSA: Combinatorial Training and Budget-Aware Depth Allocation for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
s61299b2edb.description: arXiv:2611.27198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State-of-the-art multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) models rely on large pretrained encoders, yet typically process every modality to its full depth, regardless of its computational cost or predictive contribution. This raises a fundamental question: how should limited computation be allocated across modalities to preserve predictive performance? We reveal a substantial mismatch between the computational cost of modality encoders and the predictive benefit of processing them more deeply, suggesting that different modalities require different encoding depths. s61299b2edb.summary: DepthMSA proposes combinatorial training and budget-aware depth allocation so multimodal sentiment models process each modality to different depths.
s61299b2edb.why: Allocating compute per modality by predictive benefit could cut inference cost in multimodal models without losing accuracy.

s7ee87e7987.title: LingSante-Pulse: Unified Physiological Pretraining through Random-Feature Prediction and Cross-Modal Alignment
s7ee87e7987.description: arXiv:2611.27206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical monitoring and wearable devices capture complementary physiological signals, but their partially overlapping modality coverage makes within-signal information and cross-modal relationships difficult to exploit jointly. We introduce LingSante-Pulse, a unified, general-purpose and flexible physiological representation framework that learns from these heterogeneous recordings. A shared, signal-conditioned encoder processes each physical channel independently and supports different numbers and combinations of signals for multimodal assessment and single-sensor inference. s7ee87e7987.summary: LingSante-Pulse is a unified physiological representation framework that pretrains a shared encoder on heterogeneous clinical and wearable signals.

sbcf622f91e.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Qwen3-VL for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
sbcf622f91e.description: arXiv:2611.27208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Handwritten mathematical expression recognition (HMER) requires joint recovery of symbol identity and two-dimensional syntax, so a locally plausible transcription may still be structurally wrong. We study whether a compact vision-language model can be adapted to generate linearized Symbol Label Graphs (SLGs) under limited computing resources. Starting from a 4-bit Qwen3-VL-4B checkpoint, we apply rank-16 Low-Rank Adaptation to the vision, language, attention, and MLP modules and train with instruction-formatted CROHME 2019 examples. sbcf622f91e.why: It shows a compact vision-language model can be adapted to structured recognition tasks under limited compute.

s0263b6cc99.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
s0263b6cc99.description: arXiv:2611.27211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user's patterns, quoted evidence, and habits to avoid, then drafts from the user's samples and revises the draft twice against this profile, guided by its own style scores. s0263b6cc99.summary: StylePrism defines 28 stylistic aspects and SP-Refine makes style extraction an explicit inference-time step for personalized long-form text generation.
s0263b6cc99.why: Explicit style extraction offers an alternative to leaving retrieved user texts for the model to interpret implicitly.

s74af93fbd3.title: EAF-TTS: Rethinking Codec-Latent Coordinates for Flow TTS
s74af93fbd3.description: arXiv:2611.27214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent text-to-speech (TTS) systems generate codec latents decoded by a frozen decoder, but good reconstruction does not ensure geometry suitable for Flow generation from isotropic Gaussian noise. s74af93fbd3.summary: EAF-TTS adapts codec latents for flow-based text-to-speech, adding a fixed ZCA interface estimated from training data without learned parameters.

s4b07141410.title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard
s4b07141410.description: arXiv:2611.27215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Commercial detectors of AI-generated audio are usually promoted with results on internal test sets that buyers cannot inspect. Independent benchmarks with private labels give a more reliable comparison. We report the results of Neural Defend's ARCAS foundation models on the Podonos audio deepfake detection benchmark, an independent leaderboard that scores commercial detection APIs and open-source detectors on one held-out set of real speech and speech from current text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems, delivered in six file formats, against labels that only Podonos holds.
