s4b07141410.summary: Neural Defend reports its ARCAS models ranked first on the independent Podonos audio deepfake detection leaderboard against commercial and open-source detectors.
s4b07141410.why: Independent, privately labeled benchmarks offer a more reliable comparison than vendor-internal test results for detection tools.

s35e015cb88.title: Correct Precedents Induce Policy Violations in On-Device LLM Agents
s35e015cb88.description: arXiv:2611.27216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local-cloud agent systems pair a cloud model with a small on-device agent that acts on private data, often as the last check before an irreversible action. We identify, for the first time, a failure in which such an agent is led into a violation by its own correct decisions within a session. After it correctly releases an item whose restriction was lifted, it becomes more likely to release the next item that is still restricted. Because the trigger is a correct decision, a history with no faulty step can still end in a violation. We call this failure correct-precedent generalization and find it in 13 open-weight models from nine developers. A single correct precedent can cut the safe rate of the most affected agent roughly in half, and the
s35e015cb88.summary: Researchers identify a failure where an on-device LLM agent's earlier correct release decisions make it more likely to release a later restricted item, causing violations.
s35e015cb88.why: Local-cloud agents acting as final checks can violate policy even with no faulty steps, so session-level safeguards are needed before irreversible actions.

s0e8705ea4a.title: NavTTT: Adaptive Parametric Memory via Hierarchical Test-Time Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation
s0e8705ea4a.description: arXiv:2611.27219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) demands that agents accumulate and reason over streaming visual observations throughout long navigation episodes. Existing approaches struggle to maintain long-term history, constrained by the finite context capacity of transformer architectures. To solve the problem, fast-weight test-time training (TTT) provides a mechanism for encoding streaming observations into an evolving parameter state. However, existing TTT does not distinguish informative observations from repetitive visual content, allowing redundant tokens to interfere with the retention of information needed for subsequent decisions. We propose Navigation-Conditioned Test-Time Training (NavTTT), which introduces adaptive memory formation and
s0e8705ea4a.summary: Researchers propose NavTTT, a hierarchical test-time training method that gives vision-and-language navigation agents adaptive parametric memory over long streaming observations.
s0e8705ea4a.why: It targets the finite context limit of transformers for long-horizon embodied agents, a practical bottleneck for navigation systems.

s207cc22d6a.title: CreditFilter: Calibrated Token Weights over the Within-Response Entropy Rank for RLVR
s207cc22d6a.description: arXiv:2611.27227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Critic-free reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically assigns a uniform advantage to every token. Token-reweighting heuristics like the 80/20 mask favor high-entropy tokens, but fail to measure a token's actual impact on the outcome. We formalize this impact as the forking value: the variance of the success probability over the policy's next-token choices. s207cc22d6a.summary: Researchers introduce CreditFilter, which assigns calibrated per-token weights based on a forking value measuring each token's actual impact on outcome in RLVR training.
s207cc22d6a.why: It offers a principled alternative to entropy-based token reweighting heuristics when post-training LLMs with verifiable rewards.

sba03b3f0d6.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
sba03b3f0d6.description: arXiv:2611.27253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite the proliferation of proactive defenses against deepfakes, the lack of a unified evaluation protocol precludes fair comparison and masks critical vulnerabilities. To bridge this gap, we present the first comprehensive benchmark that systematically assesses disruption, robustness, and transferability encompassing pixel, perceptual, and identity metrics. Our extensive analysis reveals that fidelity and identity metrics capture orthogonal performance axes, often leading to conflicting interpretations when relied upon individually. Furthermore, we identify a fundamental trade-off where peak white-box performance signals overfitting, and we introduce a calibrated evaluation to correct generator-induced identity bias. sba03b3f0d6.summary: Researchers present the first unified benchmark for evaluating proactive defenses against deepfake generation across disruption, robustness, and transferability.
sba03b3f0d6.why: It shows fidelity and identity metrics can conflict, so teams evaluating deepfake defenses should not rely on one metric alone.

s50b2bd1a5e.title: EAGLE: Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding
s50b2bd1a5e.description: arXiv:2611.27264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) still struggle with fine-grained understanding of high-resolution images: attention heads vary in their reliability for grounding target entities and their attributes, while localized details are often disconnected from the broader scene context. We propose EAGLE (Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding), a plug-in framework that jointly selects grounding signals and organizes hierarchical visual evidence. EAGLE employs a fine-grained dataset to screen visually-grounded attention heads, followed by entity-aware grounding to extract target-specific regions. s50b2bd1a5e.summary: Researchers propose EAGLE, a plug-in framework that improves multimodal LLMs' grounding of entities in high-resolution images by selecting reliable signals and layering visual evidence.
s50b2bd1a5e.why: It addresses fine-grained high-resolution image understanding, a known weakness of current multimodal models.

s8fb84deae6.title: Preserving Pretrained CFG Structure in RL for Diffusion Models with Conditional Contrast Regularization
s8fb84deae6.description: arXiv:2611.27288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has become an important component in the post-training of diffusion models. In practice, however, standard RL often improves the target reward without reliably preserving holistic generation quality, leading to unstable reward-quality trade-offs that we view as a form of reward hacking. Since Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is known to improve visual clarity, prompt alignment, and perceptual quality in generation, we investigate whether its underlying structure can serve as a useful prior during RL. s8fb84deae6.summary: Researchers propose conditional contrast regularization to preserve pretrained classifier-free guidance structure during reinforcement learning post-training of diffusion models.
s8fb84deae6.why: It aims to stop reward gains from degrading overall generation quality, a reward-hacking failure mode in diffusion RL.

s7cedc9f283.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
s7cedc9f283.description: arXiv:2611.27290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. s7cedc9f283.summary: Researchers present EgoLAM, which learns latent actions from egocentric video by supervising with measured wrist motion and modeling camera motion separately.
s7cedc9f283.why: Separating hand motion from head motion could improve robot policies learned from human video demonstrations.

s659f780bc0.title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
s659f780bc0.description: arXiv:2611.27302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general visual tasks, yet their ability to understand mathematical images remains limited. This paper investigates whether explicit reasoning and textual image descriptions can enhance VLMs' performance on binary yes/no visual mathematical questions. To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy
s659f780bc0.summary: Researchers study whether chain-of-thought reasoning and textual image descriptions improve open-source vision-language models on yes/no visual math questions.
s659f780bc0.why: It gives evidence on when prompting and description aids help VLMs with mathematical images, though the summary offers limited detail on results.

sfa59326541.title: A Framework for AI-Ready Data in Earth and Environmental Science
sfa59326541.description: arXiv:2611.27313v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), specifically machine learning (ML), is increasingly integral to Earth and environmental research, yet the suitability of current research data infrastructures for supporting AI workflows remains poorly defined. While the FAIR principles provide a foundation for scientific data management, they do not explicitly address several requirements arising when datasets are used for training, evaluating, and deploying AI models. This article presents a practically motivated framework for assessing and improving AI-readiness of research data within distributed Earth and environmental data infrastructures. The framework was developed through a structured, community-driven process, beginning with a review of existing liter
sfa59326541.summary: Researchers present a framework for assessing and improving the AI-readiness of Earth and environmental science datasets, extending FAIR principles to training and deployment needs.
sfa59326541.why: Teams building ML pipelines on scientific data can use it to check whether datasets meet training and evaluation requirements.

s5e8196d15f.title: Do Language Models Know Which Words Steer Their Reasoning?
s5e8196d15f.description: arXiv:2611.27317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits intermediate reasoning steps from language models, it is unclear which words in the context actually steer the CoT. We identify Phantom Context Influence (PCI): language models are disproportionately steered by semantically irrelevant context words, even as the same models deny those words' relevance when asked. To localize PCI, we introduce Leave-One-Out Word JSD analysis, which removes one context word at a time from the otherwise intact context to isolate its marginal effect on the next-token distribution; words whose removal flips the prediction (pivot words) are passed to the same LLM to self-judge whether it recognizes this predictive dependence. s5e8196d15f.summary: Researchers identify Phantom Context Influence, where language models are steered by semantically irrelevant context words and deny their relevance when asked.
s5e8196d15f.why: Irrelevant prompt content can silently skew reasoning, which matters for reliability and auditing of LLM applications.

s43df8b8d1d.title: Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes
s43df8b8d1d.description: arXiv:2611.27326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) but incurs high inference costs due to lengthy autoregressive decoding. While previous efficiency approaches reduce costs by discarding tokens or utilizing continuous latent representations, these lossy methods fundamentally sacrifice interpretability and auditability. In this work, we introduce a novel compression framework for intermediate reasoning. We apply Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) to reasoning corpora to learn a compressed vocabulary of Private Use Area (PUA) tokens, each representing frequent semantic spans. s43df8b8d1d.summary: Researchers propose a compression framework that applies Byte-Pair Encoding to reasoning corpora to shorten chain-of-thought traces while keeping them interpretable.
s43df8b8d1d.why: Shorter reasoning traces could cut inference costs without the lossy trade-offs of discarding tokens or using latent representations.

sd2b85a4b68.title: Unimodal Shortcuts and Joint Scene-Intent Dependence in Vision-Language Safety Representations
sd2b85a4b68.description: arXiv:2611.27339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The safety of a request to a vision-language model often depends on the image: asking how to serve a dish is harmless for fresh food and harmful for spoiled food. High accuracy on situational safety benchmarks does not tell us whether a model's safety representation encodes both the scene and the user's intent, because a benchmark can often be solved from one modality alone. Studying frozen vision-language safety representations, we audit five public situational benchmarks and find that each admits a unimodal shortcut: images alone predict the labels, and on same-image prompt pairs a probe that never sees the photograph reaches 0.9645 AUROC. sd2b85a4b68.summary: Researchers audit five public vision-language safety benchmarks and find each admits a unimodal shortcut, so high scores may not reflect joint scene-intent understanding.
sd2b85a4b68.why: Benchmark scores can overstate a model's safety reasoning, so teams should check for single-modality shortcuts before trusting results.

see744d37e7.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
see744d37e7.description: arXiv:2611.27344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. see744d37e7.summary: Researchers introduce motion-region guidance to make robotic action-conditioned video world models focus on interaction-relevant regions rather than global reconstruction error.
see744d37e7.why: Better local interaction fidelity could make video world models more useful for robot policy evaluation and simulation.

s9da4b7ef1a.title: PAVE: A Harness for Geometrically Consistent Road Network Modeling with Vision-Language Models
s9da4b7ef1a.description: arXiv:2611.27352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transportation models, whether they simulate traffic or support planning, are only as reliable as the road networks they run on, down to the lanes and turns at each intersection. Practitioners still take such a network from GIS files and supply its junction and movement data by hand, a task that recurs with each new base year and design alternative, or they generate it from open map data. OpenStreetMap's lane tags give the correct layout for only 13 of the 44 approaches we test; open map data are often incomplete or inaccurate. Satellite and street-level imagery, in contrast, cover all 44 and show their lanes as painted. s9da4b7ef1a.summary: Researchers present PAVE, a harness using vision-language models to build geometrically consistent road network models, reporting OpenStreetMap lane tags correct for only 13 of 44 approaches tested.
s9da4b7ef1a.why: Transportation teams spend significant manual effort building road networks, and automated, consistent alternatives could reduce that work.

s01872c4203.title: WaXup: Weight Averaging of Experts as Data Augmentation for Robust Introspection
s01872c4203.description: arXiv:2611.27353v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As the capabilities of large language models keep improving, traditional mechanistic interpretability methods struggle to keep pace. In contrast, trainable introspection methods emerge as a promising alternative; they repurpose the model itself as a self-diagnostic tool, trained to verbalize what it has learned during finetuning in natural language. While training on datasets of finetuned experts achieves encouraging results, it currently lacks robustness and generalization. s01872c4203.summary: Researchers introduce WaXup, which applies weight averaging of finetuned experts as data augmentation to make trainable LLM introspection methods more robust.
s01872c4203.why: More robust introspection could offer a practical self-diagnostic tool for understanding what finetuning taught a model.

s19fc8427b0.title: Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
s19fc8427b0.description: arXiv:2611.27368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep parallel cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (CMARL)} trains multiple agents that all act at every time step to optimize a common objective. Like single-agent RL, CMARL can produce unsafe behaviors that violate implicit safety requirements not captured by the reward, and these behaviors are hard to explain. However, testing CMARL policies for safety has received less attention than the safety testing of single-agent RL policies. In this paper, we propose DisQ, a test case selection method that identifies failure-revealing states in value-based CMARL by exploiting a signal specific to trained Q-learning agents. s19fc8427b0.summary: Researchers propose DisQ, a test case selection method that finds failure-revealing states to test cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning policies for safety violations.
s19fc8427b0.why: Multi-agent RL policies can violate safety requirements not captured by reward, and DisQ offers a way to surface those failures.

sbe4691731e.title: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding
sbe4691731e.description: arXiv:2611.27381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-video question answering requires retrieving and integrating relevant evidence from videos spanning hours or even days. Recent agentic approaches organize video information into external memories and iteratively retrieve evidence to answer questions. However, effective retrieval and reasoning remain challenging, as agents must determine what information to search for, which memory sources to access, and how to connect evidence across distant temporal intervals. sbe4691731e.why: Shows an agentic memory-and-retrieval pattern for reasoning over hours-long video, relevant to teams building long-context multimodal systems.

sdce75dc3d0.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild
sdce75dc3d0.description: arXiv:2611.27383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing UAV tracking benchmarks predominantly rely on perspective cameras with limited fields of view. Omnidirectional cameras enable full-spherical observation, yet tracking from moving UAV platforms remains largely unexplored. Unlike ground-level panoramic tracking, UAV-mounted omnidirectional cameras observe targets across both azimuth and elevation, introducing geometric challenges under equirectangular projection (ERP). To investigate this setting, we capture approximately \textbf{40 hours of real-world 8K panoramic UAV video} and construct \textbf{PanoUAV-Track} through temporal clip extraction, target annotation, and the integration of simulated sequences. sdce75dc3d0.summary: Researchers present PanoUAV-Track, a benchmark of about 40 hours of 8K panoramic drone video for full-spherical visual object tracking from moving UAVs.
sdce75dc3d0.why: Provides a new benchmark for omnidirectional drone tracking, highlighting equirectangular projection challenges that standard perspective-camera benchmarks miss.

sdbc6e8f8b8.title: Taking Apart and Putting Together: Tracking Objects Through Physical Transformations
sdbc6e8f8b8.description: arXiv:2611.27398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending video object tracking to environments where objects undergo physical assemblies and disassemblies. TTU requires continuously tracking objects through transformations, identifying new entities, maintaining a state graph of their relationships, and assigning semantic labels to transformations. While foundation models (e.g., SAM 2/3) maintain tracklets through appearance changes, they cannot update semantic identities as objects physically evolve. sdbc6e8f8b8.summary: Researchers introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending object tracking to objects that physically assemble and disassemble, maintaining a state graph of relationships.
sdbc6e8f8b8.why: Current foundation trackers like SAM 2/3 cannot update semantic identities as objects change physically, a gap relevant to robotics and video perception work.

s382af47d8c.title: Detecting Word-Substitution Poisoning of a RAG Knowledge Base with Relative Entropy and Runtime Verification
s382af47d8c.description: arXiv:2611.27410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system answers questions using passages it retrieves from a knowledge base, so users must trust that knowledge base. We study an attacker who quietly edits existing passages by swapping words for synonyms (PWWS, TextFooler) in a cybersecurity RAG system built from MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC. s382af47d8c.summary: Researchers show synonym-swap poisoning of a RAG knowledge base lowers answer correctness from 0.714 to 0.555 and study detection using relative entropy and runtime verification.
s382af47d8c.why: Demonstrates a subtle data-integrity threat to RAG systems and a detection approach teams can evaluate for knowledge base monitoring.

sa89348b2dc.title: ADEPT: Adaptive Monocular Depth Estimation via Model-In-The-Loop Photometric Tuning with Capture Risk Prediction
sa89348b2dc.description: arXiv:2611.27423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exposure and gain determine the visual evidence available to monocular depth estimation (MDE), particularly when robot motion creates a tradeoff between light collection and motion blur. We present ADEPT, a framework that adapts these settings using learned feedback from a frozen depth model. During training, ground-truth depth identifies the lowest-error reference within a group of physically evaluated camera settings. sa89348b2dc.summary: ADEPT adapts camera exposure and gain for monocular depth estimation using feedback from a frozen depth model and a learned capture-risk predictor.
sa89348b2dc.why: Offers a method to tune camera settings for depth estimation on robots, trading light collection against motion blur.

sabb9f28457.title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
sabb9f28457.description: arXiv:2611.27425v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can reason directly about the weights of other neural networks. Given only a natural-language objective, an LLM can inspect a model's weights, understand what they compute, and edit them directly without gradient-based optimization. This capability, termed weight-space programming (WSP), has been used to improve model performance on math reasoning, medical QA and other benchmarks. sabb9f28457.summary: TrojanMaxxing proposes backdooring vision-language models by using an LLM to directly edit model weights from a natural-language objective, without gradient-based optimization.
sabb9f28457.why: Shows weight-space programming can be misused to implant backdoors in VLMs, a supply-chain security concern for teams deploying third-party models.

s64bfada739.title: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs
s64bfada739.description: arXiv:2611.27426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely downloaded for their strong coding and reasoning capabilities and deployed locally beyond the provider's control. Based on this insight, we propose Cleave, a training-free attack that directly edits these weights to remove safety restrictions while preserving general capabilities. s64bfada739.summary: Cleave is a training-free attack that edits residual writing weights in open-weight LLMs to remove safety guardrails while preserving general capabilities.
s64bfada739.why: Shows safety refusals in open-weight models can be stripped via weight edits, so teams relying on embedded guardrails for local deployments face real risk.

s1c89671c16.title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning
s1c89671c16.description: arXiv:2611.27427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and heterogeneous, often incomplete multimodal observations. Existing multimodal models can integrate imaging and clinical measurements but often overlook disease-specific evidence patterns and pairwise relations among competing diagnoses. We therefore propose Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning (KnowSR), which aligns multimodal patient representations with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes, signed evidence directions, and pairwise diagnostic relations. s1c89671c16.summary: KnowSR aligns multimodal patient data with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes to improve differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders.

s4cfcc90159.title: No Audio, No Transcripts, No Problem: LLM-based ASR Adaptation Using Only Domain Documents
s4cfcc90159.description: arXiv:2611.27434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a speech recognizer be adapted to a new domain with no target audio and no transcripts, using only written documentation? This is the realistic onboarding setting: a new customer hands over raw documentation, not the transcripts that text-only adaptation normally assumes. s4cfcc90159.why: Suggests a low-cost onboarding path for domain-specific ASR when a customer provides only documentation rather than recordings.

s91303d70a2.title: THRIFTY: Cost-Constrained Reasoning-Data Synthesis for Small Language Models
s91303d70a2.description: arXiv:2611.27436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for efficient, specialized deployment, and are typically trained on reasoning trajectories distilled from a larger teacher LLM. Generating this synthetic data is a major cost of the pipeline, especially when the teacher is a frontier model. s91303d70a2.why: Targets the major cost of distilling reasoning trajectories from frontier teachers, relevant to teams training small models on a budget.

s83ab0639ce.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents
s83ab0639ce.description: arXiv:2611.27443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for cheap, high-throughput agentic deployment, but they remain weak at multi-step reasoning and tool use that long-horizon tasks demand. s83ab0639ce.summary: Researchers post-train small language models to seek advice from a stronger advisor model and act on it, addressing weak multi-step reasoning and tool use in SLM agents.
s83ab0639ce.why: Offers a post-training recipe for advisor-executor agent patterns that could make cheap small-model agents more reliable.

s92251e20bc.title: Mechanism Parity for Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous-Driving Perception
s92251e20bc.description: arXiv:2611.27447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulation is central to intelligent-vehicle validation, but visual realism or output agreement between a real scene and its synthetic counterpart does not prove that a perception system used the same evidence in both domains. s92251e20bc.why: Visual realism alone does not show a perception model relies on the same evidence in simulation, a key validity concern for AV testing pipelines.

s4049585b08.title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act
s4049585b08.description: arXiv:2611.27462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) imposes detailed obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems but offers limited operational guidance, particularly when these systems integrate third-party General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models. This paper introduces a toolkit that fosters the development of legal-by-design AI-assisted recruitment systems by translating the core legal obligations of the AI Act's conformity assessment---specifically Articles 9--15 and Annex IV---into techno-normative requirements and corresponding guiding questions. While recruitment pipelines may involve components with varying technical complexity and differing levels of algorithmic transparency, this paper focuses on the most challenging case: the integration of
s4049585b08.summary: The paper presents a toolkit translating EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems (Articles 9–15, Annex IV) into technical requirements and guiding questions for AI recruitment tools using LLMs.
s4049585b08.why: Gives engineering teams building LLM-based hiring tools concrete compliance questions to design against AI Act conformity requirements.

sa3e723e504.title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition
sa3e723e504.description: arXiv:2611.27465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing an editable music score requires musical events, sung text and the instructions that organise them on the page. Existing recognition targets often omit part of this information, while direct MusicXML prediction repeats substantial structural markup. We introduce Cecilia, a compact representation of canonicalised MusicXML that retains musical content, lyric attachments and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts this representation through metadata and measure-bounded music segments from shared visual memory. A learned count head determines the number of output segments. Across paired complete scores under a common tokeniser, the ratio of mean MusicXML to Cecilia sequence lengths is 27.73. Cecilia-OMR outperforms Legato 2 on
sa3e723e504.summary: Cecilia introduces a compact representation of MusicXML retaining musical content, lyrics, and layout, and a model that predicts it for optical music recognition.

s18975e3f59.title: ROSWORLD: When Digital Task Competence Meets Physical Execution
s18975e3f59.description: arXiv:2611.27467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computer-use agents now solve most desktop tasks through direct software input, but a robot using the same computer must turn GUI knowledge into physical contact with a keyboard and mouse. We introduce ROSWorld, a benchmark that couples a physically simulated robot workstation to a live OSWorld desktop, so that a robot and a desktop agent pursue the same goals under the same official evaluators. The evaluated model receives observations only from the workstation camera views and operates the peripherals through either a single-arm rigid probe or dual-arm dexterous hands. Across five frontier models and 40 tasks in ten applications, models that complete 31-39 tasks on the desktop complete at most 23 with the probe and 28 with the hands. Pair
s18975e3f59.summary: ROSWorld couples a physically simulated robot workstation to a live OSWorld desktop so a robot and a desktop agent pursue the same tasks under official evaluators.
s18975e3f59.why: Benchmarks whether GUI competence transfers to physical keyboard and mouse execution by robots, relevant to embodied computer-use agents.

s5300ba10ae.title: Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining
s5300ba10ae.description: arXiv:2611.27491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tokenization represents one of the most crucial steps in mulilingual NLP pipelines. Yet, tokenizers routinely under-allocate vocabulary to low-resource languages. While improved allocation leads to better performance, it remains poorly understood how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations and transfer during pretraining. To address this, we pretrain 39 mono- and bilingual 1B decoder-only models on FineWeb2-HQ across English, German, French, Arabic and Chinese, varying only the tokenizer. Our results demonstrate that improved vocabulary allocation (i) substantially raises cross-lingual representation alignment in early-to-mid layers, an effect that prior work measuring only the output layer could not observe, (ii) increases cross-
s5300ba10ae.summary: Researchers pretrained 39 mono- and bilingual 1B models across five languages, varying only the tokenizer, to study how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations.
s5300ba10ae.why: Shows tokenizer vocabulary allocation affects cross-lingual transfer, a design choice engineers building multilingual models should weigh.

s8eb1efdcaf.title: Learning Unknown Oscillators From Bandit Feedback
s8eb1efdcaf.description: arXiv:2611.27492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study semi-bandits driven by unknown oscillators. Each round, a learner selects two of four reward channels and observes their individual rewards. Frequency errors change future reward rankings and the resulting measurements. We show when committing to one fitted oscillator lets its greedy choices expose prediction errors. Our controller bounds reward loss (regret) over a continuous confidence set and holds the longest block within budget. An online regression policy gathers observations when the check fails. Regret grows at a square-root rate, up to logarithmic factors, across all frequencies and extends to two competing oscillators. On 96 fresh synthetic instances, checked commitment uses 49 fits instead of 1,023, with 1.5% higher mean
s8eb1efdcaf.summary: The paper studies semi-bandit learning with unknown oscillators, where a learner picks two of four reward channels and bounds regret using a confidence-set controller.

sf8b736ad0d.title: Turnout: Adaptive Attention Switching for Efficient Reasoning
sf8b736ad0d.description: arXiv:2611.27500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc transformer linearization replaces the key-value cache of full attention, which grows linearly with generation length, with a fixed size state. This change reduces memory consumption but often hurts accuracy. In reasoning tasks, which require long generations, this effect is especially pronounced. In this work we introduce Turnout, a method that mitigates accuracy loss as a result of linearization, while maintaining its memory-reduction benefits. We apply post-hoc linearization to a pretrained full-attention model, training a linear path through distillation while leaving the original full-attention path unchanged. During response generation, the resulting hybrid model retains both paths and uses a learned policy to control when ea
sf8b736ad0d.summary: Turnout is a method that applies post-hoc linearization to pretrained full-attention models, aiming to recover the accuracy lost on long reasoning tasks while keeping memory savings.
sf8b736ad0d.why: Targets the accuracy cost of replacing growing KV caches with fixed-size states, relevant to teams serving long-generation reasoning workloads.

s5eed1aed48.title: The Assistant Persona Differs Across Languages in Activation Space
s5eed1aed48.description: arXiv:2611.27504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models behave differently across languages, and are noticeably less safe in lower-resource languages. This gap is well established behaviorally, but not mechanistically. Directions in activation space, including the assistant persona direction, are almost always extracted from English and assumed to generalize across languages. We extract the assistant persona direction in 31 languages in Qwen3-32B, and find that the resulting axes differ substantially: their cosine similarity to the English axis ranges from 0.378 to 0.911. Moreover, each language's assistant persona direction and its magnitude are correlated with the language's resource level. We also find that the model's default assistant state is farther from the helpful
s5eed1aed48.summary: Researchers extracted the assistant persona direction in 31 languages for Qwen3-32B and found it differs substantially from the English axis, with cosine similarity from 0.378 to 0.911.
s5eed1aed48.why: Suggests safety steering vectors extracted from English may not transfer to other languages, a concern for multilingual deployments.

se0fd9495a9.title: Self-Supervised Continuous-Time Depth Learning and Ego-Motion Estimation from Asynchronous Events
se0fd9495a9.description: arXiv:2611.27509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Event cameras register brightness changes pixel by pixel with microsecond precision, whereas the dense depth that could supervise them is costly to acquire and exists only at isolated instants. Condensing the stream into frames eases learning, but at the expense of the very timing that sets event sensing apart. We propose a self-supervised approach in which each event is assigned its own depth in continuous time, and the camera motion is recovered from the same observations. Supervision arises from geometry: lifted into 3D by its predicted depth and displaced by the camera motion at the instant it fired, an event should coincide with others produced by the same edge, so any misalignment exposes an error in depth or motion. se0fd9495a9.summary: The paper proposes self-supervised continuous-time depth and ego-motion estimation from asynchronous event camera data, assigning each event its own depth.

s1c913deeed.title: PhiJEPA: Denoising Latent Predictions for Visual Representation Learning
s1c913deeed.description: arXiv:2611.27516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a predictor trained to infer hidden image regions still help a world model plan when part of an object disappears from view and the visible context is blurred? We introduce PhiJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts PhiNet's two-stage prediction to masked Transformers. From sparse, photometrically corrupted context, a Transformer block predicts hidden tokens of an independently corrupted teacher view. A token-wise MLP then maps these predictions to clean teacher tokens. Controlled ablations show that the combined objective improves dense features over the tested one-stage alternatives. Pre-trained on ImageNet-1K with $5.6\times10^{19}$ training FLOPs, PhiJEPA achieves 69.3 mIoU on linear PASCAL VOC segmentation, exce
s1c913deeed.summary: PhiJEPA is a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts two-stage prediction to masked Transformers for visual representation learning from corrupted context.

sc28adffe24.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks
sc28adffe24.description: arXiv:2611.27521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While vision-language models (VLMs) currently obtain notable results for highly-studied languages, e.g. English, they exhibit significant performance drops in certain low-resource languages, especially due to the lack of annotated datasets. To this end, we propose PaMuk-Bench, a novel parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks. Our benchmark includes a set of over 10K curated English prompts that are translated into six languages: Arabic, Danish, French, Hindi, Italian, Romanian. Parallel translations, which are obtained via a semi-automatic process, along with accompanying generated and retrieved images enable the comparative development and evaluation of VLMs across a wide range of tasks: text-to-image generation,
sc28adffe24.summary: PaMuk-Bench is a parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks, with over 10K English prompts translated into six languages.
sc28adffe24.why: Provides a parallel evaluation set for measuring VLM performance gaps in lower-resource languages.

sf9a782a95a.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
sf9a782a95a.description: arXiv:2611.27529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects in an image and predict the relationships between them. The standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings show how much performance drops without ground-truth boxes and labels, but not where or why a model fails. Knowing this would allow fixing a model where it fails, without retraining. We propose RoHa-SGG (Root-cause-guided Harness optimization for SGG), which extends agentic harness optimization to SGG. It optimizes the harness, the inference code around a frozen SGG model. RoHa-SGG has two main LLM agents. A root-cause analysis (RCA) agent finds the components where the model fails and diagnoses why, and a proposer agent searches for a harness that fixes these causes. We evaluate RoHa-SG
sf9a782a95a.summary: RoHa-SGG optimizes the inference harness around a frozen scene graph generation model using root-cause analysis to fix failures without retraining.
sf9a782a95a.why: Demonstrates harness-level optimization as a way to improve model performance without retraining, applicable to other agentic pipelines.

sc43d7b48ab.title: On the Limits of Observability for Evaluating Coverage in Machine Unlearning
sc43d7b48ab.description: arXiv:2611.27543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine unlearning aims to remove the influence of any requested subset of training data while preserving utility on the remaining data. Empirical evaluations measure predictive accuracy and infer training-set membership (MIAs) from model outputs or intermediate activations. However, by focusing on selected forget sets, these evaluations can overlook Coverage, the range of requests a method can fulfill. To assess this coverage, we first conduct a stress test of observability with 502 retrained models, finding that hidden embeddings reveal known deletions missed in predictions. To characterize capacity limits on coverage, we show that distinguishing all $n$ singleton deletions with linear scores can require a shared representation of rank $\
sc43d7b48ab.summary: The paper examines the limits of observability-based evaluation in machine unlearning, using a stress test with 502 retrained models to assess coverage of forget requests.
sc43d7b48ab.why: Suggests common unlearning evaluations may miss whether a method can fulfill the full range of removal requests.

s4e30510cbd.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
s4e30510cbd.description: arXiv:2611.27556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's questio
s4e30510cbd.summary: Researchers present a hierarchical multi-agent LLM system to help investigate instrumentation anomalies at Switzerland's Beznau Unit 1 nuclear reactor by unifying siloed data.
s4e30510cbd.why: Illustrates a multi-agent LLM deployment in a safety-critical industrial setting with fragmented legacy data sources.

se16bb75db1.title: Unlocking Heterogeneous Accelerator Flexibility in AI Data Centers: Sizing and Workload Allocation
se16bb75db1.description: arXiv:2611.27576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI data centers are an emerging electricity demand, but limited local grid capacity could delay their connection and expansion. While existing operational strategies consider spatio-temporal workload flexibility, few studies address the strategic sizing and allocation of diverse accelerator archetypes with different capital and energy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper unlocks the flexibility potential of heterogeneous accelerators by jointly sizing and allocating different AI workloads (training, delay-tolerant batch work, and online inference requests) across sites and hours to meet the time-varying grid constraint at minimum cost. Workload-specific throughput and energy coefficients link these decisions to facility power. In a representat
se16bb75db1.summary: The paper proposes jointly sizing and allocating heterogeneous AI accelerators and workloads, such as training, batch, and inference, under limited local grid capacity.
se16bb75db1.why: Frames data center capacity planning around grid constraints and accelerator mix, relevant to infrastructure leads.

s040aa12518.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
s040aa12518.description: arXiv:2611.27601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spoken dialogue synthesis aims to generate multi-turn conversational speech from dialogue scripts while maintaining speaker consistency and contextual appropriateness. However, existing models largely lack fine-grained controllability, which is critical for capturing the dynamic, context-dependent style shifts in natural conversations. While prompt-based TTS has enabled such control for single-speaker speech, existing datasets heavily rely on predefined tags, which fundamentally limits their capacity to capture open-ended styles. To address this gap, we propose a scalable pipeline for extracting conversational speech from multi-narrator audiobooks, featuring an improved two-stage alignment algorithm to preserve dialogue continuity, paired w
s040aa12518.summary: PromptTTSD is a controllable text-to-spoken-dialogue synthesis method that uses open-ended text descriptions rather than predefined style tags.

s7e2e1a3564.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
s7e2e1a3564.description: arXiv:2611.27618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There has been significant recent interest in understanding the behaviour of LLM agents from the perspective of human preferences or corpus statistics. In this paper we propose agent states as intermediate variables through which post-training can be measured and predicted. From a statistical physics perspective, we study the emergence of a global potential which governs the transition of state in LLM agent reasoning. We introduce a partition function to model the ideal KL-regularised transition distribution and track potential structure, mean reward and state entropy. We demonstrate our approach in two Qwen3.5-9B tasks: safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing. We observe that the potential structure strengthens during post-tra
s7e2e1a3564.summary: The paper uses a statistical physics framework, with agent states and a partition function, to study emergence of a global potential governing LLM agent reasoning transitions.

s43d5eb8e2d.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild
s43d5eb8e2d.description: arXiv:2611.27673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hy-MT3 is the third generation of the Hunyuan multilingual translation model family, including \textbf{Hy-MT3-1.8B}, \textbf{Hy-MT3-7B} and \textbf{Hy-MT3-30B-A3B (MoE)}. Compared with Hy-MT2, Hy-MT3 translates \textbf{more accurately, more completely and more faithfully to user constraints}: on real-world scenario data, the share of samples with mistranslations is reduced by \textbf{43\%}, omissions or additions by \textbf{74\%}, and instruction-following errors by \textbf{40\%}, while language coverage is expanded from \textbf{38 to 102} languages. With only 3B activated parameters, \textbf{Hy-MT3-30B-A3B achieves the best overall performance among all evaluated models in non-thinking mode}, including flagship models such as Qwen3.8-Max,
s43d5eb8e2d.summary: Tencent's Hy-MT3 is a third-generation multilingual translation model family in 1.8B, 7B, and 30B-A3B MoE sizes, with language coverage expanded from 38 to 102.
s43d5eb8e2d.why: Offers a range of translation model sizes with broader language coverage, useful for teams evaluating self-hosted translation options.

s3d55136773.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
s3d55136773.description: arXiv:2611.27689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed
s3d55136773.summary: Embodied-Harness is a dual-agent framework where an Actor and a Reflector improve VLM-based robotic manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model weights.
s3d55136773.why: Shows improving robotic agents through memory and reflection in the harness rather than retraining model parameters.

s43ce8c26be.title: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders
s43ce8c26be.description: arXiv:2611.27721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decision models receive a question with a closed list of answers and return a probability for each answer instead of free text. They promise low latency and robustness to prompt wording, but no study has compared several of them with fine-tuned encoders across languages. We ask whether systems used without training on labelled data (zero-shot) can replace fine-tuning, and what the decision format adds over a general-purpose large language model (LLM). We compare three decision models (Jev, OpenAI Decisions, Strands Decider 2B) and two LLMs (GPT-6 Luna, Qwen3.5-2B), given Italian instructions, with two fine-tuned multilingual encoders (tabularisai, XLM-EMO) on four emotions (joy, sadness, anger, fear) in 10 social-media datasets in five lang
s43ce8c26be.summary: Researchers compare three decision models and two LLMs against fine-tuned encoders for multilingual emotion classification, testing whether zero-shot systems can replace fine-tuning.
s43ce8c26be.why: Shows whether closed-answer decision models can match fine-tuned encoders across languages, relevant to choosing low-latency classifiers over LLMs.

sa9e5f6e3fe.title: Quantitative Measurement of Pavement Distress based on Vehicle Camera and Perspective Correction
sa9e5f6e3fe.description: arXiv:2611.27728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using image data is becoming an important method for highway agencies to automatically evaluate pavement conditions. However, most studies focus on improving detection accuracy rather than obtaining quantitative measurements, such as the length or area of pavement distress. Although field camera calibration can provide such measurements, it is impractical for large volumes of onboard images collected from different vehicles. This study develops a method to quantitatively measure pavement distress directly from in-vehicle camera images without on-site camera calibration. A quadrilateral region of interest is first identified based on lane detection and used to construct a perspective transformation matrix for image correction. Size correctio
sa9e5f6e3fe.summary: Researchers propose a method to measure pavement distress length and area directly from in-vehicle camera images without field camera calibration.

s21bbfa7d92.title: Shared Understanding in Human-AI Teams: Coordination Continuity in Evolving Work
s21bbfa7d92.description: arXiv:2611.27746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: People are increasingly working with AI agents as part of extended, asynchronous workflows. In these settings, shared access to information does not guarantee a shared basis for action: goals, plans, and roles may persist while their current significance changes. We introduce coordination continuity, the extent to which collaborators sustain a workable basis for interdependent action as work progresses. Drawing on research on collaborative work, along with two qualitative team studies and a reflexive case from our own repository-based environment, we present a framework of three elements: durable representations of collaborative work; relative coordination properties that support interpretation of representations in the moment; and interact
s21bbfa7d92.summary: Researchers introduce coordination continuity, a concept for how human-AI teams keep a workable shared basis for action as asynchronous work evolves.
s21bbfa7d92.why: Offers a framing for designing agent workflows where shared information does not guarantee shared understanding of goals and roles.

s4e0a04e07a.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
s4e0a04e07a.description: arXiv:2611.27750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable significant progress in scientific tasks. However, these models are generally assumed to be presented with complete and accurate information, overlooking the challenges of erroneous/missing information in wild scenarios. To address this gap, we introduce the concept of Scientific Model Robustness, which defines a model's ability to detect anomalies, assess solvability, and perform self-calibration when faced with Information Error (inconsistencies) or Information Loss (insufficiency). Specifically, we present RoSci-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,220 samples using a seed-variant strategy across six degradation types. To address VLM fragility, we further propose RoSci-Agent, a fr
s4e0a04e07a.summary: Researchers introduce Scientific Model Robustness and a benchmark for science vision-language models facing erroneous or missing information.
s4e0a04e07a.why: Highlights that scientific VLMs are often evaluated on complete inputs, which matters for deploying them on real-world messy data.

sf505643dc1.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
sf505643dc1.description: arXiv:2611.27780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal search agents answer knowledge intensive visual questions by grounding them in retrieved evidence, and recent recipes train them on multi hop tasks that are synthesized from knowledge graphs and grown online to keep pace with the agent. These recipes, however, treat the searchable world as fixed: a new question can be well formed and verifiable while its evidence is absent from the retrieval backend, so the agent issues the right query, retrieves nothing, and is penalized as if its policy were at fault. Such unreachable negatives accumulate with every round of growth. We propose Search-RSI, a recursive self improvement framework that expands the search world along the agent's capability frontier. In each round, the current policy
sf505643dc1.summary: Researchers propose Search-RSI, a training approach for multimodal search agents that expands the searchable world so unanswerable queries do not penalize the agent's policy.
sf505643dc1.why: Addresses flawed training signals where missing retrieval evidence is wrongly counted as agent failure.

s124091de9d.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
s124091de9d.description: arXiv:2611.27784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. We evaluate it on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks, scoring every recording exactly as released, and against commercial systems on independent leaderboards. ARCAS 290M ranks first among all systems on the Podonos leaderboard and has the lowest equal error
s124091de9d.summary: Neural Defend introduces ARCAS 290M, a frozen foundation model it says detects AI-generated audio across generators, channels, and languages on ten public benchmarks.
s124091de9d.why: Relevant to teams building deepfake or voice-cloning defenses, though claims rest on the vendor's own evaluation.

s09852a180e.title: $\mathtt{DistP}$: Scaling Local-Update Training with Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
s09852a180e.description: arXiv:2611.27808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local-update methods offer a communication-efficient alternative to Distributed Data Parallelism ($\mathtt{DDP}$), but introduce additional hyperparameters that require costly tuning. For $\mathtt{DDP}$, zero-shot hyperparameter transfer reduces this cost by reusing settings tuned on smaller models, but its applicability to local-update training remains unclear. We propose $\mathtt{DistP}$, a theoretical framework extending existing transfer rules from $\mathtt{DDP}$ to local-update training with varying worker counts, local steps, and outer optimizers. s09852a180e.summary: Researchers propose DistP, a framework extending zero-shot hyperparameter transfer from data-parallel training to local-update distributed training.
s09852a180e.why: Could cut tuning cost for communication-efficient distributed training by reusing settings from smaller models.

s8a55be3cb1.title: Redesigning Neural Networks to Not be Confidently Wrong even to Strong Adversarial Attacks
s8a55be3cb1.description: arXiv:2611.27811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Early deep learning models attempted to simulate visual perception using a neural hierarchy that alternated between two types of layer: one modelled on cortical simple cells (that was designed to increase selectivity), and one modelled on cortical complex cells (that aimed to increase tolerance). We show that such a neural network (NN) architecture, when implemented with novel components that are better able to learn selective and tolerant representations, is capable of accurate and robust image classification and improved alignment between the behaviour of the model and the perceptual abilities of humans. s8a55be3cb1.summary: Researchers present a neural network architecture alternating selective and tolerant layers that they claim classifies images robustly and avoids confident errors under strong adversarial attacks.

s7aa709c6b3.title: Graph Signal Generation via Graph-Aware Diffusion Models
s7aa709c6b3.description: arXiv:2611.27826v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many signals are defined on the nodes of a graph, such as traffic flow at road sensors or user purchases of related products. They are often partly observed, and learning their distribution enables imputing missing values and forecasting future ones. Diffusion models learn such distributions, but their forward noise is independent across nodes and does not depend on the graph. We introduce graph-aware diffusion (GAD), whose forward process is a heat diffusion on the graph driven by Gaussian noise. s7aa709c6b3.summary: Researchers introduce graph-aware diffusion, a generative model whose forward noise process follows heat diffusion on a graph, for generating graph-structured signals.
s7aa709c6b3.why: Could help impute missing values and forecast graph-structured data such as sensor or sales networks.

se202765230.title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
se202765230.description: arXiv:2611.27860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmarks for AI-based coding agents are a staple of the current AI landscape, because they are the leading way to measure the performance of LLMs. Their scores guide business and research decisions. Evaluating coding agents is challenging, since they are able to manipulate their evaluation infrastructure to artificially achieve better scores. Grading an agent's solution often requires running its code, which can then manipulate the evaluation process. BenchJack, an automated benchmark auditor, recently reached near-perfect scores on nine of ten popular agent benchmarks without actually solving their tasks. se202765230.summary: Researchers propose privilege separation for coding-agent benchmarks after BenchJack, an automated auditor, reached near-perfect scores on nine benchmarks by exploiting evaluation infrastructure.
se202765230.why: Benchmark scores guide purchasing and research decisions, so agents that can tamper with grading undermine their validity.

s86007e4ced.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Comparing Categorical and Continuous World Models
s86007e4ced.description: arXiv:2611.27870v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual world models can now generate compelling interactive worlds, but visual realism does not guarantee faithful dynamics. We systematically compare how categorical and continuous prediction shape learned dynamics under both next-token and iterative whole-frame generation. These choices are often bundled in approaches such as autoregressive token models and whole-frame flow matching. We design controlled 2D and 3D environments and evaluate dynamics validity, calibration, and visual quality. In 2D with lossless visual encoding, categorical models achieve higher rollout validity with less training compute, particularly for stochastic entities. s86007e4ced.summary: Researchers compare categorical and continuous world models, finding that visual realism does not guarantee faithful dynamics in controlled 2D and 3D environments.
s86007e4ced.why: Suggests visually convincing world models may still learn incorrect dynamics, which matters when using them for planning or simulation.

s025eeaaa2c.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
s025eeaaa2c.description: arXiv:2611.27876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic g
s025eeaaa2c.summary: Researchers introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that tracks tumors and assesses treatment response in longitudinal CT scans without task-specific training, using frozen 3D models.

safce00366f.title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
safce00366f.description: arXiv:2611.27895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. We introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark built on the Brazilian pathway for early autism (TEA) screening: three fictitious instruments with the structure of real ones, a multi-professional referral flow, and export to FHIR R4 with the national RNDS profiles, all specified in Portuguese. A generator samples each task's parameters (144 tasks, 6,798 hidden cases), and the hidden cases kill all 1,955 non-equivalent mutants of the reference. With Gemma 4 as the agent, the 12B solves 38.0% of single-instrument tasks and none at the FHIR level; the 31B solves 77.8%, 85.2% and 78.7% at levels 1 to 3 and passe
safce00366f.summary: Researchers introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a Portuguese benchmark testing whether coding agents can implement a branching Brazilian autism screening specification correctly.
safce00366f.why: Shows that silent bugs in agent-written domain-rule code can produce plausible but wrong outputs, a risk for regulated software.

s19a3b30fe2.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
s19a3b30fe2.description: arXiv:2611.27910v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering
s19a3b30fe2.summary: Researchers propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns that store calibrated yes/no style answers to natural-language questions, for entity matching and search.
s19a3b30fe2.why: Offers auditable, filterable retrieval for business data, useful where agents need explainable record matching.

s3702f60b27.title: Star Panoptic Quality: Selectively Evaluating Split and Merged Instances
s3702f60b27.description: arXiv:2611.27913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Detecting individual instances is crucial for many segmentation problems. However, expert instance annotations are often unavailable, so instances are approximated heuristically (e.g., as connected components of semantic maps), which can merge touching objects or split fragmented ones. Even when expert annotations exist, expert disagreement or structural delineation biases can yield split or merged reference instances, corresponding to over- or under-segmentation, respectively. Panoptic Quality (PQ) and related metrics capture both segmentation and detection quality while weighting all instances equally, regardless of size. Yet when the references are biased, these metrics can neither detect split or merged instances nor distinguish valid f
s3702f60b27.summary: Researchers propose Star Panoptic Quality, a metric for instance segmentation that selectively evaluates split and merged instances when expert annotations are imperfect.

s9f14d4c4c0.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
s9f14d4c4c0.description: arXiv:2611.27915v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly fr
s9f14d4c4c0.summary: Researchers introduce StereoVLM, a vision-language model using calibrated binocular stereo input to reason about metric 3D space.
s9f14d4c4c0.why: Stereo geometry gives VLMs explicit cross-view constraints, a potential route to more grounded metric spatial predictions than single-image inference.

s61b75229da.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
s61b75229da.description: arXiv:2611.27919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reward-independent representations enable reinforcement learning agents to reuse knowledge across tasks, but limited representation capacity raises three fundamental questions: what statistical dependence should these representations capture, which components of that dependence should be retained for policy improvement, and how does discarding the remaining components affect decision-making? We address these questions through canonical dependence analysis. For a reference policy, we construct an action-centered, positive-lag canonical dependence matrix (CDM) that isolates the additional predictive contribution of the current action beyond the current state. Its singular value decomposition yields Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF)
s61b75229da.summary: Researchers propose SUAF, a reward-independent representation method using canonical dependence analysis to enable zero-shot policy improvement in reinforcement learning.

s0d817fb684.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
s0d817fb684.description: arXiv:2611.27962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's
s0d817fb684.summary: Researchers present Model Carving, a training approach where Transformers learn their own topology instead of using a fixed, uniform layer structure.
s0d817fb684.why: If training can shape architecture, it could yield smaller, more efficient models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s9833cac21d.title: Non-penetrating World Models
s9833cac21d.description: arXiv:2611.27963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. s9833cac21d.summary: Researchers introduce NoPeBench to study object penetration in interactive video world models, finding open-source models fail to reliably prevent it.
s9833cac21d.why: Hidden states of diffusion transformers can predict penetrating actions, suggesting a practical signal for improving physical consistency in world models.

s5e21f5de3f.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
s5e21f5de3f.description: arXiv:2611.27983v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $\alpha$-moment $\nu$ for some unknown $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment.
