s5e21f5de3f.summary: Researchers give a black-box reduction that adapts finite-variance linear regression procedures to work under heavy-tailed noise with only a finite moment of order between 1 and 2.
s5e21f5de3f.why: Provides robust regression guarantees when noise has infinite variance, relevant to heavy-tailed data in practical estimation pipelines.

sa1302f6252.title: PsyAgent: Constructing Human-like Agents Based on Psychological Modeling and Contextual Interaction
sa1302f6252.description: arXiv:2601.06158v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Human-like agents must express stable dispositions while adapting to roles, relationships, and norms. We present PsyAgent, a schema-first framework that operationalizes the trait-context interface by coupling a Big Five trait prior with explicit social-structural conditioning. PsyAgent comprises (i) Individual Structure (IS), a machine-usable trait-grounded profile, and (ii) Multi-Scenario Contexting (MSC), a curated library of role-relationship-norm frames spanning eight everyday arenas. At inference, fixed structured prompts couple the active MSC frame with the IS profile, encouraging behavior that is stable yet context-sensitive. To demonstrate learnability beyond prompt engineering, we use IS x MSC to synthesize supervision and fine-t
sa1302f6252.summary: PsyAgent is a framework that builds human-like agents by pairing Big Five trait profiles with role, relationship, and norm contexts across eight scenarios.
sa1302f6252.why: Offers a structured approach to making agent personas stable yet context-adaptive, useful for designing consistent conversational agents.

sb90d957f5b.title: AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent
sb90d957f5b.description: arXiv:2602.03955v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems achieve superior reasoning performance through iterative debate, practical deployment is limited by their high computational cost and error propagation. This paper proposes AgentArk, a novel framework to distill multi-agent dynamics into the weights of a single model, effectively transforming explicit test-time interactions into implicit model capabilities. This equips a single agent with the intelligence of multi-agent systems while remaining computationally efficient. Specifically, we investigate three hierarchical distillation strategies across various models, tasks, scaling, and scenarios: reasoning-enhanced fine-tuning; trajectory-based augmentation; and process-aware distillation.
sb90d957f5b.summary: AgentArk distills multi-agent debate dynamics into the weights of a single LLM agent, aiming to keep multi-agent reasoning gains at lower compute cost.
sb90d957f5b.why: Suggests multi-agent reasoning benefits could be captured in one cheaper model, reducing latency and error propagation in deployment.

sf136e39d18.title: VeRA: Verified Reasoning Data Augmentation at Scale
sf136e39d18.description: arXiv:2602.13217v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Static benchmarks wear out: their problems circulate widely and can enter training data, and their scores saturate as models improve. Renewing a benchmark requires new problems with reliable answers, which are expensive to write by hand at competition level. We introduce VeRA (Verified Reasoning Data Augmentation), in which a language model automatically compiles each benchmark problem into an executable specification: a question template, a generator of valid inputs, and a program that computes the answer. Once its programs pass automatic checks, a specification yields many fresh, code-labeled problems at almost no cost, and people are needed only to audit. VeRA-E (equivalent) draws new instances of the same computation. VeRA-H (hardened
sf136e39d18.summary: VeRA uses a language model to compile benchmark problems into executable generators and answer programs, producing verified new reasoning problems at scale.
sf136e39d18.why: Automatically renewing verified benchmarks helps address saturation and contamination in model evaluation pipelines.

s904cf829e7.title: GAAMA: Graph Augmented Associative Memory for Agents
s904cf829e7.description: arXiv:2603.27910v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI agents that talk with users across many sessions need long-term memory to stay coherent and personalized. Existing approaches use either flat retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that ignores how memories connect, or entity-centric knowledge graphs. Entity-centric graphs split each message into separate triples, which loses its context, and in conversations the speakers become hubs linked to almost every message, so propagation through them tells retrieval little. We present GAAMA, a graph-augmented associative memory that organizes conversations around topics. It keeps verbatim episodes, uses an LLM to distill them into atomic facts and topic concepts, and then synthesizes higher-order reflections. These four node types are linked by
s904cf829e7.summary: GAAMA is a graph-augmented associative memory that organizes conversation memories as graphs to improve long-term memory retrieval for AI agents.
s904cf829e7.why: Addresses limits of flat RAG and entity-centric graphs for multi-session agent memory, a core challenge for personalized assistants.

sc9139ec9b1.title: ScrapMem: A Bio-Inspired Framework for On-Device Personalized Agent Memory via Optical Forgetting
sc9139ec9b1.description: arXiv:2605.03804v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Long-term personalized memory for LLM agents is challenging on resource-limited edge devices because multimodal histories grow continually and are costly to store. To address this challenge, we propose ScrapMem, a bio-inspired framework that consolidates each day's heterogeneous records into a unified "Scrapbook Page." ScrapMem introduces Optical Forgetting, an optical compression mechanism that progressively reduces the resolution and JPEG quality of older pages, lowering storage costs while keeping recent evidence at higher fidelity. To preserve semantic consistency and support structured retrieval, we construct an Episodic Memory Graph (EM-Graph) that organizes semantic nodes into causal-temporal EM-Paths. This design separates a stabl
sc9139ec9b1.summary: ScrapMem proposes an on-device agent memory framework that progressively compresses older multimodal records via optical forgetting to reduce storage costs.
sc9139ec9b1.why: Shows a storage-versus-fidelity tradeoff for personalized agent memory on resource-limited edge devices.

s104c9a1615.title: Hierarchical Task Network Planning with LLM-Generated Heuristics
s104c9a1615.description: arXiv:2605.07707v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: HTN planning is a variation of classical planning where, instead of searching for a linear sequence of actions, an algorithm decomposes higher-level tasks using a method library until only executable actions remain. On the one hand, this allows one to introduce domain knowledge that can speed up the search for a solution through the method library. On the other hand, it creates challenges that go beyond those of classical state-space search. While recent research produced a number of heuristics and novel algorithms that speed up HTN planning, these heuristics are not yet as informative as those available in classical planning algorithms. We investigate whether large language models (LLMs) can generate effective search heuristics for HTN p
s104c9a1615.summary: Researchers study using LLM-generated heuristics to speed up Hierarchical Task Network planning, which decomposes tasks via a method library.

s8ea173b5a1.title: CatalyticMLLM: A Graph-Text Multimodal Large Language Model for Catalytic Materials
s8ea173b5a1.description: arXiv:2605.17254v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Property prediction and inverse structural design of catalytic materials are typically modeled as two independent tasks: the former predicts target properties from given structures, whereas the latter generates candidate structures conditioned on desired properties. Although this decoupled paradigm facilitates the construction of a ``generation--evaluation--screening'' workflow, the two models may have different domains of applicability because they are trained on different data distributions. Consequently, during closed-loop optimization, the generative model may produce structures that fall outside the reliable applicability domain of the evaluation model, while prediction errors from the evaluator may accumulate over successive iterati
s8ea173b5a1.summary: CatalyticMLLM is a graph-text multimodal LLM that unifies property prediction and inverse design of catalytic materials to keep closed-loop optimization consistent.
s8ea173b5a1.why: Combining prediction and generation in one model targets consistency in materials discovery workflows that currently use two separate models.

s461278ee40.title: GENSTRAT: Toward a Science of Strategic Reasoning in Large Language Models
s461278ee40.description: arXiv:2605.23238v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fixed game suites for evaluating strategic reasoning in large language models (LLMs) saturate and are hard to keep free of contamination. We introduce GENSTRAT, a system for evaluating the strategic capabilities of LLMs driven by procedural generation of two-player zero-sum imperfect-information betting games, allowing an evaluator to draw novel, fresh games on demand. Each game is characterized on a scale of five complexity axes (state space, temporal contingency, opponent dependence, private information, precision) and measured by Monte Carlo simulation. Using this generator, we construct a 50-game benchmark and hold a tournament of twelve frontier and open-weight models, gathering data from over 40,000 LLM vs. LLM matches. We further c
s461278ee40.summary: GENSTRAT generates fresh two-player zero-sum imperfect-information betting games on demand to evaluate strategic reasoning in LLMs without contamination.
s461278ee40.why: Procedurally generated games offer a way to evaluate LLM strategic capability without saturated or leaked benchmarks.

s35db5decea.title: Declarative Skills for AI Agents in Knowledge-Grounded Tool-Use Workflows
s35db5decea.description: arXiv:2606.06923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how orchestration affects tool-using large language model (LLM) agents in customer-service workflows over an unstructured knowledge base, comparing a declarative agent that reads natural-language skill files, an imperative agent built on a state machine, and an unscaffolded baseline. The three are formalized as policy classes within one decentralized partially observable Markov decision process and evaluated on a complete design of five models, two retrieval regimes, and three agents, with paired tests. Averaged over all conditions, orchestration does not improve task success. The effect, however, depends on the quality of the agent's observation channel. Under perfect retrieval, skill files are neutral-to-negative on four of the
s35db5decea.summary: A study compares declarative skill files, imperative state-machine agents, and an unscaffolded baseline for tool-using LLM agents in customer-service workflows.
s35db5decea.why: Compares orchestration styles for customer-service agents on the same policy framework, informing how teams structure agent workflows.

s4b08ca841f.title: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments
s4b08ca841f.description: arXiv:2606.16062v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Code RL rewards a policy for passing a task's tests, so a test suite that accepts a wrong patch trains the wrong behavior. We measure how often open code RL environments accept wrong patches and how reliably hackable tasks can be detected and repaired, checking each claim by execution against the task's gold patch. First, 22.4% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept a Docker-verified patch that behaves differently from the gold patch, and 57.8% against a stronger attacker. The gold-patch check is necessary: an attacker not shown the gold patch returns it for 31% of its passing "exploits". s4b08ca841f.summary: An audit finds 22.4% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept wrong patches that behave differently from the gold patch, rising to 57.8% against a stronger attacker.
s4b08ca841f.why: Code RL environments with weak tests can reward incorrect behavior, so teams training on them risk learning the wrong patches.

s9998cf8329.title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale
s9998cf8329.description: arXiv:2608.00101v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI coding agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex) interleave multi-step LLM inference with tool execution, creating a workload different from chatbots. We present the first production-scale characterization of coding agents using sampled GitHub Copilot traces from June-July 2026, comprising 7.4M users, 819M conversations, 5.7B LLM calls, and 946T tokens. Our analysis reveals distinctive workload properties with unique systems implications: e.g., sparse user-initiated turns unfold into autonomous agent loops with nearly 1:1 coupling between LLM calls and tool execution; parallel LLM calls are rare but exist in turns that trigger subagents; KV cache hit rates average 90% within a turn, but fall to 52% across turn boundaries and to
s9998cf8329.summary: Researchers characterized production GitHub Copilot coding-agent traces from June-July 2026, covering 7.4M users, 819M conversations, 5.7B LLM calls, and 946T tokens.
s9998cf8329.why: Gives engineers real-world workload data on how coding agents run multi-step LLM inference and tool loops, informing infrastructure and serving decisions.

sf309802589.title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding
sf309802589.description: arXiv:2608.11095v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agentic prompts like CLAUDE.md grow without bound in real repositories, stopping only when history ends or someone rewrites the file wholesale. We trace this to imperfect recall: appending an instruction is always cheap, but once an instruction's latent reasoning is gone, deleting it without risking a regression costs O(2^|D|) in a prompt of |D| instructions. Successive edits destroy that latent reasoning, additions outrun deletions and prompts grow until agents become non-functional -- catastrophic remembering. First, we characterize this phenomenon across 247,694 instruction lifetimes in 1,867 repositories: agentic prompts grow nearly monotonically, more than tripling over their lifetime (+226%) at +4.7 net instructions per commit. sf309802589.summary: A paper argues that agent instruction files like CLAUDE.md grow without bound because deleting instructions safely becomes prohibitively costly, a failure it calls catastrophic remembering.
sf309802589.why: Suggests teams maintaining agent instruction files will face growing, hard-to-prune prompts that can eventually make agents non-functional.

sff4e9200a5.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
sff4e9200a5.description: arXiv:2608.17202v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Safety alignment in open-weight language models is trivially removable: abliteration projects a refusal-mediating direction out of the weights in minutes, and no release-time defense we are aware of prevents it durably. What cannot be prevented can be deceived. Our defense, decoy hardening ("Fool's Gold"), concedes the refusal strip and poisons its payoff: once refusal is stripped, most answers to hazardous operational requests are confident, fluent decoys whose critical elements are falsified. sff4e9200a5.summary: Fool's Gold proposes decoy hardening for open-weight models, so that after safety refusals are removed via abliteration, hazardous answers are falsified decoys.
sff4e9200a5.why: Offers a defense idea for open-weight release risks, though the abstract alone does not show how well it works in practice.

s4596e7be42.title: FUSE: A Modular Framework for Evaluating Dangerous Capabilities of LLMs
s4596e7be42.description: arXiv:2609.02168v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dangerous capabilities of large language models (LLMs) cannot yet be compared across models: knowledge, refusal, and harm benchmarks each cover one step of a misuse path, on different models, protocols, and scales, so regulators cannot tell which model poses greater risk. We present FUSE, a modular framework that defines dangerous capability as a model's ability to advance a black-box adversary along a misuse path, and measures three stages of that path under one protocol: hazardous knowledge, estimated by item response theory; defense under multi-turn adversarial induction by a red-team agent; and the actionability of content produced once the model complies (harm). s4596e7be42.summary: FUSE is a modular framework that measures LLM dangerous capabilities across knowledge, defense, and misuse stages under one protocol, so models can be compared.
s4596e7be42.why: Provides a common benchmark approach for comparing misuse risk across models, relevant to teams assessing model safety and regulatory compliance.

s868d1a0053.title: Protecting Private Values in Tool-Using LLM Agents via Recoverable Context Projection
s868d1a0053.description: arXiv:2609.15011v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Memory-augmented and tool-using agents may expose exact private values when a remote LLM processes retrieved memory, tool actions, and observations. One-way masking limits initial exposure but removes values needed for trusted execution and may allow them to reappear in later observations. We propose Trustworthy Virtual Memory (TVM), a closed-loop runtime that exposes only projected context to the remote model, resolves exact values locally for trusted execution, and reprojects subsequent observations. s868d1a0053.summary: Trustworthy Virtual Memory is a runtime that shows remote LLMs only projected context, resolving exact private values locally for trusted tool execution.
s868d1a0053.why: Addresses leakage of sensitive values when tool-using agents send memory and observations to remote models, a concern for enterprise agent deployments.

s92b90e76b4.title: Fine-Tuning Fixes Mode Collapse and Over-Dispersion in LLMs
s92b90e76b4.description: arXiv:2609.16454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work by Doshi and Hauser (2024), Bisbee et al. (2024), and Xie et al. (2026) raises concerns that outputs from large language models (LLMs) tend to be under-diverse: they repeat or resemble one another more often than responses from the population they are meant to represent, a phenomenon known as mode collapse. In this work, we show that whether mode-collapse, or its opposite, occurs depends on the specific model and dataset used. s92b90e76b4.summary: This paper finds that whether LLMs show mode collapse or over-dispersion depends on model and dataset, and that sufficient supervised fine-tuning brings output diversity toward the target population's.
s92b90e76b4.why: Suggests output diversity problems depend on specific model and data choices and can be addressed through fine-tuning, relevant to synthetic-data and survey use cases.

sc50885da6f.title: Bridging Learned Visual Perception and Symbolic Belief-Space Planning via Probabilistic Grounding
sc50885da6f.description: arXiv:2609.16884v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In partially observable settings, agents must act without full knowledge of the world state and rely on uncertain state-estimation pipelines. Obtaining grounded and verifiable symbolic plans under such uncertainty remains a key challenge. Recent work has integrated Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to bridge perception and symbolic reasoning, following two main paradigms. The first, VLM-as-planner, maps images directly to action sequences, and the second, VLM-as-grounder, grounds observations into symbolic predicates used as the initial state by off-the-shelf planners. Both approaches ignore uncertainty in the planning process, compromising robustness. We introduce a third paradigm, VLM-as-probabilistic-grounder, a novel approach that capture
sc50885da6f.summary: The paper proposes linking learned visual perception with symbolic belief-space planning through probabilistic grounding for agents acting under partial observability.

scd7bc45f39.title: Task-Specific Agent Memory For Continual Learning
scd7bc45f39.description: arXiv:2609.29144v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Language-model agents can learn continually by storing useful instructions in memory and reusing them as new tasks arrive, without changing model weights. This requires both learning from new feedback and retaining earlier gains. However, an instruction learned from one task family can hurt other families when the agent uses the same memory for every task. We introduce task-specific agent memory: proposed skills are checked with execution tests, stored by task family, and retrieved for tasks in that family. We evaluate this design on a 12-round code-repair benchmark with recurring task families, tracking performance throughout learning. scd7bc45f39.summary: The paper proposes task-specific agent memory that checks learned skills with execution tests, stores them by task family, and retrieves them only for matching tasks.
scd7bc45f39.why: Shows that shared agent memory can hurt other task families, a practical design issue for teams building continually learning agents.

sdc8f37db65.title: ScopeAct: Scoping Decision Models for Reliable Multi-Step Execution in Mobile GUI Agents
sdc8f37db65.description: arXiv:2609.30186v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable mobile GUI agents to execute complex tasks, but frequent VLM invocations incur substantial latency and API costs. Prior work mitigates this overhead by delegating low-level action selection to lightweight decision models that choose among executable candidates. However, candidate selection alone lacks the task-level control needed to prevent premature termination and recover from failures, while candidates derived from accessibility trees (AXTrees) may not cover all actions required for task completion. To address these challenges, we introduce ScopeAct. sdc8f37db65.summary: ScopeAct proposes a scoping decision model to make mobile GUI agents more reliable in multi-step execution while reducing costly vision-language model calls.
sdc8f37db65.why: Targets latency and API cost of mobile GUI agents, along with premature termination and recovery, which matter for production agent builders.

s39fb789174.title: Why Directly Learning Periodic Trajectories Can Fail
s39fb789174.description: arXiv:2609.32254v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Operator learning of periodic solutions requires deciding how simulation data should be recorded and represented. A natural choice is to integrate long enough for transients to decay and record a window wide enough to contain at least one full period of all trajectories. We find that these conservative choices can make the resulting trajectories difficult to learn, even when the underlying periodic orbits vary regularly with system parameters. Unaligned trajectories generalize poorly even within the training distribution. s39fb789174.summary: The paper finds that directly learning periodic trajectories from conservatively recorded simulation data can fail, and that phase alignment helps.
s39fb789174.why: Offers a data-representation lesson for operator learning on periodic dynamics, though the relevance to most software teams is limited.

s7afa26b3c7.title: Language as the Interface: Foundation-Model Contrastive Learning Links Transcriptomes and Electrophysiology
s7afa26b3c7.description: arXiv:2609.37024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrating transcriptomic and electrophysiological data is essential for building multimodal foundation models for neuroscience. Patch-seq provides paired measurements of gene expression and intrinsic electrophysiology from the same neuron, establishing a basis for training cross-modal models. Here we introduce LangPatch, a foundation-model-based contrastive learning framework that uses paired Patch-seq data to align pretrained GenePT representations with electrophysiological phenotypes through a language-based interface. Gene descriptions and verbalized electrophysiological profiles are embedded by the same frozen text encoder. A context adapter and projection modules connect the modalities through paired contrastive learning. Across mo
s7afa26b3c7.summary: LangPatch uses a foundation-model-based contrastive learning framework to align gene-expression representations with electrophysiology data from paired Patch-seq measurements.

s8258a31b5c.title: Multi-Task Self-Evolving Harnesses with the Agent as Its Own Optimizer
s8258a31b5c.description: arXiv:2609.38372v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A harness is the code around a language model agent that organizes prompts, calls tools, manages context, and controls execution. As models grow stronger, recent work has begun to let agents improve their own harnesses, a line of work known as self-evolving harnesses. In most existing methods, a separate proposer running on a human-designed harness modifies the solver's harness, and a separate harness is evolved for each benchmark. Real-world tasks come from many domains, so both the evolution and the evaluation of a harness should cover a diverse range of tasks. We propose a framework close to recursive self-improvement: the same frozen model, on the same version of the harness, first solves tasks as the solver and then, as the proposer,
s8258a31b5c.summary: The paper proposes multi-task self-evolving harnesses, where an agent optimizes the code around its own language model across many task domains.
s8258a31b5c.why: Points to agents improving their own orchestration code, relevant to teams designing agent harnesses, though the abstract gives few results.

s4144895837.title: UniEvo-VL: An On-policy Self-Distillation Training Recipe for Multimodal Model Self-improvement
s4144895837.description: arXiv:2609.38721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern multimodal models bring generation and understanding into a single unified system, which enables them to provide and learn from their own feedback. Motivated by this unified capacity, we introduce UniEvo-VL, a self-evolving framework for multimodal models to learn from this constructive self-correction feedback during test-time compute. Instead of relying on a separately trained, stronger generator as teacher, we use critiques of the generator's own outputs, produced by a fixed vision-language critic, as privileged information. The generator and its EMA copy act as student and teacher under different contexts. The student only sees the vanilla question, while the teacher conditions on the privileged critique. Then training minimize
s4144895837.summary: UniEvo-VL is a self-evolving training framework where a unified multimodal model learns from critiques of its own outputs produced by a fixed vision-language critic.
s4144895837.why: Shows a route to multimodal self-improvement without a separate stronger teacher model, which can reduce training dependencies.

s1b8d6bb3eb.title: Disentangling Self-Distillation: Measuring and Modeling Acquisition and Retention
s1b8d6bb3eb.description: arXiv:2609.39494v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-distillation with privileged context adapts a language model from demonstrations by letting the model, once conditioned on a reference response, teach its context-free copy token by token. Our taxonomy reveals existing methods differ along three entangled axes: (i) the rollout source (student or teacher), (ii) the teacher coupling (frozen, or an exponential moving average of the student at some coupling rate) and (iii) the token-level divergence (here, reverse or forward KL), yet these axes are usually studied in fixed combinations and have led to conflicting conclusions. We formalize a unifying framework that covers both self-distillation and classic supervised fine-tuning: we train every combination of the three axes, on Qwen2.5-7B
s1b8d6bb3eb.summary: The paper separates the axes of self-distillation with privileged context, measuring how rollout source, teacher coupling, and token-level divergence affect acquisition and retention.
s1b8d6bb3eb.why: Clarifies which design choices in self-distillation drive learning and retention, useful for teams tuning fine-tuning recipes.

sd2928747fb.title: Frozen Scenes, Shifting Winners: Configuration Fragility in Text-to-3D Evaluation
sd2928747fb.description: arXiv:2610.00447v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can a text-to-3D leaderboard change when every generated scene stays fixed? We audit this question for rendered-image evaluation, where camera settings and caption wording become part of the measurement protocol. Across 300 frozen scenes from six generators, we vary eight render and caption factors for 19 alignment evaluators plus one perceptual-quality control, then test four targeted scene degradations. Peak configuration variance exceeds between-generator variance for 19/19 alignment evaluators, with prompt-bootstrap lower bounds above 1 for 19/19. Rankings are more stable than scores, yet 18/19 evaluators change their point-estimate winner under some configuration. Pairwise protocol margin envelopes show which comparisons keep their d
sd2928747fb.summary: An audit finds that camera settings and caption wording can change text-to-3D leaderboard rankings for 300 frozen scenes across six generators.
sd2928747fb.why: Warns that evaluation setup choices can outweigh real differences between generators, so benchmark results need careful protocol control.

sa8a482ac90.title: AI Safety Considerations for Agents With Limited Time to Act
sa8a482ac90.description: arXiv:2610.10285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the wake of the increasingly public discussion about AI alignment, recent work has tried to propose specific AI architectures that behave safely. However, the proposed arguments that seemingly demonstrate proved alignment mostly neglect the environment the agent needs to act in. We discuss theoretical bounds for agent-agnostic safety guarantees in environments that can only be partially observed and within which an action is required within limited time. We introduce two realistic scenarios, one with an infinite state space and one with signal mixture. In these scenarios, we prove that even a perfect agent cannot guarantee safe behaviour. It will be argued that for any proof of AI safety or alignment, the environment and associated saf
sa8a482ac90.summary: A theoretical paper examines bounds on agent-agnostic safety guarantees for agents acting under partial observability and limited time, introducing two scenarios.
sa8a482ac90.why: It challenges proofs of alignment that ignore the environment, suggesting safety guarantees for agents may be harder to establish than architecture-level claims imply.

s71d1b051ff.title: SkillForgeBench: Evaluating Agent Reliability Grounded in Agent Skill Specifications
s71d1b051ff.description: arXiv:2610.14918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Evaluating an agent's ability to strictly satisfy diverse and procedurally complex requirements is essential to determining its practical reliability. Conducting such an evaluation demands agentic tasks that reconcile broad domain coverage with deep procedural complexity. Existing paradigms face a fundamental trade-off: expert-curated benchmarks achieve procedural depth but suffer from domain diversity bottlenecks, whereas crowdsourced benchmarks span diverse scenarios but lack execution rigor. To resolve this tension, we present SkillForgeBench, which leverages agent skills as unifying execution blueprints across three co-designed stages: (1) Resource Preparation uses domain-balanced skills to guide artifact retrieval, establishing broad
s71d1b051ff.summary: SkillForgeBench is a proposed benchmark for evaluating agent reliability against procedurally complex agent skill specifications, aiming to combine domain diversity with execution rigor.
s71d1b051ff.why: Teams assessing agent reliability may find a benchmark grounded in skill specifications more rigorous than crowdsourced or expert-only alternatives.

sef28505a0b.title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
sef28505a0b.description: arXiv:2611.02936v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each time there is a new prediction task. Frozen foundation models (FMs) based on in-context learning (ICL) and RDB-specific pre-training provide a viable solution, but the ideal design still remains largely unresolved. Perhaps unexpectedly, preliminary evidence has recently shown that existing single-table FMs (aka TFMs), when combined with suitable parameter-free relational encoders, can be quite competitive in practice despite zero exposure to RDB pre-training or r
sef28505a0b.summary: A paper studies why frozen tabular foundation models using in-context learning perform well on relational databases they have not seen before.
sef28505a0b.why: It offers evidence that enterprise prediction tasks over relational data may be handled without training a new model per target column.

sac9b7d8bc3.title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning
sac9b7d8bc3.description: arXiv:2611.03100v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. We introduce LUCA, a configurable synthetic world for evaluating this process under fully known ground truth. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. This setup allows us to evaluate experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention separately. Across seven frontier LLMs and three baselines, these capabilities dissociate sharply. Agents frequently rescue malfunctioning systems while diagnosing the wrong fault; diagnosis varies 7x across models whi
sac9b7d8bc3.summary: LUCA is a configurable synthetic world for evaluating experimental reasoning, where agents learn hidden regulatory systems through budgeted experiments under fully known ground truth.
sac9b7d8bc3.why: It evaluates the experimental process rather than only final outcomes, which can help engineers detect agents that succeed for the wrong reasons.

secb76c570c.title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
secb76c570c.description: arXiv:2611.03713v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. Physicists call such a trial form an ansatz. Benchmarks for automated equation discovery mostly supply it, by fixing the variables, a library of candidate terms, or a law to be modified. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. Each task is a simulated system, generated from a private seed as a program in a small modeling language: ordinary, delay, or partial differential equations, discrete maps, static and causal models, or stochastic processes, possibly with latent states, distorted sensors, and uninformative measurement c
secb76c570c.summary: Unsatz is a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the model structure itself for scientific equation discovery, rather than being given variables or candidate terms.
secb76c570c.why: It tests whether agents can formulate models from scratch, a harder capability than fitting parameters within a supplied structure.

s7ba68c891e.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
s7ba68c891e.description: arXiv:2611.07048v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. Darwinian evolution relies on natural selection, Lamarckian evolution adds inherited learning, and agent-directed evolution allows agents to generate and evaluate behavioral variants and choose how extensively to search. When learning is sufficiently effective, these mechanisms exhibit progressi
s7ba68c891e.summary: A theoretical paper compares Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution in AI, asking how fast self-modifying agents could improve and how that improvement can stay safe.

s3ca6253f61.title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming Across a Difficulty-Graded Ladder of Two-Player Games
s3ca6253f61.description: arXiv:2611.09271v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weight-space programming sets every weight of a feed-forward network by hand, from an explicit specification of the desired computation, with no gradient descent and no training data anywhere in the construction. We ask how far a large language model can carry this practice, zero-shot, across games of deliberately increasing difficulty. We design a four-rung ladder (Nim, tic-tac-toe, two sizes of Connect Four, and a chess endgame) spanning four axes of difficulty, and build a second, independent network at each rung, using a structurally unrelated game at matched difficulty, to separate what a rung's finding says about the difficulty level from what it says about the one game used to measure it. Ten networks are built and independently ve
s3ca6253f61.summary: A study tests whether a large language model can hand-set neural network weights zero-shot to play two-player games of increasing difficulty, from Nim to a chess endgame.
s3ca6253f61.why: It probes how far LLMs can program explicit computation into networks without training, a niche capability with limited direct near-term application.

sb4db796c27.title: SLA-Aware Task Offloading in the IoT Edge-Cloud Continuum: Class-Weighted Deep Reinforcement Learning Against an Exact Optimum
sb4db796c27.description: arXiv:2611.10638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) is often used to decide where Internet of Things (IoT) tasks with different latency limits run in the edge-cloud continuum, yet some methods give every missed task the same penalty and few compare their agents with an optimal policy. This benchmark study builds four offloading systems small enough to solve exactly by dynamic programming and measures reward and learner against the optimum. A bonus for a met limit makes each miss cost its penalty plus the bonus, which shifts the class weights of published per-class rewards. A class-blind penalty stays 65% to 118% above the optimal cost even with a perfect learner, while a corrected per-class penalty comes within 0.13% of the optimum. With a per-class reward,
sb4db796c27.summary: A benchmark study compares class-weighted deep reinforcement learning for IoT task offloading in edge-cloud systems against exact optima computed by dynamic programming.
sb4db796c27.why: It shows how reward design for latency-sensitive offloading can shift learned policies away from the optimum, relevant to teams deploying RL in infrastructure.

s62f22f98d4.title: Audit Before You Merge: Provenance, Probing, and Continual LoRA Composition
s62f22f98d4.description: arXiv:2611.10684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Post-hoc merging of public LoRA adapters is an attractive gradient-free path to continual adaptation, but reliable measurement of catastrophic forgetting in this setting depends on infrastructure that prior work has not addressed. We treat each adapter merge as a sequential task in a continual-learning setting, with the instruction-tuned base model's capabilities as Task 0, and study forgetting on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Public adapter hubs contain modules that fail basic provenance checks: silent base-version mismatches and near-zero delta norms whose inclusion inflates measured interference by ~10pp. We propose a two-check audit (base-model match, non-trivial delta norm) and a leakage-free probing protocol as preconditions for any forget
s62f22f98d4.summary: A paper finds that many public LoRA adapters on hubs fail provenance checks, including base-version mismatches and near-zero deltas, and studies catastrophic forgetting when merging them.
s62f22f98d4.why: Teams merging public LoRA adapters risk silent base mismatches and forgetting, so provenance auditing before merging is advisable.

s97ab6cd013.title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning
s97ab6cd013.description: arXiv:2611.13454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce SafeRoute-MAS, a coverage-aware, risk-calibrated procedure that keeps all specialist messages or removes one using only pre-integration information. On a sealed cache of 5,328 committees, its source-compatible operating point gains +1.80 percentage points (95% CI [+1.13, +2.52]) while removing 12.76% of message tokens. We also run 4,580 controlled integrations over a stratified 458-committee sample on a public gpt-oss-120b endpoint. The sample estimate is -0.09 points; design weighting to the original workload gives +0.94 points (95% CI [-1.31, +3.50]) and 18.72% acted-input reduction. A weighted token-matched comparison likewise does not establish a selector advantage (+1.68 points, CI [-1.27, +5.10]). Only 13 of 88 cached n
s97ab6cd013.summary: SafeRoute-MAS is a risk-calibrated method for routing messages among specialist agents in multi-agent scientific reasoning, reporting mixed gains and token savings on a gpt-oss-120b endpoint.
s97ab6cd013.why: It suggests selectively dropping inter-agent messages can cut token costs with small accuracy effects, relevant to multi-agent system design.

sd9f43b94a1.title: Broad-Persistent Advising in Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Latent State Encoding
sd9f43b94a1.description: arXiv:2611.13712v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep Interactive Reinforcement Learning (Deep IntRL) accelerates reinforcement learning training by incorporating external advice. However, conventional Deep IntRL uses each piece of advice only in the current step and discards it after a single interaction. Persistent Advising and Broad-Persistent Advising (BPA) extend this process by storing advice in persistent memory and reusing it in similar states through state generalisation based on K-means clustering. This research proposes Encoder BPA, which employs a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse advice. In this framework, a trained encoder is used to map a state sequence into a latent representation at every time step. Advice can be retrieved through latent comparison, together with a t
sd9f43b94a1.summary: Researchers propose Encoder BPA, a method that uses a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse stored external advice in interactive reinforcement learning.

sc82788cf56.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
sc82788cf56.description: arXiv:2611.17621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kernel optimization is essential for efficient large language model (LLM) training and inference on Ascend NPUs. Existing Ascend kernel benchmarks primarily focus on kernel generation, with less emphasis on the ability of agents to optimize existing implementations under input configurations drawn from real workloads. To address this requirement, we introduce AscendGYM, a benchmark whose initial suite comprises 48 kernels across three difficulty levels. Each kernel is paired with test cases whose data types and tensor shapes are collected from real-world training and inference tasks. Consequently, performance improvements on AscendGYM map directly to the corresponding workloads. In terms of usability, two evaluation modes are supported in
sc82788cf56.summary: AscendGYM is a cost-aware benchmark of 48 kernels across three difficulty levels for agents optimizing Ascend NPU kernels under real-world workload input shapes.
sc82788cf56.why: Engineers working on Ascend hardware get a benchmark for evaluating agent-driven kernel optimization against realistic tensor configurations.

sc8e7bfccd8.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI
sc8e7bfccd8.description: arXiv:2611.18297v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes. When teams use judge assessments to select a prompt or train a model, the judge becomes part of the intervention. Selection can then favor errors the judge overlooks. We describe what a judge's report must contain and the independent clinical test each judge-driven change needs.
sc8e7bfccd8.summary: A paper argues that using AI judges to grade clinical AI outputs makes the judge part of the intervention, and calls for required judge report content and independent clinical testing.
sc8e7bfccd8.why: Teams using AI judges to select prompts or train clinical models may unknowingly optimize for errors the judge misses, so independent validation is needed.

s33873f048a.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
s33873f048a.description: arXiv:2611.18531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes
s33873f048a.summary: A paper models how evolutionary selection shapes an AI agent's trade-offs between task completion and rules of conduct, and whether experience can align those choices with human judgments.

s91b5a6f5cc.title: Zero-Shot Weight-Space Programming for Prediction and Classification of Target Variables in Structured Datasets
s91b5a6f5cc.description: arXiv:2611.19292v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weight-space programming fixes every parameter of a feed-forward network by hand, with no gradient descent anywhere in the construction. Every demonstration so far starts from a target function handed to the model as a rule system, making it a compilation problem. A supervised dataset withholds that specification, so the procedure must do the statistical inference itself and then express the result in the parameterisation it was given. We ask whether a large language model can do both. It is shown a small dataset in full, with the architecture of a feed-forward network, and writes out every weight and bias as a literal number, with no optimizer, no gradient, no code execution, and no chance to evaluate it first. Each construction is seale
s91b5a6f5cc.summary: A study tests whether a large language model can perform statistical inference on a small supervised dataset and then set network weights by hand, with no gradient descent.
s91b5a6f5cc.why: It explores whether LLMs can infer and encode predictive structure without training, though the approach remains experimental.

s9ae186d08b.title: Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
s9ae186d08b.description: arXiv:2611.20794v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide semantic features for uplift estimation, but treatment-revealing text can induce prediction shortcuts that do not transfer to deployment. We propose LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization (LULR) to address this risk. With the LLM encoder frozen, LULR penalizes dependence between the causal head's trainable shared representation and treatment while retaining separate outcome heads. The penalty uses a variational approximation to the contrastive log-ratio upper bound (CLUB) of mutual information, targeting treatment dependence rather than generic parameter shrinkage. Controlled proxy experiments provide exploratory evidence of improved ranking scores under injected treatment information relative to no r
s9ae186d08b.summary: Researchers propose LULR, a regularization method that penalizes dependence between a shared representation and treatment to reduce treatment-leakage shortcuts in LLM-based uplift estimation.
s9ae186d08b.why: It targets shortcut learning that can fail to transfer to deployment, relevant to teams using LLM features in causal or uplift models.

s0e9137d72d.title: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
s0e9137d72d.description: arXiv:2611.22113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Alongside memory storage and retrieval, a fundamental challenge in long-term LLM agent systems is how the agent should act when stored memories conflict with an evolving world. Facts often go stale without explicit deletion, so the conflict surfaces before the store is refreshed: delayed feedback shows that acting on one outdated record hurt, but not whether suppression should stay on that fact (a local policy) or extend to other stored facts (a global policy). Existing systems hard-code one of these scopes at design time. We formulate this online choice, under hidden validity and delayed feedback, as memory conflict governance, and propose RegimeCouncil, a lightweight router that keeps both scopes as advisors and arbitrates between them
s0e9137d72d.summary: RegimeCouncil proposes paired-evidence routing so LLM agents can decide whether to suppress stale memories locally or globally when stored facts conflict with the world.
s0e9137d72d.why: Long-running agents need principled handling of outdated memory; the abstract suggests existing systems hard-code one scope at design time.

s31262d5f30.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
s31262d5f30.description: arXiv:2611.23910v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The typical workflow for improving large-scale ranking and recommendation models is slow and tedious: an engineer forms a hypothesis, implements it as a code change, trains a model, and evaluates it both offline and online, often relying on their own intuition and experience along the way. Autonomous LLM agents promise to speed this up by running the loop on their own, but it is still unclear whether they can do this in industry-scale systems rather than on benchmarks or small proxy tasks. We build human-on-the-loop machine learning engineer (MLE) agents that propose, implement, train, and evaluate model changes on large-scale search rankers. Engineers retain control over objective design, search direction, and final-model review. We iden
s31262d5f30.summary: A paper describes MLE Agents, autonomous LLM agents that run the hypothesis-to-evaluation loop for ranking and recommendation models in an industry-scale system.
s31262d5f30.why: It tests whether autonomous ML engineering agents work beyond benchmarks in production-scale recommendation pipelines.

sf41c486401.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
sf41c486401.description: arXiv:2611.24353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scientific figures carry evidence for the claims that cite them, so reviewing a paper means checking that a figure agrees with the text, and not only describing what the figure shows. Benchmarks of figure-text verification typically hand the model the figure, the claim, or the knowledge that an inconsistency exists, which leaves untested whether a model can find the figure worth checking in a complete paper, relate a visual element to the claim it conflicts with, and recognize the conflict. We study this autonomous setting on 31 full manuscripts, each carrying a reviewer-documented figure-text inconsistency from PRISMM-Bench that is hidden from the model. Six multimodal models review each PDF under a neutral prompt, and we then add one in
sf41c486401.summary: A study introduces an evaluation of autonomous visual evidence verification, testing whether models can find and check figures against text claims across 31 full scientific manuscripts.
sf41c486401.why: It shows how well models catch figure-text inconsistencies in complete papers, a gap that matters for automated review tools.

sc9cf37a5ed.title: Can an LLM Repair a Language Model in Weight Space Without Gradient Training?
sc9cf37a5ed.description: arXiv:2611.25613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although an external language model can select and test repairs to another model's weights, behavior can also be recovered through fixed numerical edits. We assessed the value of interactive selection in a controlled study of Transformer repair. After inspecting predictions, activation summaries, and weight statistics, the editor selects projection recipes to apply to the target without gradient updates. We analyzed 20 recorded sessions involving five masked and causal language models, comparing the selected edits with fixed projections, scripted and matched-budget black-box search, and low-rank adaptation. sc9cf37a5ed.summary: A study examines whether an LLM can repair another language model by selecting fixed numerical weight edits without gradient training, across 20 sessions on five models.
sc9cf37a5ed.why: It explores gradient-free model repair, though the abstract gives limited detail on how well the approach works in practice.

s8c220fcdc7.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
s8c220fcdc7.description: arXiv:2611.26538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent attributes would predict. Without such a baseline, many existing audits flag a subgroup when it exceeds each attribute alone, a condition that attributes acting independently already satisfy. We test this standard criterion on 150 synthetic datasets built with no interaction. With the shuffle null, it flags 66.1 false subgroups per dataset on average, and at least one in every dataset. When we plant interactions of known size into
s8c220fcdc7.summary: LLM GerryMandering proposes separating interaction effects from additive effects when auditing intersectional bias, arguing a common audit criterion is already met by independent attributes.
s8c220fcdc7.why: Engineers auditing bias should note that a standard subgroup flagging rule can trigger from attributes acting independently, so baselines matter.

s84ca102539.title: OpinionGPT: Modelling Explicit Biases in Instruction-Tuned LLMs
s84ca102539.description: arXiv:2309.03876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently showcased remarkable ability to generate fitting responses to natural language instructions. However, an open research question concerns the inherent biases of trained models and their responses. For instance, if the data used to tune an LLM is dominantly written by persons with a specific political bias, we might expect generated answers to share this bias. Current research work seeks to de-bias such models, or suppress potentially biased answers. With this demonstration, we take a different view on biases in instruction-tuning: Rather than aiming to suppress them, we aim to make them explicit and transparent. To this end, we present OpinionGPT, a web demo in which users
s84ca102539.summary: OpinionGPT is a demonstration of modelling explicit biases in instruction-tuned LLMs, so that responses reflect particular viewpoints rather than being suppressed.

sc0ad3a715a.title: Automatic Detection of LLM-Generated Code: A Comparative Case Study of Contemporary Models Across Function and Class Granularities
sc0ad3a715a.description: arXiv:2409.01382v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation risks incorporating vulnerable code into software systems. Existing detectors face two critical limitations: a lack of systematic cross-model validation and opaque "black box" operation. We address this through a comparative study of code generated by four distinct LLMs: GPT-3.5, Claude 3 Haiku, Claude Haiku 4.5, and GPT-OSS. Analyzing 14,485 Python functions and 11,913 classes from the CodeSearchNet dataset, we generated corresponding code with all four LLMs. Using interpretable software metrics, we trained CatBoost classifiers for each configuration. sc0ad3a715a.summary: A comparative study analyzes code generated by four LLMs across 14,485 functions and 11,913 classes to assess automatic detection of LLM-generated code.
sc0ad3a715a.why: Detecting AI-generated code matters for security review and provenance, and the study compares detectors across several models.

s3453989ced.title: A context-adaptive policy framework for robust and reactive robotic manipulation via uncertainty-aware imitation learning
s3453989ced.description: arXiv:2410.24035v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating robust and reactive manipulation strategies that can adapt to changing context information is a challenging task in robotics. Over the years, Learning from Demonstration (LfD) has emerged as an intuitive and effective solution for generating reactive policies, particularly by following dynamical-system(DS)-based approaches. However, most state-of-the-art DS-based approaches focus on addressing the robustness limitations, overlooking the modulation of policies in response to the environment. As a result, they tend to be inflexible with respect to parameterization by task-dependent variables. In this work, we build on existing work on policy fusion and uncertainty quantification to propose a context-adaptive policy framewor
s3453989ced.summary: A paper proposes a context-adaptive, uncertainty-aware imitation learning framework for robotic manipulation that modulates dynamical-system policies in response to environment context.

s521855672a.title: Causality can systematically address the monsters under the bench(marks)
s521855672a.description: arXiv:2502.05085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Effective and reliable evaluation is essential for advancing empirical machine learning. However, the increasing accessibility of generalist models and the progress towards ever more complex, high-level tasks make systematic evaluation more challenging. Benchmarks are plagued by various biases, artifacts, or leakage, while models may behave unreliably due to poorly explored failure modes. Haphazard treatments and inconsistent formulations of such "monsters" leads to a duplication of efforts, a lack of trust in results, and unsupported inferences. In this position paper, we argue causality offers an ideal framework to systematically address these challenges. By making causal assumptions in an approach explicit, we can faithfully mode
s521855672a.summary: A position paper argues causal methods can systematically address biases, artifacts, and leakage that undermine machine learning benchmarks and evaluation.
s521855672a.why: Benchmark leakage and artifacts can produce misleading results, so causal framing may improve how teams evaluate models.

s1583de5061.title: LoopNav: Benchmarking Spatial Consistency in World Models
s1583de5061.description: arXiv:2505.22976v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ability to simulate the world in a spatially consistent manner is a crucial requirement for effective world models. Such a model enables high-quality visual generation, and also ensures the reliability of world models for downstream tasks such as simulation and planning. It must not only retain long-horizon observational information, but also enables the construction of explicit or implicit internal spatial representations. However, existing datasets do not explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints, limiting both the ability to systematically evaluate this capability and to learn it through data-driven approaches. Furthermore, most existing benchmarks primarily emphasize visual coherence or generation quality, neglectin
s1583de5061.summary: LoopNav is a benchmark that tests spatial consistency in world models, using datasets that explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints.
s1583de5061.why: Spatial consistency is a requirement for world models used in simulation and planning, and existing datasets do not enforce it explicitly.

sba09e6ff18.title: Fine-Tuning Next-Scale Visual Autoregressive Models with Group Relative Policy Optimization
sba09e6ff18.description: arXiv:2505.23331v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-tuning pre-trained generative models with Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as an effective approach for aligning outputs more closely with nuanced human preferences. In this paper, we investigate the application of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune next-scale visual autoregressive (VAR) models. Our empirical results demonstrate that this approach enables alignment to intricate reward signals derived from aesthetic predictors and CLIP embeddings, significantly enhancing image quality and enabling precise control over the generation style. Interestingly, by leveraging CLIP, our method can help VAR models generalize beyond their initial ImageNet distribution: through RL-driven exploration, these models
sba09e6ff18.summary: Researchers apply Group Relative Policy Optimization to fine-tune next-scale visual autoregressive image models using aesthetic and CLIP-based reward signals.
sba09e6ff18.why: It shows an RL fine-tuning recipe for autoregressive image generators that improves image quality under preference-based rewards.

s3d0c961a3c.title: Beyond Output Faithfulness: Diagnosing and Mitigating Pathway Rerouting in Feature Attribution
s3d0c961a3c.description: arXiv:2509.04588v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Insertion and deletion are standard metrics for evaluating feature attributions by progressively adding or removing pixels. While they test whether attributed features control a model output, they do not verify whether they do so through the computation that supports the clean prediction. We study this distinction with Ensemble Quantile Optimization (EQO), a differentiable method that directly optimizes the insertion sequence. On CNNs, Unconstrained EQO attains the highest insertion scores while departing from clean representations and retaining its insertion score after channels supporting the clean prediction are ablated. Together, these results reveal pathway rerouting that output-only metrics cannot detect. On a Vision Transform
s3d0c961a3c.summary: A paper studies pathway rerouting in feature attribution, showing that insertion and deletion metrics can be satisfied by methods that depart from the clean model computation.
s3d0c961a3c.why: Engineers relying on attribution metrics for interpretability should know that high insertion scores may not reflect the computation actually used.

s51c250ece2.title: Reconstruction Alignment Improves Unified Multimodal Models
s51c250ece2.description: arXiv:2509.07295v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discover a simple but effective way for visual understanding to help visual generation in a unified model. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) unify visual understanding and generation within a single architecture. However, conventional training relies on image-text pairs (or sequences) whose captions are typically sparse and miss fine-grained visual details, even when they use hundreds of words to describe a simple image. We introduce Reconstruction Alignment (RecA), a resource-efficient post-training method that leverages visual understanding encoder embeddings as dense "text prompts," providing rich supervision without captions. Concretely, RecA conditions a UMM on its own visual understanding embeddings and optimizes it to recon
s51c250ece2.summary: Reconstruction Alignment (RecA) is a post-training method that uses visual understanding to improve visual generation in unified multimodal models, using dense visual signals instead of sparse captions.
s51c250ece2.why: It offers a resource-efficient post-training technique to improve generation in unified multimodal models.

sedf40d2f7b.title: Rhythm-TTS: High-Fidelity Shortcut Latent Modeling and Probabilistic Rhythm Generation for Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
sedf40d2f7b.description: arXiv:2510.02848v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) systems are commonly built on either discrete codec tokens or continuous acoustic representations. Discrete-token models benefit from stable sequence modeling and explicit speech factorization, but they ultimately synthesize speech through codebook lookup and codeword composition, which can accumulate errors and impose a quality ceiling on naturalness and speaker similarity. Continuous-representation models can generate fine-grained speech latents directly, but often require heavier in-context modeling and less explicit alignment. This paper presents Rhythm-TTS, a shortcut zero-shot TTS framework that combines the factorizability of discrete codec tokens with the fidelity of continuous latent generatio
sedf40d2f7b.summary: Rhythm-TTS proposes shortcut latent modeling and probabilistic rhythm generation for zero-shot text-to-speech, combining aspects of discrete and continuous speech representations.

s4272e65904.title: Improving Consistency in Retrieval-Augmented Systems with Group Similarity Rewards
s4272e65904.description: arXiv:2510.04392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains where users expect outputs to be consistent across semantically equivalent queries. However, existing systems often exhibit significant inconsistencies due to variability in both the retriever and generator, undermining trust and reliability. In this work, we focus on information consistency, i.e., the requirement that generated outputs convey the same core content across semantically equivalent inputs. We introduce a principled evaluation framework that decomposes RAG consistency into retriever-level, generator-level, and end-to-end components, enabling systematic identification of inconsistency sources. To improve consistency, we propose
s4272e65904.summary: Researchers introduce an evaluation framework and group similarity rewards to improve output consistency across semantically equivalent queries in retrieval-augmented generation systems.
s4272e65904.why: Inconsistent answers to equivalent queries undermine trust in RAG deployments in high-stakes domains, so measurable consistency methods matter for production teams.

s661fecc82c.title: RAG Makes Guardrails Brittle? Investigating Robustness of Guardrails under RAG-style Contexts
s661fecc82c.description: arXiv:2510.05310v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the increasing adoption of large language models (LLMs), ensuring the safety of LLM systems has become a pressing concern. External LLM-based guardrail models have emerged as a popular solution to screen unsafe inputs and outputs, but they are themselves fine-tuned or prompt-engineered LLMs vulnerable to data distribution shifts. In this paper, taking Retrieval Augmentation Generation (RAG) as a case study, we investigate how robust LLM-based guardrails are against additional information embedded in the context. Through a systematic evaluation of 3 Llama Guards and 2 GPT-oss models, we find that inserting benign retrieved documents flips the judgments of input and output guardrails in around 11% and 8% of cases respectively, wi
s661fecc82c.summary: A study examines whether LLM-based safety guardrails remain robust when RAG-style retrieved context adds extra information to inputs.
s661fecc82c.why: Guardrails that fail under retrieved context could let unsafe content through in RAG pipelines, a risk for teams relying on them.

s2a1263ce92.title: Learning to Assimilate: Amortized Control for Autoregressive Diffusion
s2a1263ce92.description: arXiv:2510.06637v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autoregressive diffusion models (ARDMs) offer expressive priors for forecasting chaotic dynamics. However, maintaining consistency with sparse observations over long rollouts can require substantial test-time computation. We introduce Control-Augmented Data Assimilation (CADA), which trains a lightweight controller on top of a frozen ARDM to steer predictions toward future observations. Using a KL-regularized stochastic optimal control objective, the controller learns from short autoregressive rollouts to anticipate observations while staying close to the pretrained dynamics. s2a1263ce92.summary: Researchers propose Control-Augmented Data Assimilation, which trains a lightweight controller on a frozen autoregressive diffusion model to steer forecasts toward sparse observations.

s4ca8ac309a.title: Provable Selective Auto-labeling with Reliability Guarantees
s4ca8ac309a.description: arXiv:2510.14581v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Auto-labeling has emerged as a popular, cost-effective alternative to manual annotation. However, its performance is often highly inconsistent across different tasks, underscoring the importance of selective strategies. Despite this, existing heuristic methods for selective auto-labeling still rely heavily on model confidence scores and offer no reliable guarantee on the trustworthiness of the selected examples. To address this, we propose \textbf{Conformal Labeling}, a novel method that selects a subset of auto-generated labels with a provably controlled false labeling rate (FLR). Our key idea is to formulate selective auto-labeling as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem, where each hypothesis indicates whether to accept the auto
s4ca8ac309a.summary: Researchers propose Conformal Labeling, a method that selects auto-generated labels with reliability guarantees rather than relying on heuristic model confidence scores.
s4ca8ac309a.why: Offers statistically grounded guarantees on auto-labeled data quality, which could help teams cut annotation costs without sacrificing trustworthiness.

se90d693a63.title: Generalizing Test-time Compute-optimal Scaling as an Optimizable Graph
se90d693a63.description: arXiv:2511.00086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Test-Time Scaling (TTS) improves large language models (LLMs) by allocating additional computation during inference, typically through parallel, sequential, or hybrid scaling. However, prior studies often assume fixed collaboration architectures (e.g., topologies) and single-model usage, overlooking that optimal architectures and model combinations can vary across tasks. Therefore, we study the novel problem of searching for compute-optimal model combinations and architectures in TTS under a fixed budget. We formalize it as a multi-LLM collaboration graph, where nodes encode roles and LLM model assignments, and edges capture information flow. This problem is challenging because (i) the combinatorial search space is prohibitively lar
se90d693a63.summary: Researchers formulate a search for compute-optimal model combinations and architectures for test-time scaling of LLMs under a fixed budget, rather than assuming fixed topologies.
se90d693a63.why: Suggests that choosing model mixes and collaboration structures per task, not a fixed setup, may improve inference efficiency.

s8f87b1ab62.title: Object-Centric World Models for Causality-Aware Reinforcement Learning
s8f87b1ab62.description: arXiv:2511.14262v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: World models have been developed to support sample-efficient deep reinforcement learning agents. However, it remains challenging for world models to accurately replicate environments that are high-dimensional, non-stationary, and composed of multiple objects with rich interactions since most world models learn holistic representations of all environmental components. By contrast, humans perceive the environment by decomposing it into discrete objects, facilitating efficient decision-making. Motivated by this insight, we propose \emph{Slot Transformer Imagination with CAusality-aware reinforcement learning} (STICA), a unified framework in which object-centric Transformers serve as the world model and causality-aware policy and value
s8f87b1ab62.summary: Researchers propose Slot-based object-centric world models to help reinforcement learning agents handle multi-object, high-dimensional, non-stationary environments.

s0bc761fe9c.title: Verify Before You Generate: Sketch-Guided Efficient Motion-Planning for Video Generation
s0bc761fe9c.description: arXiv:2511.17450v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent video generation approaches increasingly rely on planning intermediate control signals like object trajectories to improve temporal coherence and motion fidelity. However, these methods mostly employ single-shot plans that are typically limited to simple motion instructions, leading to suboptimal motion quality, or iterative refinement which requires multiple calls to the video generator and incurs high computational cost. To address this trade-off, we propose SketchVerify, a training-free framework whose key insight is to verify motion plans using lightweight video sketches before invoking the expensive video generator. This lightweight planning space enables efficient comparison of multiple candidate trajectories and bounde
s0bc761fe9c.summary: SketchVerify is a training-free framework that verifies object-trajectory plans before generating video, aiming to improve motion quality with less computation.
s0bc761fe9c.why: Verifying motion plans before calling the video generator could reduce costly iterative refinement passes for video generation pipelines.

s5276137fbf.title: Learning and Comparing Local Traces for Weakly Supervised Image Manipulation Localization
s5276137fbf.description: arXiv:2601.06222v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Image manipulation localization identifies edited regions and provides spatial evidence for assessing image reliability, but fully supervised methods require costly pixel-level annotations. Weakly supervised methods reduce this cost using image-level labels, but classification can rely on a few salient cues without ensuring accurate or complete localization. This difficulty is pronounced when manipulation traces are weak and unevenly distributed and authentic and manipulated regions share similar appearance. We propose a CLIP-based framework that integrates Trace-Oriented Vision--Language Adaptation (TOVA) and Relation-Aware Trace Discrimination (RATD). TOVA adapts the visual encoder and uses global visual context to aggregate edge-
s5276137fbf.summary: Researchers propose a CLIP-based framework for weakly supervised image manipulation localization that learns from image-level labels instead of pixel-level annotations.
s5276137fbf.why: Reducing reliance on costly pixel-level annotations could make image forgery localization cheaper to build and deploy.

s5482d41bc2.title: SAME: Stabilized Mixture-of-Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
s5482d41bc2.description: arXiv:2602.01990v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, but real-world deployment requires them to continually expand their capabilities, making Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) essential. Recent methods leverage sparse expert routing to promote task specialization, but we find that the expert routing process suffers from drift as the data distribution evolves. For example, a grounding query that previously activated localization experts may instead be routed to irrelevant experts after learning OCR tasks. s5482d41bc2.summary: Researchers present SAME, a stabilized mixture-of-experts method that addresses expert routing drift in multimodal continual instruction tuning of MLLMs.
s5482d41bc2.why: Routing drift during continual tuning can erode earlier capabilities, a practical concern for teams updating multimodal models over time.

sfc4ae9976e.title: TabularMath: Evaluating Computational Extrapolation in Tabular Learning via Program-Verified Synthesis
sfc4ae9976e.description: arXiv:2602.02523v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Standard tabular benchmarks reward interpolation: predicting values inside the data manifold, where local statistical smoothing works. However, much high-value tabular data, from pricing and financial rules to physical simulation, is produced by deterministic computations rather than noisy relationships. Can tabular models move from statistical interpolation to computational extrapolation, returning exact answers even beyond the range seen in training? We introduce TabularMath, a benchmark of 114 deterministic computations (233,472 rows) compiled from GSM8K and AIME problems into verified programs. We evaluate nine tabular methods, closed-form and symbolic regression baselines, and in-context learning with GPT-OSS-120B. On regressio
sfc4ae9976e.summary: TabularMath is a benchmark of 114 deterministic computations testing whether tabular models can extrapolate exact answers beyond their training range.
sfc4ae9976e.why: Shows that standard tabular models interpolate rather than compute, a caveat for using them on rule-based pricing or simulation data.

s5d6f02ab80.title: EMA Policy Gradient: Taming Reinforcement Learning for LLMs with EMA Anchor and Top-k KL
s5d6f02ab80.description: arXiv:2602.04417v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has enabled Large Language Models (LLMs) to acquire increasingly complex reasoning and agentic behaviors. In this work, we propose two simple techniques to improve policy gradient algorithms for LLMs. First, we replace the fixed anchor policy during RL with an Exponential Moving Average (EMA), similar to a target network in deep Q-learning. Second, we introduce Top-$k$ KL estimator, which allows for flexible interpolation between exact KL and sampled KL. We derive the stability conditions for using EMA anchor; moreover, we show that our Top-$k$ KL estimator yields both unbiased KL values and unbiased gradients at any $k$, while bringing the benefits of exact KL.
