s5d6f02ab80.summary: Researchers propose replacing the fixed anchor policy in LLM reinforcement learning with an exponential moving average and introduce a Top-k KL estimator to improve stability.
s5d6f02ab80.why: Offers practical stabilization tweaks for policy gradient training of LLMs on reasoning and agentic tasks.

s8de9bec328.title: The Landscape of Generative AI in Information Systems: A Synthesis of Secondary Reviews and Research Agendas
s8de9bec328.description: arXiv:2603.11842v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The post-ChatGPT surge has rapidly reframed IS research and practice. As organizations and society grapple with GenAI adoption, a body of secondary studies and research agendas has emerged to synthesize early evidence and chart directions for future inquiry. This study reviews secondary and roadmap papers to synthesize the state of knowledge on GenAI's benefits and challenges in IS, and to identify future research directions. We performed a systematic search across Scopus, WoS, and eAIS for publications from 2023 onwards. Following a rigorous, multi-stage screening process, we selected a final set of 28 papers for analysis using bibliometric mapping and thematic analysis. We also conducted a quality assessment of all sources to gaug
s8de9bec328.summary: A review synthesizes secondary studies and research agendas on generative AI in information systems, covering benefits, challenges and future research directions from 2023 onward.

s7b1b2c4a0a.title: Delightful Policy Gradient under Distributed Friction
s7b1b2c4a0a.description: arXiv:2603.20521v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Distributed reinforcement learning trains on data from stale, buggy, or mismatched actors, whose actions often have high surprisal (negative log-probability) under the learner's policy. Supervised fine-tuning learns stably from such logged data, while policy gradient often does not. We trace the difference to negative learning from surprising data: rare failures can dominate finite-batch updates, while rare successes carry information the current policy would otherwise miss. s7b1b2c4a0a.summary: Researchers propose the Delightful Policy Gradient to handle learning from stale or mismatched distributed actors by gating surprising samples.
s7b1b2c4a0a.why: Addresses instability in distributed RL training on logged or off-policy data, relevant to teams running large-scale RL pipelines.

s14769caf59.title: Does This Gradient Spark Joy?
s14769caf59.description: arXiv:2603.20526v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Policy gradient computes a backward pass for every sample, although the backward pass is expensive and most samples carry little learning value. The Delightful Policy Gradient (DG) scores learning value in the forward pass with \emph{delight}, the product of advantage and surprisal (negative log-probability). We introduce the \emph{Kondo gate}, which compares delight against a compute price and pays for a backward pass only when the sample is worth it; sweeping the price traces a quality--cost trade-off. s14769caf59.summary: Researchers introduce the Kondo gate, which decides per sample whether a costly backward pass is worth computing in policy gradient training, trading quality against cost.
s14769caf59.why: Could cut backward-pass compute in RL training by skipping low-value samples, with a tunable quality-cost tradeoff.

s0423bb48f3.title: TopoPilot: Reliable Conversational Workflow Automation for Topological Data Analysis and Visualization
s0423bb48f3.description: arXiv:2603.25063v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent agentic systems demonstrate that large language models can generate complex codebases from natural language prompts. Despite this progress, they present reliability concerns for scientific visualization due to invalid operations, subtle errors, and failure to resolve underspecified inputs. In this work, we introduce TopoPilot, a reliable and extensible agentic framework for automating complex scientific visualization workflows. We focus on topological data analysis and visualization as a primary use case, while designing the framework to generalize to broader visualization domains. s0423bb48f3.summary: TopoPilot is an agentic framework that automates topological data analysis and scientific visualization workflows from conversational prompts, aiming for reliable operations.
s0423bb48f3.why: Shows agentic LLM tooling being designed with guardrails for scientific workflows where invalid operations and subtle errors are costly.

s29700aa9c3.title: The Projector Forgets Too: Joint Merging for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
s29700aa9c3.description: arXiv:2604.14016v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) is essential for sequential task adaptation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) but is severely restricted by catastrophic forgetting. While existing literature focuses on the reasoning language backbone, in this work, we find that forgetting can arise from changes in both the cross-modal projector and the language model's LoRA adapters. s29700aa9c3.summary: Researchers find catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning stems from both the cross-modal projector and LoRA adapters, not only the language backbone.
s29700aa9c3.why: It suggests merging or restoring only language adapters is insufficient when adapting multimodal models sequentially, so teams need to track projector changes too.

s725da7b3f3.title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
s725da7b3f3.description: arXiv:2604.21903v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep-learning video super-resolution has progressed rapidly, but climate applications typically super-resolve (increase resolution) either space or time, and joint spatiotemporal models are often designed for a single pair of super-resolution (SR) factors (upscaling spatial and temporal ratio between the low-resolution sequence and the high-resolution sequence), limiting transfer across spatial resolutions and temporal cadences (frame rates). s725da7b3f3.summary: Researchers propose a diffusion-based joint spatiotemporal super-resolution framework for climate data that reuses one architecture across different spatial and temporal upscaling factors.

s875390a671.title: When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on $\ell_1$-norm Lower Bounds
s875390a671.description: arXiv:2605.06615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sign-based optimization algorithms, such as SignSGD and Muon, have garnered significant attention for their remarkable performance in training large foundation models. Despite this empirical success, we still lack a theoretical understanding of when and why these sign-based methods outperform vanilla SGD. s875390a671.summary: A theoretical study examines when SignSGD and related sign-based optimizers outperform SGD, using l1-norm lower bounds to explain their advantage.
s875390a671.why: It gives engineers a theoretical basis for choosing sign-based optimizers like Muon over SGD when training large models.

s71588ff850.title: Mosaic: Efficient CPU-GPU Coordinated Block-Sparse Attention
s71588ff850.description: arXiv:2605.07719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-context LLM serving increasingly relies on CPU-resident context KV cache, driven by KV offloading and disaggregated prefill--decode execution. Although block-sparse attention reduces KV access, existing designs remain inefficient: GPU-centralized execution fetches selected KV blocks from CPU memory at each decoding step, making it PCIe-bound, while CPU--GPU partitioned execution places CPU-side sparse attention on the critical path, leaving substantial GPU time idle. s71588ff850.summary: Mosaic proposes a CPU-GPU coordinated block-sparse attention design to speed up long-context LLM serving that uses CPU-resident KV cache.
s71588ff850.why: It targets PCIe bottlenecks and idle GPU time in KV offloading, which affects the cost and latency of long-context inference serving.

s4630be0ac2.title: NoiseRater: Meta-Learned Noise Valuation for Diffusion Model Training
s4630be0ac2.description: arXiv:2605.08144v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Training a diffusion model involves two sources of randomness for each data sample: the timestep and the Gaussian noise realization. The timestep has been studied extensively through scheduling and weighting, whereas the impact of the noise realization at a given timestep is still underexplored. In this work, we examine whether different noise instances are equally informative. s4630be0ac2.summary: NoiseRater is a meta-learned network that scores individual noise realizations for diffusion model training, learned via bilevel optimization.
s4630be0ac2.why: It challenges the assumption that all Gaussian noise samples are equally informative, which could affect diffusion training efficiency.

sc845e47ad3.title: Comment and Control: Hijacking Agentic Workflows via Context-Grounded Evolution
sc845e47ad3.description: arXiv:2605.11229v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. While bringing convenience for developers, this integration exposes a new risk: An adversary may control and craft certain inputs, such as GitHub issue comments, to manipulate the LLM agent for unwanted actions, such as credential exfiltration and arbitrary command execution. To our knowledge, no prior academic work has studied such a risk in agentic workflows. sc845e47ad3.summary: Researchers study how adversarial GitHub issue comments can hijack LLM agents in agentic workflows on platforms like GitHub Actions and n8n, enabling credential exfiltration.
sc845e47ad3.why: Teams running LLM agents in CI or automation pipelines face prompt-injection risks that can lead to credential theft and arbitrary command execution.

s7d89ac99d2.title: PhyMotion: Structured 3D Motion Reward for Physics-Grounded Human Video Generation
s7d89ac99d2.description: arXiv:2605.14269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating realistic human motion is a central yet unsolved challenge in video generation. While reinforcement learning (RL)-based post-training has driven recent gains in general video quality, extending it to human motion remains bottlenecked by a reward signal that cannot reliably score motion realism. Existing video rewards primarily rely on 2D perceptual signals, without explicitly modeling the 3D body state, contact, and dynamics underlying articulated human motion, and often assign high scores to videos with floating bodies or physically implausible movements. s7d89ac99d2.summary: PhyMotion proposes a structured 3D motion reward for reinforcement learning post-training to produce physically plausible human videos, addressing floating bodies and physics violations.

s322840ddec.title: StreamPro: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Grained Rewards for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
s322840ddec.description: arXiv:2605.16381v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to continuously monitor evolving video streams and decide whether, when, and what to respond. However, training models with such proactive capabilities remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) suffers from severe imbalance between silence and response signals, while reinforcement learning (RL) faces sparse response-level rewards and difficulties in optimizing interdependent response sequences. s322840ddec.summary: StreamPro is a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with multi-grained rewards for models that proactively decide when and what to respond to streaming video.

s32a789c9a7.title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Ophthalmic VQA via Spatially-Grounded Lesion Evidence
s32a789c9a7.description: arXiv:2605.22414v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) holds great promise for clinical support, particularly in ophthalmology, where retinal fundus photography is essential for diagnosis.
